Policy: Order No. 8 of the Ministry of Health validating the Procedure for assessing risks associated with exposure to hazardous chemicals and validating Maximum biological values of chemicals.
Policy_Content: This Order establishes minimum requirements for conducting an assessment of risks associated with exposure to hazardous chemical substances present at the workplace or arising in the process of handling chemicals. This Procedure applies to economic entities, regardless of their form of ownership, that carry out activities related to work with dangerous chemical substances. Maximum biological values of chemicals shall be intended the limit value of the concentration in the relevant biological environment of the relevant substance, the products of its metabolism, or the indicator of its action. Chemical substances that are used or formed at the workplace in the course of work and negatively affect the health of employees are subject to hygienic regulation, which is carried out in order to limit the intensity or duration of the action of such factors by establishing their permissible impact on human health. Risk assessment consists in systematically identifying hazards, determining the magnitude of risks, and taking measures necessary for the safety and health protection of employees. Risk assessment is carried out in stages, taking into account the previously identified hazards that arose during work. If these hazards cannot be completely eliminated, their risk to the health and safety of workers is assessed. Based on the risk assessment, the employer makes a decision to increase the level of safety.

Policy: Regulation on agricultural land use records.
Policy_Content: This Regulation, based on the provisions of the Croatian Law on agriculture, prescribes the conditions, content and method of keeping records of the use of agricultural land. ARKOD is a record of the use of agricultural land in the territory of the Republic of Croatia, which is maintained in digital graphic form by the Agency for Payments in Agriculture, Fisheries and Rural Development. Digital orthophoto map (or DOF) is a map sheet in electronic form composed of one or more orthophotos (aerial photographs) of a unique scale, with a rectangular coordinate grid applied and cartographic signs for some objects, isohypses, equipped with names, elevations and out-of-frame data, which represents the basis according to which data on the use of agricultural land are produced and updated. Digital cadastral plan is a cadastral plan translated or created in electronic form. Register of spatial units contains data on the type and name, identifier, display of boundaries and source of data on the boundaries of spatial units, data on spatial units with which they are connected, special data (status, headquarters, etc.) and type, source and date of application. The Annex (I, II, III, IV and V) is also an integrated part of this publication (technical data and related sheets and lists).

It outlines voting allocation based on membership size and provides mechanisms for dispute resolution and the inclusion of observer status for certain organizations; (viii) replacement of Article 93 with a new article outlining the powers and responsibilities of labor officers in handling labor disputes and unfair labor practices, emphasizing conciliation and arbitration processes.

Policy: Directive to Provide for the Application of Tax Incentives for Expansion/Upgrading of Investment No. 941/2023.
Policy_Content: The Directive provides for the application of tax incentives for expansion/upgrading of investment. An investor engaged in expanding the production and service rendering capacity of the existing enterprise and an investor who increases in variety or volume by at least 100% by introducing new production or service rendering line of an existing enterprise shall be beneficiary of an income tax exemption. The Directive also establishes conditions for being beneficiary: a) submit evidence showing that the enterprise has been engaged in production or service rendering activities for a certain period of time; b) submit financial statement certified by an external auditor showing the capital invested to modernize the production process, to introduce new technology or to increase the production or service type; c) submit financial statement certified by an external auditor showing the volume of production or service rendered within a year after the completion of the upgrading; d) if it has been granted tax exemption that it has fulfilled privilege; submit evidence showing its obligations exemption period in accordance to tax laws.  Section 3 contains criteria for exemption from customs duties. Also liability is disciplined.

Policy: Electricity Consumption Reduction Act (SVRG).
Policy_Content: This Law aims for reducing peak-time electricity consumption in order to reduce electricity prices and minimize the use of fossil fuels. This Federal Law regulates the implementation of Articles 4 and 5 of Council Regulation (EU) 2022/1854 of October 6, 2022 on emergency measures. The Law defines the methods for nomination of the peak times while requires for reduction of electricity use in peak times by an average of at least 5%. The Law specifies the measures to be taken for reduction of electricity use including increasing public awareness, optimization of user behaviours such as increasing use of more efficient devices and early replacement of old devices, and having energy saving contracts. The Law further lays out provisions for holding tenders for electricity consumption reductions and provides regulations for its participation, procedures and award contracts. The Law further elaborates on allocation of fund for coverage of costs, monitoring and implementation.     The Law consists of 23 Articles divided into 6 Parts.

Policy: Regional Law No. 100-OZ “On responsible subsoil management on the regional territory.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law, in order to protect environmental rights and legal interests of natural persons and legal entities, preservation of the environment, preservation of the traditional way of life of indigenous peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East of the Russian Federation, living in the territory of the Chukotka Autonomous Area, prevention of environmental harm, ensuring environmental safety on the territory of the Chukotka Autonomous Area,  establishes the grounds for legal regulation of interaction of subsoil users operating on the territory of the Chukotka Autonomous Area, state authorities of the Chukotka Autonomous Area, bodies of local self-government, organizations of indigenous peoples Chukotka Autonomous Area and citizens. Policy: Decree-Law No. 95/2022 on the General regime regulating norms of origin.
Policy_Content: This Decree-Law establishes the legal framework for the rules of origin and the issuance of certificates of origin. It applies to the national territory of Timor-Leste and to trade agreements to which Timor-Leste is a party. The rules of origin are the set of norms and procedures used by States in specifying the criteria to qualify goods as originating in a given country. Goods wholly obtained in a country are considered to be: a) Mineral products extracted in that country; b) The products of the plant kingdom harvested therein; c) Live animals born and bred therein; d) Products obtained from live animals reared therein; e) Hunting and fishing products carried out therein; f) Sea fishing products and other products extracted from the sea, outside the territorial sea of any country, by ships registered or registered in that country and flying its flag; g) Goods obtained on board factory ships from products referred to in paragraph f) originating in that country, provided that these factory ships are registered or registered in that country and fly its flag; h) Products extracted from marine soil or subsoil located outside the territorial sea, provided that that country exercises, for the purposes of exploitation, exclusive rights over that soil or subsoil; i) Waste resulting from manufacturing operations and out-of-use items, subject to having been collected there and used only for the recovery of raw materials; j) Those that are obtained exclusively from the goods referred to in subparagraphs a) to i) or their derivatives, whatever their stage of manufacture.

Eco-tourism included organization of eco-tours. The main activities in the field of agricultural and educational tourism include: (a) activities for the production and processing of agricultural commodities, providing nutrition using agricultural commodities produced and (or) processed on land plots owned by the subject of agrarian and educational tourism; and (b) activities for organizing animal rides, with the exception of wild fauna species, and horse-drawn transport.

Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates relations in the field of protection of the atmospheric air within the limits of competence of the regional public authorities and is aimed at ensuring the constitutional rights of citizens to a favorable environment and reliable information about its condition. In order to monitor air pollution, comprehensive assessment and prognosis of its condition, as well as provision of the bodies of state authorities, local self-government bodies, municipalities, organizations and the population of the current and emergency information about air pollution, authorized regional executive body in in the field of atmospheric air protection takes part in the organization and conducting state monitoring of the atmospheric air and within its competence ensures its implementation on the regional territory. In accordance with the legislation of the Russian Federation in the field of environmental protection, state monitoring of the atmospheric air is carried out within the framework of the state environmental monitoring according to the procedure established by the Government of the Russian Federation. Policy: Law No. 166-VII ZRK of the Republic of Kazakhstan “On geodesy, cartography and spatial data”.
Policy_Content: This Law regulates social relations arising in the process of the performance of geodetic and cartographic activities, including search, collection, storage, processing, provision and distribution of spatial data. Geographic information system shall be intended information system, providing collection, processing, analysis, modeling, storage, distribution and other use of spatial information about the Earth, about earthly surface, natural, man-made and social processes. Distant zoning of the Earth is the process of obtaining information about surface of the Earth by observing and measuring from space and air of the space of own and reflected radiation of elements of land, ocean and atmosphere. This Law contains 5 Chapters divided into 32 Articles. Chapter 1 lays down general provisions. Chapter 2 regards state management in the field of geodesy, cartography and spatial data. Chapter 3 regards ensuring the performance of geodetic and cartographic activities. Chapter 4 regards geodetic and cartographic supervision. Chapter 5 lays down final provisions. The objects of geodetic and cartographic activities are the territory of the Republic of Kazakhstan, territory of the globe, air and space, including natural celestial bodies and artificial satellites of the Earth. State regulation of public relations in the field of geodesy, cartography and spatial data is based on the following principles: (a) consistency and continuity in the implementation of geodetic and cartographic activities; (b) the completeness, reliability and relevance of spatial data sets; (c) uniformity of measurements when performing geodetic, cartographic, topographical and gravimetric work; (d) use of uniform standards; (e) accessibility and openness of spatial data, with the exception of information constituting state secrets, proprietary information of limited distribution and other information protected by law; (f) use of approved reference systems; (g) interoperability; and (h) stimulating the development of the field of geodesy, cartography and spatial data.

Todas las actividades, obras o proyectos nuevos, requieren una Viabilidad (Licencia) Ambiental (VLA), dicho otorgamiento estará sujeto al cumplimiento de la aprobación del proceso de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental. La Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental (EIA) se deberá completar con la Matriz de Significancia de Impactos Ambientales (SIA). El resultado de este análisis por parte del consultor ambiental, deberá permitir determinar el trámite a seguir para la obtención de la viabilidad ambiental, salvo para aquellos casos que por ley especial exijan realizar un Estudio de Impacto Ambiental. Este reglamento contempla la Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental para actividades, obras y proyectos, a través de distintos formularios, según la especificación de cada AOP, así como el seguimiento y control ambiental de los proyectos

Policy: Ley 28/2022 -  De fomento del ecosistema de las empresas emergentes.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley tiene por objeto establecer un marco normativo específico para apoyar la creación y el crecimiento de empresas emergentes en España. Igualmente, establece un sistema de seguimiento y evaluación de sus resultados sobre el ecosistema español de empresas emergentes. Los objetivos de la Ley son: a) Fomentar la creación, el crecimiento y la relocalización de empresas emergentes en España; b) Atraer talento y capital internacional para el desarrollo del ecosistema español de empresas emergentes; c) Estimular la inversión pública y privada en empresas emergentes; d) Favorecer la interrelación entre empresas, agentes financiadores y territorios, con especial atención al fomento de polos de atracción de empresas emergentes en entornos rurales; e) Impulsar el acercamiento entre la formación profesional y la universidad y las empresas emergentes; f) Contribuir a incrementar la transferencia de conocimientos de la Universidad y de los organismos públicos de investigación; g) Eliminar las brechas de género existentes en el ecosistema español de empresas emergentes; h) Apoyar el desarrollo de polos de atracción de empresas e inversores; i) Impulsar la compra pública innovadora con empresas emergentes; j) Garantizar la eficacia y coherencia del sistema estatal de ayudas al emprendimiento basado en innovación; k) Promover el seguimiento participativo de la evolución del ecosistema español de empresas emergentes y de los resultados de esta ley. La Ley será de aplicación a las empresas emergentes señaladas en el artículo 3º. Policy: Regulation No. 1171 on organic production and labelling of organic agricultural products, aquaculture products, food and feed (Ecology Regulation).
Policy_Content: The present Regulation contains 29 Articles and applies to agricultural and aquaculture products which mention organic production in their labeling and/or advertising. It applies to every phase of production, processing, distribution, sales and import from countries outside the EEA area of such products. It applies to: a) live and unprocessed agricultural and aquaculture products; b) processed products for food or feed; c) vegetative propagation material; d) seeds for cultivation; e) yeast for foodstuffs or feed; f) salt for foodstuffs or feed; g) certain products closely related to agricultural products, including untreated cotton and wool, raw hide, untreated leather and beeswax. Article 2 makes Regulation (EU) 2018/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council on organic production and labelling of organic products applicable in Norway, and articles 3 and 4 makes other relevant EU legislation applicable. Businesses that intend to carry out activities covered by these regulations must apply to the Norwegian Food Safety Authority for approval. Further rules are laid down concerning registration, greenhouse farming, maximum number of livestock in farms, feed additivies, fees, etc.

Policy: Law No. 4.046 on the concept and application of traceability of primary products originating from mineral extraction.
Policy_Content: This Law establishes the concept and application of traceability of primary products originating from mineral extraction. The traceability aims to guarantee the monitoring of information regarding the phases that make up the mineral extraction chain, allowing the products originating from the mineral extraction, carried out by mining companies duly registered with the competent bodies. The primary objective of traceability is to ensure and control mining activities in the State and guarantee the regular exploitation of mineral resources. Economic agents in the mineral extraction chain are responsible for the maintenance, for five years, of the tax documents for the extraction, movement and commercialization of the products originating from the exploration of the ores which have authorization for economic exploitation. The controls must be implemented within a period of up to one year from the date of regulation of this Law, and the regulatory norm must, whenever possible, establish procedures that do not burden the extractor in terms of administrative formalities.

El sistema público de evaluación de políticas públicas estará integrado por la organización institucional de la evaluación en la Administración General del Estado y por las medidas destinadas a la formalización y sistematización de las prácticas de evaluación. El ámbito de aplicación de la Ley será la evaluación de las políticas públicas desarrolladas por la Administración General del Estado y sus organismos públicos vinculados o dependientes. Policy: Regional Law No. 168 “On state support in the field of agriculture.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates the issues related to state support of agricultural development. It shall be applicable to citizens, associations thereof, entrepreneurs and organizations acknowledged as producers of agricultural commodities and performing primary and subsequent processing of agricultural commodities. State support in the field of agricultural development is carried out in the following areas: (a) the development of crop production, ensuring the conservation and increase of fertility of agricultural land, including through land reclamation; (b) development of animal husbandry, including livestock breeding and reindeer herding; (c) technical re-equipment of agricultural production, technological modernization and innovative development of agro-industrial complex; (d) development of the food and processing industry; (e) development of agricultural cooperation and small forms of management; (f) staffing of the agro-industrial complex; (g) prevention and elimination of diseases of farm animals and ensuring veterinary safety of products of animal husbandry; (h) development of a risk insurance system in agriculture; and (i) ensuring the integrated development of rural areas.

Policy_Content: This Act, divided into thirteen chapters and consisting of seventy-six paragraphs, provides for defining a sustainable planning and standards for implementing waste management, in order to eliminate or reduce the adverse impacts of waste, protect the environment and public health, thus the Act applies to the generation and management of all types of waste; to the storage for recovery, recycling and disposal of waste and of useful substances from waste; to import, export and transboundary movement of waste. Policy: Building a Green Prairie Economy Act (S.C. 2022, c. 21).
Policy_Content: The Act requires the Minister responsible for economic development in the Prairie provinces to develop a framework to coordinate local cooperation and engagement in the implementation of federal programs across various sectors, with the objective of building a green economy in the Prairie provinces. In developing the Framework, the Minister must consult with provincial government representatives responsible for transportation, environment and employment, and with municipalities, Indigenous governing bodies, the private sector and representatives of employers and employees in that sector; exceptions are also considered. Under point 3 the Act clarifies the content of the Framework. The Framework must include measures that promote economic sustainability and growth and employment in the Prairie provinces by addressing the transportation issue; must foster job creation and skills transfer from traditional energy industries to enable them to build a net-zero emissions green economy and mitigate their impact on climate change; prioritize projects that generate natural infrastructure and a clean environment, such as tree-planting initiatives, solar energy projects and environmental management of the boreal forest, and that make use of all sources of energy, including nuclear energy; support the continued development of clean energy in fields such as agriculture, forestry, transportation, manufacturing and tourism; establish programs and projects that stimulate a green economy; prepare infrastructure projects that facilitate adaptation to climate change and mitigation of its adverse effects. The Act also fixes the timing for tabling of framework, publication and reporting.

Policy: Government Decree No. HG885/2022 establishing Information System for Supervision of vector-borne diseases and events in public health.
Policy_Content: Information System for Supervision of vector-borne diseases and events in public health is an information system consisting of a set of interconnected information resources and technologies, technical software and methodologies designed to ensure registration, storage, processing and use of information on cases of infectious diseases and events in the field of public health, including poisoning, foodborne illnesses and acute occupational diseases. Information System ensures digitalization of systematic and continuous collection, analysis, interpretation and dissemination of health data in regard of vector-borne diseases and public health events in context of their distribution in time, space, population group and analysis of risk factors for contracting these diseases, including also within epidemiological studies. The overall goal of the Information System is to improve process for recording, managing and reporting cases of vector-borne diseases and events in the field of public health. The main functions of the Information System are: (1) the formation of an Information System database reflecting registered notifications of cases of vector-borne diseases and public health events, which are assigned an identification number, and information about their management throughout the entire life cycle; the main functions in the formation of the database are registration and updating of data, as well as exclusion of information objects: (a) registration, notification and registration on the basis of forms approved by the Ministry of Health; consists of assigning a unique identification number to an accounting object and entering a specified amount of data into the Information System database; (b) data update; consists of systematically updating the database when data on information objects is changed or supplemented; (c) deregistration/archiving; represents a change in the status of an information object, rather than a physical exclusion of data about the object; (2) the formation of a database that reflects records of requests for laboratory tests/analysis, consists of entering and updating data and information as a result of laboratory processes: (a) registration and recording of calls for laboratory tests/analysis; (b) management of analyzes and their results; (c) creation and management of a centralized catalog of laboratory tests; (d) ensuring traceability, history and correlation of laboratory tests; (e) reporting and interpretation of laboratory results; (f) control and management of processes; (3) formation of a database that reflects records of the vaccination process: (a) recording and management of information about the vaccine; (b) accounting and management of the vaccination process; (c) creating, downloading and printing a vaccination certificate; (d) pre-registration for vaccination; (e) taking into account side effects when administering immunobiological drugs; (4) development of a database that allows contact tracing to interrupt chains of transmission and prevent further transmission of the disease: (a) investigation of outbreaks and public health events generated by the Information System; (b) smart contact tracing; (c) identifying links between individual records and existing outbreaks/events; (d) view cases and contacts in on-board mode; (e) viewing transmission chains; (f) reporting; and (5) information support.

Policy: Loi visant la protection du milieu marin et l'organisation de l'aménagement des espaces marins belges.
Policy_Content: La présente loi a pour objet de protéger le milieu marin par sa préservation, sa restauration ou sa création, sur la base de mesures de gestion durable, y compris des mesures de prévention, de confinement, de restauration et de compensation des dommages. La présente loi a pour objet d'organiser la planification spatiale des espaces marins. La présente loi s'applique à quiconque exerce des activités ayant un impact potentiel sur les espaces marins belges. Le champ d'application territorial est limité aux activités exercées dans les espaces marins belges, sauf disposition contraire. La présente loi s'applique aux activités militaires, à l'exception des activités des Forces armées belges et des Forces alliées, qui sont urgentes ou indispensables à la protection de l'ordre public et de la sécurité publique, en ce compris la défense du territoire. Le Roi détermine les modalités et conditions d'application de l'alinéa précédent. Le Roi désigne également les autorités militaires compétentes pour décider de l'urgence ou du caractère indispensable d'un acte pour la protection de l'ordre public et de la sécurité publique. Pour toute activité dans les espaces marins, les services publics et les personnes morales et physiques, publiques et privées, prennent les précautions nécessaires pour prévenir les pollutions ou les dommages. Sans préjudice des dispositions du chapitre 3 du titre 5 du livre 2 du Code belge de la navigation, l'armateur et l'usager de navires doivent prendre toutes les précautions nécessaires pour prévenir et limiter la pollution.

Policy_Content: This Act lays down provisions to: (I) develop, promote and implement a holistic, comprehensive, integrated, and proactive approach to disaster risk management that (a) lessens the socio-economic and environmental impacts of disasters including climate change and (b) focuses on reducing risk, including the risk of loss of life, health, physical integrity, economic disruption and damage to the environment and property, especially to those members of population who are most vulnerable by reason of age, disability, poverty, lack of resources, physical displacement or gender; and (II) promote the involvement and participation of all relevant sectors and stakeholders, at all levels of the society. Parts II and III of this Act provides for the principles, planning, financing, and administration of the National Disaster Risk Management Policy and the establishment of a National Disaster Emergency Operations Centre, National Disaster Risk Information System, National Network of Hazard Monitoring Forecasting Systems, National Early Warning System, Disaster Emergency Fund, Disaster Prevention Fund, and the National Humanitarian Assistance Standards. The National Humanitarian Assistance Standards shall provide the minimum standard in relation to the supply of water supply; the promotion of sanitation and hygiene; food security and nutrition; shelter and settlement; and health. Part IV sets out provisions on the composition and functions of the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Disaster Risk Management. Part V establishes the Disaster Risk Management Authority, constitutes the Board of Directors of the Authority, and lists the functions of the Authority.

Policy_Content: This Decree, based on the provisions of the Serbian Law on energy, prescribes the criteria and conditions for acquiring the status of an energy-vulnerable customer, including contents and requirements for acquiring the status of an energy vulnerable customer, the method of determining the fulfillment of the conditions for acquiring such status (energy-endangered customer), the validity periods of the decision, the content and scope of the right to a reduction of the monthly payment obligations, procedures for acquiring the status of an energy-endangered customer due to health conditions, the way of keeping records of energy-dangerous customers, the method of providing funds for the protection of energy-dangerous customers, penal provisions and other issues necessary to determine that status. Policy: Presidential Decree No. 279/22 approving the Statute of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forests (MINAGRIF).
Policy_Content: This Presidential Decree approves the Statute of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forests (MINAGRIF). This Statute, consisting of 18 articles divided into four Chapters and two Annexes, establishes composition, duties and responsibilities of the above mentioned ministry, entitled to perform the following activities: a) Propose policies and strategies for national development in the fields of agriculture, livestock, forests, food and nutrition security, in a perspective of sustainable development; b) Draw up proposals for agricultural, livestock, forestry and food security development programmes to be included in the National Development Plan; c) Ensuring the implementation of policies, programmes and projects in the fields of agriculture, livestock, forestry and food security, contained in the National Development Plan; d) Support economic activities related to the production, transport, processing, packaging, industrialization, transformation and commercialization of agricultural, livestock and forestry products; e) Promote and support the development of family farming and business agriculture; f) Promote and ensure the rational management of water resources available for agriculture in conjunction with the relevant Ministerial Department; g) Promoting the elaboration of irrigation plans and ensuring the licensing of the respective projects; h) Promote the increase in production and productivity indices in accordance with technical-scientific progress and through better use of natural, human, material, financial and patrimonial resources; i) Promote the organization and development of infrastructures to support agricultural, livestock and forestry production; j) Foster production and agro-industrialisation, promoting the processing, packaging and marketing of agricultural, livestock and forestry products; k) Promote and support rural extension through technical assistance and the dissemination of good agricultural, livestock and forestry production practices; l) Comply with regional and international obligations regarding the protection and management of forestry, wildlife and beekeeping resources, as well as their economic enhancement; m) Promote the expansion of the forest surface and approve plans for afforestation and reforestation, with a view to their inclusion in the national forest heritage and conservation of terrestrial biodiversity; n) Promote policies and strategies aimed at combating desertification and mitigating the effects of drought, as well as preventing and combating burning and forest fires; o) Ensure the protection of plant and animal species in the national territory against the appearance or spread of local or cross-border diseases and pests; p) Comply with regional and international obligations in terms of animal health and veterinary public health, etc.

Policy: Law “On Local Self-Government.”
Policy_Content: This Law establishes the legal basis for the implementation of local self-government, the procedure for formation and activity, the powers of local self-government bodies, their officials, members, and regulates interaction with state authorities. The system of local self-government is formed by Gengeshes and bodies of territorial public self-government. Gengeshes are representative bodies, whose members are elected by citizens of Turkmenistan living in the respective administrative-territorial units, on the basis of universal, equal and direct suffrage by secret ballot for a period of five years. The procedure for holding elections of members of the Gengesh is determined by the Constitution of Turkmenistan and the Electoral Code of Turkmenistan. Territorial public self-government bodies are a non-membership community of capable individuals on a voluntary basis, without forming a legal entity, the purpose of which is to jointly solve various social problems aimed at meeting the needs of the population in the relevant territory. Bodies of local self-government are not included in the system of state authorities. Citizens of Turkmenistan living in the respective administrative-territorial units exercise local self-government by participating in local referendums, elections, meetings, as well as through elected bodies or meetings of local self-government. Citizens, regardless of nationality, skin color, gender, origin, property and official status, place of residence, language, attitude to religion, political opinions or other circumstances, have equal rights to exercise local self-government directly or through their elected representatives. Foreign citizens, stateless persons permanently or predominantly residing in the relevant territory may participate in local self-government in accordance with the legislation of Turkmenistan. Local self-government bodies are independent within their powers and exercise the powers established by the legislation in the relevant territory. Intervention in the activities of local self-government bodies in matters related to their powers is not allowed. The powers of the Gengesh include: (a) determination of measures for the rational use of natural resources and environmental protection; (b) improvement of places of collective gardening, recreation areas and beaches; (c) organization of public utility facilities for the population (water supply, including potable water supply for the population, gas pipeline, sewerage, energy and heat supply systems, reservoirs, wells, baths and others); and (d) public catering, including school feeding.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. PP-426 “On measures to protect the population and territories from emergency situations associated with dangerous hydrometeorological phenomena and geological processes”.
Policy_Content: The President appoints the Government Commission for ensuring the safe passage of flood waters and mudflows, reducing the risk of snow avalanches and landslides (Governmental Flood Control Commission) in accordance with Appendix No. 1, entitling it with the following tasks: (a) development and implementation of measures to prevent emergency situations associated with hazardous hydrometeorological phenomena and geological processes, as well as strengthening preparations for mitigation of the consequences thereof; (b) coordination of activities and ensuring effective interaction between government bodies, local government bodies and other organizations in the implementation of measures to protect the population and territories from emergencies associated with dangerous hydrometeorological phenomena and geological processes; (c) development and implementation of comprehensive measures for the temporary resettlement of the population located in areas prone to mudflows, floods, avalanches and landslides, and in the future (if necessary) phased resettlement to safe places for permanent residence; (d) management of work to eliminate the consequences of major emergencies associated with dangerous hydrometeorological phenomena and geological processes; (e) checking the status of work on the prevention and elimination of the consequences of emergency situations associated with hazardous natural phenomena in the territories, carried out by ministries and departments, as well as hearing reports from officials on these issues; and (f) annually by March 20, submit to the office of the Security Council under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan a report on the ongoing work to protect the population and territories from emergencies associated with dangerous hydrometeorological phenomena and geological processes, as well as the readiness of forces and means to eliminate them. Measures to protect the population and territories from emergency situations associated with dangerous hydrometeorological phenomena and geological processes are coordinated by the Governmental Flood Control Commission. The instructions and tasks of the Government Flood Control Commission, in accordance with the regulatory legal acts regulating issues within its powers, are binding on all ministries, departments and other organizations, regardless of their legal form and departmental affiliation, the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Karakalpakstan, local self-government (khokimiyats of regions and the city of Tashkent, khokimiyats of districts (cities), as well as citizens. The Governmental Flood Control Commission approves annually until March 5 measures to protect the population and territories from emergencies associated with dangerous hydrometeorological phenomena and geological processes in the corresponding year.

Policy: Regional Law No. 157-Z “On procurement of timber by citizens for individual personal needs.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law establishes the procedure and rate of timber extraction, procurement of non-timber forest resources, collection of alimentary forest resources and medicinal plants by citizens for individual personal needs. It shall not be applicable to the procurement of timber by citizens for their own needs on land of protected natural areas of federal significance, as well as agricultural land not located in state, municipal property, and land plots pertaining to agricultural land allotted in use to third parties. Citizens have the right to extract timber for heating purposes, construction of buildings and other personal needs. Timber extracted by citizens for their own needs may not be alienated or transferred from one person to another by other ways. On forest plots pertaining to the forest fund lands, free from lease for timber extraction, as well as on land plots of agricultural land pertaining to regional or municipal property, citizens exercise timber extraction for their own needs in accordance with purchase and sale contract of forest plantations. The procedure for concluding contracts for the sale of forest plantations for personal needs of citizens in relation to forest plots pertaining to the forest fund land, as well as the procedure for concluding contracts for purchase and sale of forest plantations for the personal needs of citizens in relation to land plots of agricultural land pertaining to regional and municipal property is established by the Regional Government. The term of the contract for the purchase and sale of forest plantations shall not exceed one year. This Regional Law establishes the rates of extraction, procurement and collection of timber and non-timber resources.

The main tasks in the field of tourism in the Magadan region are: (a) creation of a modern, highly efficient and competitive tourism industry; (b) ensuring and maintaining the quality of service for tourists; (c)  creating conditions for the preservation, development, renewal and efficient use of tourism resources located on the regional territory; (d) development of activities of the subjects of the tourism industry; (e) creation of conditions for the development of investment projects in the field of tourism; (f) environmental protection; and (g) development of a system for training and education of subjects of tourism industries in order to provide them with quality services in the field of tourism and tourist activities.

Policy: Law No. ZRU-800 “On standardization”.
Policy_Content: The purpose of this Law is to regulate relations in the field of standardization. This Law shall apply to relations arising from the development, adoption and application of standards and relevant standardization documents, as well as the implementation of state control in the field of standardization. Features of standardization in the military sphere, in the field of protecting state secrets and other information, in the field of the use of atomic energy, ensuring nuclear and radiation safety, in the field of finance and education are established by separate acts of the legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan. National standard shall be intended a standard adopted by the Uzbek Institute of Standards of the Uzbek Agency for Technical Regulation under the Ministry of Investments and Foreign Trade of the Republic of Uzbekistan and available to the general public. Standard shall be intended a document that establishes for general and repeated use rules, general principles or characteristics relating to various activities or their results, and which is aimed at achieving the most optimal degree of regulation in a particular sphere. Standardization shall be intended an activity aimed at achieving the most optimal degree of regulation in a certain sphere, establishing rules for general and repeated use in relation to actual or potential problems. National standardization body is the Uzbek Institute of Standards of the Uzbek Agency for Technical Regulation under the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Object of standardization shall be intended products, goods, services, processes, management systems, terms, symbols, studies (tests), measurements (including sampling) and test methods, marking, labelling, conformity assessment procedures and other objects. The main principles of standardization are: (a) legality; (b) consensus of interested parties in the development of national standards; (c) impartiality; (d) consistency to avoid duplication and inconsistencies in standards; (e) the inadmissibility of a discriminatory attitude towards products, regardless of the country and (or) place of origin of the product, as well as the form of ownership of the manufacturer; and (f) openness and transparency. The main objectives of standardization are: (a) protection of life, health of citizens and their property; (b) environmental protection; (c) protection of the rights and legally protected interests of consumers in matters of product quality; (d) ensuring interchangeability and compatibility of products; (e) improving the quality and competitiveness of products, depending on the level of development of science and technology to meet the needs of the population and sectors of the economy; (f) promotion of saving all types of resources, improvement of technical and economic indicators of production; (g) practical assistance in the implementation of socio-economic and scientific and technical programs and projects; (h) promoting the development of the economy and scientific and technological progress of the Republic of Uzbekistan; (i) ensuring openness and reliability of information on the range and quality of products; (j) assistance in promoting domestic products to foreign markets; and (k) ensuring the unity of measurements.

Policy: Law No. 1818-IX “On energy efficiency.”
Policy_Content: This Law defines the legal, economic and organizational grounds of relations arising in the field of ensuring energy efficiency, and reducing energy shortage, during production, transportation, transmission, distribution, supply and consumption of energy. The scope of ensuring energy efficiency covers energy-efficient measures carried out during the production, transportation, transmission, distribution, supply and consumption of energy. State policy in the field of ensuring energy efficiency is an integral part of the policy in the fields of energy, economy, sustainable development and environmental protection. It establishes the competence of the Cabinet of Ministers, the National Commission and local government in the field of energy efficiency. State policy in the field of ensuring energy efficiency is aimed at achieving the national energy efficiency goal established in the National Energy Efficiency Action Plan. The national goal for energy efficiency is calculated in absolute values of primary energy consumption and final energy consumption by the central executive body implementing state policy in the field of efficient use of fuel and energy resources, energy conservation, renewable energy sources and alternative fuels. When calculating the national energy efficiency goal, the measures defined by this Law, previously implemented measures, as well as factors affecting primary energy consumption, are taken into account, in particular: (a) economically justified energy efficiency potential; (b) trends and forecasts of changes in gross domestic product; (c) changes in energy export and import; (d) state and development of renewable energy, nuclear energy and others fields of energy, carbon absorption and storage technologies; and (e) other factors. The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine shall revise the National Plan every three years. The national plan contains: (a) list of measures aimed at achieving the national goal of energy efficiency, in particular, in the production, transportation, transmission, distribution and consumption of energy, and the terms of their implementation; (b) sources and amounts of funding; (c) the estimated amount of energy savings when implementing measures aimed at achieving the national energy efficiency goal; (d) description of methodical approaches to calculating the amount of energy savings achieved when implementing measures aimed at achieving the national energy efficiency goal; and (e) other information in accordance with the requirements of the legislation of the European Union, decisions of the Energy Community. This Law contains 21 Articles.

Policy: Government Resolution No. 1940 validating the requirements for the circulation of animal by-products.
Policy_Content: These requirements establish mandatory requirements for handling of animal by-products during storage, processing, transportation, sale and use of animal by-products in agricultural production. Storage, processing, handling and transportation of animal by-products should be carried out by the owners and transporters of animal by-products separately from domestic, industrial and mixed wastewater, including sewage from settlements. At the facility for keeping farm animals, owners of animal by-products should be equipped with a separate cleaning system for domestic, industrial and mixed wastewater, including sewage from settlements (in case of their receipt to the facility for keeping farm animals). Storage of raw, unprocessed animal by-products is allowed only on specially equipped facilities and (or) places intended for storage and (or) processing, handling of by-products of animal husbandry, including manure storages, dung storages. The storage of animal by-products should be carried out by owners of animal by-products in ways that do not allow pollution of the environment and components of the natural environment, including the ingress of polluting substances into the aquifer.

Policy: Law No. LP289/2022 “On the basic requirements in the field of radiation safety.”
Policy_Content: This Law establishes the basic safety requirements for the protection of public health as a result of occupational and medical exposure and exposure of the population, as well as from the dangers caused by ionizing radiation. The provisions of this Law apply to all planned, existing or emergency exposure situations involving a risk caused by exposure to ionizing radiation, which cannot be neglected from the point of view of radiation protection or environmental protection for the purpose of long-term protection of human health. This Law does not apply in the case of: (a) exposure due to natural background radiation, such as the presence of radionuclides in the human body and the dominant space radiation near the soil surface; (b) exposure of the public or workers, with the exception of air crews or spacecraft due to exposure to cosmic radiation in flight or in space; and (c) irradiation at the soil surface with radionuclides from untreated Earth’s crust. The general principles of radiation protection established by this law are as follows: (a) substantiation; (b) optimization; and (c) dose limitation or standardization. The National Agency ensures that, prior to issuance of authorization, new classes or types of practical activities, substances or commodities leading to exposure to ionizing radiation are substantiated. This Law contains IX Chapters divided into 106 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II defines concepts. Chapter III determines the system of protection against radiation. Chapter IV establishes requirements for training, preparation and information in the field of protection against radiation. Chapter V regards substantiation and regulation. Chapter VI deals with professional radiation. Chapter VII deals with medical radiation. Chapter VIII regards radiation od the population. Chapter IX establishes general responsibilities of the government, competent authorities and other regulatory control requirements.

Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates some issues in the field of land reclamation in the regional territory, as well as establishes the powers of the regional state authorities in this sphere. Regional Government shall have the following powers in the field of land reclamation: (a) ensuring land reclamation; (b) ownership, use, disposal and management of property state regional property related to land reclamation systems and separately located waterworks; (c)  approval of regional (territorial) programs in the field of land reclamation and control over their implementation; (d) determination of the regional executive body authorized in the field of land reclamation; (e) determination of the regional state executive body responsible for keeping in good state and maintenance of the regional state land reclamation systems and separately located waterworks; (f) financing land reclamation measures and arrangements; and (g) other powers established by the legislation of the Russian Federation and the regional legislation. The authorized state regional body competent in the field of land reclamation shall have the following powers: (a) development and implementation of regional (territorial) programs in the field land reclamation; (b) accounting of reclamation protective forest stands, as well as accounting and conducting monitoring of reclaimed land; (c) organization of measures to preserve reclamation protective forest plantations located on land owned by the region and not transferred to third parties; (d) coordination of the construction and operation of communication lines, power lines, pipelines, roads and other objects on land subject to reclamation and reclaimed land; (e) the provision to the federal executive body, which exercises functions for the provision of public services, state property management in the sphere of the agro -industrial complex, including reclamation, information about reclamation protective forest stands in the region; and (f) other powers provided for by the legislation of the Russian Federation and the regional legislation.

Policy: Law No. LP227/2022 “On industrial emissions”.
Policy_Content: The scope of this law is to create a regulatory framework for preventing pollution caused by types of industrial and economic activities, in order to reduce both emissions into air, water, soil, and waste generation, as well as environmental control, promotion and applying the best available techniques to achieve a high level of protection environment. The subject of this Law are the procedures and rules used in the process of preventing air, water and soil pollution, waste generation, preventing or reducing negative impacts on environment and human health as a result of industrial and economic activity. Emission shall be intended direct or indirect release of substances, vibrations, heat or noise from point or diffuse sources of installation into air, water and soil. The principles of pollution prevention and environmental control are as follows: (a) the principle of priority of environmental measures and actions in the implementation of types of industrial and economic activities; (b) the principle of responsibility for the prevention, limitation, control of pollution, as well as for compensation for damage caused to the environment as a result of industrial and economic activities; (c) the precautionary principle in the operation of installations, management of hazardous substances and mixtures in order to prevent impacts on the environment and human health; (d) the principle of transparency, ensuring access to information about the negative consequences that industrial and economic activities may cause; (e) the green economy principle, which encourages the development of processes and products that reduce or eliminate the use of natural resources and the generation of waste; costs of implementing measures to prevent pollution, as well as costs associated with damage to the environment and its restoration; (g) the principle of use for a fee, which involves the use of natural resources (air, water, soil) by the operator for a fee; (h) the participatory principle, which ensures that all interested parties have access to the environmental permitting process; and (i) the principle of correctness and completeness of information, according to which pollution prevention and environmental control are carried out on the basis of information provided by the operator and information received from the competent authorities. Types of industrial and economic activities provided for in the Annex 1, are carried out on the basis of comprehensive environmental protection permits, and the types of industrial and economic activities provided for in the Annex 2, - on the basis of an environmental permit issued by the Agency for Environmental Protection. If the Agency for Environmental Protection has information that operation of the installation for which an application for the issuance of a comprehensive environmental permit may have a significant impact on environment of a neighboring state, it informs the Ministry of Environmental Protection. This Law contains XI Chapters divided into 60 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II establishes administrative and regulatory functions. Chapter III regards issuance of permits for activities posing risk for the environment. Chapter IV establishes criteria for access to environmental information. Chapter V establishes special provisions for combustion plants. Chapter VI establishes special provisions for combustion installations and combined waste burning installations. Chapter VII establishes special provisions for types of activities and installations in which are used organic solvents. Chapter VIII establishes special provisions for installations producing titanium dioxide. Chapter IX regards environmental control. Chapter X regards transboundary effects. Chapter XI lays down final and transitional provisions.

Policy: Order No. 629 of the Ministry of Agriculture validating the form and procedure for maintaining household registers.
Policy_Content: This Order validates the form of household register (Annex 1) and the procedure of keeping household register by local government (Annex 2). Rural household register includes information and data related to land area allotted for subsidiary smallholding, number of livestock, bees and agricultural equipment. Keeping rural household register shall be performed by local government on the territory of which rural households are located. The period of keeping rural household register by local government shall be five years. The information is collected annually as of January 1 by means of continuous rounds of farms and survey of rural households for the period from January 1 to February 15. Rural household register includes all farms located on the territory administered by local self-government, including those without residential buildings (dilapidated, burned, collapsed, etc.), but also individual residential buildings (farms, forest warden's huts, railway stations, sidetracks, booth houses, etc.) and houses in small settlements. In these cases, the local self-government makes a record about the condition of the facility and absence of citizens who could provide information about the farm). Accounting for private smallholdings is carried out in books in electronic form using a comprehensive information system for collecting and processing accounting and specialized reporting of agricultural producers, generating summary reports, monitoring, accounting, control and analysis of subsidies to support the agro-industrial complex. In relation to land plots of personal subsidiary plots, information on the category of the land plot and its area must be entered. When entering information about the land plot occupied by crops and plantings, it must be taken into account that crops in the aisles of orchards are included in the total of the sown area of the corresponding crop and in the total of the entire sown area. Gardens, berry beds, flower beds (flower beds), green lawns, paths and other areas not occupied by crops are not taken into account in the sown area.

"Green gardens" serve to establish, reproduce, restore, maintain, protect and increase the productivity of trees and shrubs in cities and other settlements. Organization, maintenance and development of "green parks" are financed from additional sources of local budgets, sponsorship donations of individuals and legal entities, grants and other sources not prohibited by legislation. The plots of land on which "green gardens" are located are in the possession (use) of their owners, managers, users and tenants. Construction of "green parks" will be carried out according to the scheme in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation. The following categories have the right to take the initiative to the local executive authorities for the establishment of "Green Parks": (a) state bodies and organizations; (b) self-government bodies of citizens; and (c) owners of multi-apartment buildings. Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the procedure for conducting evacuation measures in case of a risk of occurrence or occurrence of emergency situations of a natural and man-made origin. Evacuation measures are carried out in order to: (a) save lives and preserve the health of people who are in areas where there is a risk of emergency situations, or in emergency zones; (b) reduce material losses in emergency situations; and (c) preserve material and cultural values in emergency situations. The main principles of conducting evacuation measures are: (a) planning and preparation of accommodation of the population, material and cultural values in safe areas (places); (b) priority use of vehicles for carrying out evacuation measures; (c) ensuring the protection of public order and conservation of property of the population in emergency zones during evacuation activities and in safe areas (places); (d) ensuring the return of citizens to places of permanent residence, as well as material and cultural values in places of permanent storage after the elimination of the risk of emergency or liquidation of an emergency; and (e) informing the public about the progress of emergency rescue operations and other urgent work.

Policy: Equality Law No. 11/2022.
Policy_Content: This Law aims to guarantee effective equality of rights and duties between men and women, with a view to eliminating all forms of discrimination and creating the same opportunities, namely with regard to political participation and the exercise of positions of decision, aiming to achieve a more just, democratic and balanced society. It applies throughout the national territory and is binding on all public entities. Private entities are encouraged to promote gender equality, under the terms of this Law. Parity between men and women includes the adoption of all measures aimed at eliminating any distinction, exclusion or limitation based on sex, which have the consequence or purpose of compromising or preventing the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of rights relating to political participation and decision-making. Parity of treatment includes, namely: a) absence of any types of discrimination based on sex, in particular with regard to political participation and access to and exercise of decision-making positions; b) mandatory constitution of lists for the National Assembly, Regional Legislative Assembly and local authorities, other elective bodies, as well as decision-making positions, on an equal basis, in order to guarantee the effective equality of participation between men and women; c) right to benefit of related rights and privileges, and don't suffer any kind of discrimination based on sex due to the exercise of rights recognized by the Constitution and other laws of the Republic.

Policy: Resolution No. 1030 of the Cabinet of Ministers on some issues of identification of sites of increased danger.
Policy_Content: This Resolution establishes the procedure for classifying objects on which installations, storages (reservoirs, vessels), pipelines, machines, aggregates are located, technological equipment, structures or a complex of structures located within the object on the surface of the earth or underground, in which one or more hazardous substances are temporarily or permanently used, processed, manufactured, transported, stored, as facilities of increased hazard of the corresponding class. The identification of facilities of increased danger is carried out by legal entities or natural persons - entrepreneurs in relation to facilities owned or managed by them. The identification of facilities of increased danger in relation to the objects being designed is carried out by construction customers. Identification of facilities of increased danger in relation to objects, information about which is a state secret, is carried out in compliance with the requirements of the relevant regulatory legal acts. The identification of the object of increased danger is carried out in three stages. At the first stage, a list of hazardous substances is drawn up by individual names, classes of hazardous substances and hazard categories listed in Tables 1 and 2 of the Annex 1. At the second stage, a list of production units that contain hazardous substances, defined in accordance with paragraph 5 of this Procedure, is drawn up. At the third stage, the mass of the hazardous substance in each individual production unit is determined and the total mass of hazardous substances is calculated separately for each individual name of the hazardous substance determined in accordance with Table 1 of the Annex 1.

Policy: Resolution No. UP-220 of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan “On additional measures to implement energy saving technologies and the development of low power renewable energy sources”.
Policy_Content: The President, in order to introduce state support mechanisms for the widespread use of renewable energy sources by the population and business entities, to provide them with electrical and thermal energy through these sources, as well as to stimulate the efficient use of energy resources in buildings and structures for administrative and household purposes decrees as follows: (a) to allocate financial incentives for the purchase by the population and business entities of installations of renewable energy sources; (b) to implement targeted measures for the use of alternative energy sources in buildings and structures for administrative purposes, including in settlements and households; (c) to ensure the widest attraction of private investment in the industry by increasing the attractiveness of business projects for the construction of micro and small hydroelectric power plants; and (d) to provide comprehensive support for business entities engaged in the production of solar and wind power plants, as well as small hydroelectric power plants. Natural persons (consumers) shall be granted the opportunity to purchase installations of solar and wind power plants and solar water heating devices (installations of renewable energy sources) of domestic manufacturing, with payment in installments without interest for 3 years at the expense of the Extrabudgetary Intersectoral Fund for Energy Saving the Ministry of Energy. Part of the expenses of consumers who have paid the full cost, purchased and installed installations of renewable energy sources, is compensated at the expense of the Fund in the amount in accordance with Annexes Nos. 1 and 2 to this Decree. Consumers shall be granted the opportunity to pay in installments or deduct the amount of compensation from the final retail price when purchasing renewable energy installations directly from domestic manufacturing enterprises, enterprises providing delivery, installation and start-up services (production and service enterprises), at domestic retail facilities, including through e-commerce tools.

Policy: Resolution of the Council of Ministers No. 82/2022 establishing preventive measures to face the current situation and possible future disruptions, guaranteeing the security of energy supply.
Policy_Content: The foreseeable difficulties in the supply of natural gas require that Portugal adopt adequate measures to reduce demand and guarantee supply and to reinforce its capacity to receive and supply natural gas, namely from Sines. Thus, and under the current circumstances, it is essential to define measures that contribute to the security of energy supply. Therefore, in the first place, a strategic reserve of water is established in the reservoirs associated with the hydroelectric developments for the purposes of security of supply of the national electricity system (SEN), in order to guarantee that the storage in these reservoirs reaches, at least, a capacity corresponding to an increase in stored electrical energy. This measure aims to obtain a strategic reserve of water equivalent to about 6 days of average national consumption, which is relevant for satisfying consumption peaks, as it guarantees security of supply to the SEN in about 45 days. In the case of hydroelectric power plants with pumping, the obligation to set up a storage reserve does not prevent the use of the turbine-pumping cycle. Another of the measures adopted relates to the decision, and authorization of the corresponding investments, to implement in Sines the infrastructure for the transfer of liquefied natural gas between ships.

Policy: Land Commission Act 2022 (No. 47 of 2022).
Policy_Content: The objectives of this Act are to: (I) provide an independent quasi-judicial process for the expeditious determination of land tenure conversion applications regarding customary land under the Land (Tenure Conversion) Act 1963; (II) align the functions and jurisdiction of the Commission, as an independent quasi-judicial tribunal to other legislation and bodies responsible for dealing with land matters; (III) have an independent quasi-judicial process that protects national land as being acquired for public purposes by determining national land and to ensure settlement claims are properly assessed. This Act lays down provisions on the establishment, constitution, jurisdiction and functions of the Land Commission for Papua New Guinea; appointment and tenure of and qualification requirements for commissioners; powers, duties, functions and jurisdiction of the Chief Commissioner; delegation and powers of the Deputy Chief Commissioner; appointment of a Special Commissioner or Assistant Commissioner; appointment and duties of the Registrar of the Commission; establishment of a Register for the Commission; declaration of national land; description and certification of the land contained in the declaration by the Registrar; declaration of national land where land was acquired before and after the Independence Day; ownership of national land; conflicting claims in respect of any land, and dispute settlement; determination of the customary land ownership; jurisdiction of the Local Land Court over the disputes relating to ownership by custom or to the right to its use by custom; ownership of customary land for certain purposes; agreement for settlement; marking of land by the Commission; appeals and references to the National Court; conflict with a title previously registered under the Land Registration Act 1981; and power of the Head of State to make regulations for carrying out or giving effect to this Act. This Act does not derogate any rights of the State to or in respect of land under any other law.

Policy: Decree on the conditions, manner and procedure for granting the use of state-owned agricultural land for non-agricultural purposes.
Policy_Content: This Decree, based on the provisions of the Serbian Law on agricultural land, prescribes the necessary conditions, method and procedure for granting state-owned agricultural land for use as for non-agricultural purposes, as well as the criteria for determining the amount of compensation for granting state agricultural land for such use. This text applies to land that is registered in the real estate cadastre of the Republic Geodetic Institute by type as agricultural land owned by the Republic of Serbia. Cadastral plots that are subject to restitution in the sense of the law governing the return of land to previous owners cannot be subject to use defined in this text. State agricultural land can be put to use for: 1) energy production using renewable sources of wind and solar energy by building, i.e. installing: (1) wind power plant with accompanying infrastructure (windmill facilities, transmission lines, pylons, other facilities in the function of the power plant, lighting, etc.) and equipment for the production of electricity using wind energy; (2) solar energy power plant with accompanying infrastructure (solar panel facilities, transmission lines, other facilities in the function of the power plant, lighting, etc.) and equipment for the production of electricity using solar energy; 2) performing geological exploration works, i.e. exploitation of mineral raw materials: (1) clay, gravel, sand, stone, etc., (2) oil and natural gas with facilities in the function of geological research, ie oil and gas exploitation; 3) carrying out works on the disposal of tailings, ash, slag and other dangerous and harmful substances on agricultural land for a certain period of time with the submission of the necessary approvals issued by the ministry responsible for mining and geology.

Keyword: Agricultural land, Public land, Land-use planning

Policy: Resolution No. 962 of the Cabinet of Ministers validating Model Statute of water users’ association.
Policy_Content: Water users’ association is formed by owners of agricultural land plots that have not been transferred for use, and/or users of agricultural land plots with the right of lease, sublease, emphyteusis, permanent use, who have a permit for a special water use, if the need to obtain such a permit by the water user is provided for by law, in order to effectively carry out hydraulic melioration on agricultural land plots that are included in the service territory of the association and on which water is used for the needs of hydrotechnical melioration or there is a technical possibility of its implementation. The purpose of the association's activity is the effective implementation of hydraulic melioration on agricultural land plots included in the organization's service territory. The association does not have the right to manufacture products, provide services and perform work not related to the provision of hydrotechnical reclamation, except for the production and sale of other products during the main activity of the organization, the income from the sale of which is used exclusively to finance the statutory activities of the association. The association is formed as a non-entrepreneurial entity, is non-profit and does not aim to obtain profit for its distribution among the members of the association. The main areas of activity of the association are: (a) provision of services for intake, delivery of water for hydraulic melioration and its distribution among water users in the association's service territory; (b) ensuring, within the service territory of the organization, operation and proper maintenance, restoration, reconstruction of the objects of the engineering infrastructure of reclamation systems, which have been transferred to the ownership of the association; (c) collection and analysis of information on water users' need for water within the association's service territory and conclusion of contracts with such water users for water abstraction and delivery; (d) provision of services for supply (absorption), distribution and/or removal of water for the purposes of hydraulic melioration to members of the association, as well as to other water users who are owners/users of land plots included in the service area of association, on the basis of the rules for the provision of services by the association and contracts (if concluded) with such water users; (e) restoration of engineering infrastructure facilities of the reclamation network, reconstruction and modernization of irrigation, drainage and drainage systems; (f) establishment of water accounting at watershed points and in separate sections of the reclamation network; (g) prevention of water pollution for irrigation, monitoring and improvement of the ecological condition of waterbodies, as well as prevention of flooding, waterlogging, salinization and land pollution within the association's service territory; (h) implementation of measures to preserve and increase soil fertility within the organization's service territory; (i) removal of surplus surface and drainage waters from the association's service territory; (j) collection of fees for services provided by the organization; (k) attracting funding (receiving state aid, grants, loans, etc.) to ensure the operation and maintenance of engineering infrastructure facilities of reclamation systems belonging to the association, in the association's service territory, and to carry out measures for their restoration, reconstruction, modernization; (l) purchase of equipment, machinery, other goods, works (services) necessary to ensure irrigation and drainage on agricultural land plots that are included in the association's service territory;  (m) production and sale of other products during the main activity of the association, the income from the sale of which is used exclusively to finance the statutory activities of the association; (n) organization of training of members of the association in order to improve knowledge on land and water resources management, modern technologies of irrigated agriculture, drawing up business plans, improving the efficiency of irrigation, drainage, etc.; (o)  implementation of new methods and technologies for the conservation of water and energy resources during the operation of melioration systems and operational planning of irrigation; and (p)  carrying out other activities that are not prohibited by law and correspond to the purpose of the association.
