Policy: Regional Law No. 35-ZRT “On the regulation of certain issues in the field of gardening and horticulture by citizens for their own needs in the Republic of Tatarstan.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates some issues in the field of gardening and horticulture by citizens for their own needs on the regional territory. In order to provide state support by regional state bodies for the conduct of gardening and horticulture bodies by citizens for their own needs the Republic of Tatarstan has the right to: (a) create subdivisions in its structure that ensure the implementation of the Regional policy to support citizen conducting gardening and horticulture; (b) adopt regional state programs envisaging activities aimed at supporting gardening and horticulture by citizens, including investment programs; (c) conduct educational work in order to popularize the management of gardening and horticulture by citizens; (d) organize within the boundaries of the regional territory of gardening or horticulture through supply of heat and electricity, water, gas, sewerage, supply of fuel within the powers established by legislation of the Russian Federation; (e) finance the implementation of complex cadastral works in relation to the cadastral quarters within which are located gardening or horticultural areas; (f) at the request of the partnership or participants in common shared ownership on common property located within the boundaries of the area of gardening or horticulture, free of charge to acquire in the state property of the Republic of Tatarstan such common property (roads, power grid facilities, water supply, communications and other objects) in the event that such property, in accordance with legislation of the Russian Federation may pertain to the state property; and (g)  provide support for the maintenance of gardening or horticulture by citizens in other forms established by the legislation of the Russian Federation and the legislation of the Republic of Tatarstan. The main principles of state support for the conduct by citizens of gardening and horticulture are: (a) targeting and targeted nature of state support; (b) equal access to state support; (c) openness of procedures for providing state support; (d) a combination of financial and other measures of state support; and (e) provision of state support in compliance with the requirements, established by the legislation of the Russian Federation and the legislation Republic of Tatarstan.

Policy: Regulation No. 772 on market regulation of Norwegian-produced grains and oilseeds.
Policy_Content: The purpose of the present Regulation, adopted by the Ministry of Agriculture and Food, is to contribute to the effective implementation of market regulation for Norwegian-produced grains and oilseeds that are marketed through the grain marketing scheme. The objective of market regulation is to achieve the agreed-upon target price in accordance with the assumption that the target price can be achieved through market balance. The target price is understood to mean the producer price determined in the agricultural settlement (jordbrukoppgjøret) for feed grains, food wheat, food rye, and oilseeds of basic quality delivered to specific reception facilities along the Oslo Fjord. Market balance is understood to mean that the consumption of food and feed grains matches the Norwegian production and supplementary imports of food and feed grains, and that the marketing of the Norwegian-produced goods takes place at the prices agreed upon in the agricultural agreement (jordbruksavtalen). Funds allocated for market regulation within the grain sector can be used to finance the following yield measures that the market regulator initiates or facilitates: 1. Carryover of Norwegian-produced grain from one grain year to another; and 2. Price reduction through alternative use of surplus Norwegian-produced grain.

Policy: Law No. 2321-IX on amendments of some legislative acts.
Policy_Content: Land Code (No. 2768-III of 2001) shall be amended in relation to the change of specific use of land plots pertaining to public and municipal property, assigned to the categories of land for residential and public development, land for industry, transport, communications, energy, defense and other purposes, as well as land plots (except for land plots located in the territories, properties of the nature reserve fund, and land plots for forestry purposes), on which buildings and structures are located, which are privately owned by the land user, who uses the land plots with the rights of permanent use, lease, emphyteusis, superficies, may be carried out by the land user. Land suitable for agriculture (except self-forested land) should be provided primarily for the following purposes: (a) farming; (b) forest management; (c) constitution of protected areas. Forestry is authorized on land of all categories in compliance with the requirements regarding the use of the land plot for its intended purpose. Natural persons and legal entities have the right to classify land plots (including self-forested ones) owned by them and belonging to all categories of land (except for nature reserve and other nature conservation land) as forestry lands, as well as to perform forestry on them. A self-forested plot is a plot of land of any category of land (except for land for forestry purposes, nature reserves and other nature protection purposes) with an area of more than 0.5 hectares, partially or completely covered with forest vegetation, the afforestation of which occurred naturally. Forest Code (No.3852-XII of 1994) shall be amended in relation to public forest concept, in particular as regards inclusion of all forests on the territory of Ukraine, regardless of the land categories on which they grow according to the main purpose, and regardless of the ownership right to them, including forest plots, linear protective plantations with an area of at least 0.1 hectares, other forested areas. Natural persons and legal entities may, in accordance with the procedure established by law, acquire land plots for afforestation, and may also own forests constituted by afforestation on acquired ownership in land plots according to the procedure established by law, as well as self-forested plots on land plots acquired in accordance with the procedure established by law. Forest management is authorized on land of all categories in compliance with the requirements regarding the use of the land plot for its intended purpose. The rights and obligations of permanent forest users and forest owners in accordance with Forest Code and other laws apply to enterprises, institutions, organizations of all forms of ownership that use or own forests on land of all categories. Afforestation is carried out by cultivating forest species or by promoting natural regeneration on lands suitable for creating forests that are not covered by forest vegetation. Afforestation can be carried out on land of all categories in compliance with the requirements regarding the use of the land plot for its intended purpose. Law No. 962-IV “On land protection” shall be amended in relation to changing hayfields, pastures and fallows to other land categories within the boundaries of agricultural land plots of state and communal property, transferred for use under the terms of lease, emphyteusis, which is prohibited. This requirement does not apply to the change of land plots of agricultural plots of state and communal ownership, the right of lease, emphyteusis in respect of which arose before the entry into force of this amendment. Conservation shall be applicable to: (a)  land plots used in violation of the requirements for the protection of land against erosion and landslides; (b) arable land, which has one of the indicators that characterizes soil properties and determines the need for land conservation according to natural-agricultural zones; (c) degraded land, unproductive land that do not have steppe, meadow, forest vegetation, the economic use of which is ecologically dangerous and economically inefficient, as well as technogenically polluted land plots on which it is impossible to obtain ecologically clean products, and the presence of people on these land plots is dangerous for their health; and (d) other degraded and unproductive lands.

Policy: Law No. 2320-IX “On waste management”.
Policy_Content: This Law defines the legal, organizational, and economic principles of activities related to the prevention of formation, reduction of the volume of waste generation, reduction of negative consequences from waste management activities, promotion of preparation of waste for reuse, recycling and recovery in order to prevent negative impact thereof on human health and surrounding natural environment. This Law regulates relations regarding prevention of generation and management of waste generated in Ukraine, as well as management of waste transported through the territory of Ukraine, exported outside its border and imported into Ukraine for the purpose of recovery, including recycling. It shall not be applicable to: (a) gaseous substances, including non-catchable substances that are emitted directly into atmospheric air; (b) radioactive waste; (c) decommissioned military and civilian explosives; (d) uncontaminated soil and other natural materials extracted during construction works, provided that such materials are used in construction in their natural (original) state in the area where they were extracted; (e) by-products of animal origin; (f) substances intended for use as feed materials; and (g) sewage and drainage water. The main objectives of state policy in the field of waste prevention and management are: (a) protection of human health and the natural environment from the negative impact of waste; (b) implementing measures in the field of waste management without endangering people's health and causing damage to the surrounding natural environment within the limits of the established standards of harmful effects of physical factors; (c) compliance with the hierarchy of waste management; and (d) introduction of extended producer responsibility. Basic principles of state policy in the field of prevention of waste generation and waste management are: (a) prevention - the generator or owner of waste takes measures to prevent the generation of waste, as well as to avoid, reduce or mitigate the negative impact of waste on human health and the surrounding natural environment; (b) "polluter pays" - the generator or owner of waste covers the costs of preventing the generation of waste, its collection, transportation and processing, including the costs of creating and maintaining waste treatment facilities; (c) territorial proximity - waste treatment is carried out at the nearest waste treatment facility or installation, or at the burial site waste, taking into account its ecological and economic efficiency, in accordance with regional and local waste management plans; and (d) formation of a competitive environment in the field of waste management - economic entities, state authorities and local self-government bodies are obliged to promote the development of competition and must not commit any illegal actions that may have a negative impact on competition in the field of waste management. The hierarchy of waste management is implemented by central and local executive bodies, local self-government bodies, enterprises, institutions and organizations with the aim (in order of priority): (a) prevention of waste generation; (b) waste preparation for reuse; (c) recycling; (d) recovery of waste (including energy production); and (e) waste removal. Waste is classified in two categories: (a) hazardous waste; and (b) non-hazardous waste. Local self-government bodies ensure household waste management in accordance with the rules for the improvement of the locality, regional and local waste management plans and provide each generator of household waste with the provision of household waste management services. This Law contains XI Sections divided into 59 Articles. Section I lays down general provisions. Section II defines subjects in the field of waste management. Section III establishes powers of executive government bodies and local government in the field of waste prevention and waste management. Section IV deals with hazardous waste. Section V deals with domestic waste. Section VI regards incineration, co-incineration and disposal of waste. Section VII regards licensing, authorization system and provision of information in the field of waste management. Section VIII regards plans and programs of waste management. Section IX establishes liability for the infringement of the legislation in the field of waste management. Section X regards international cooperation in the field of waste management. Section XI lays down final and transitional provisions.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. 382 “"On measures to reduce the area of forest fires in the Russian Federation".
Policy_Content: The President, with a vie of reducing the areas of forest fires in the Russian Federation, decrees that the Government of the Russian Federation, together with the top officials of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation, should ensure that the area of forest fires on the land of the forest fund in 2022-2030 is reduced by at least 50 percent compared to the level of 2021. The Government of the Russian Federation within a month must approve for the constituent entities of the Russian Federation for the period up to 2030 the target indicators for the annual reduction in the area of forest fires on the land of the forest fund, as well as the methodology for calculating such indicators. The highest officials of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation shall ensure: (a) achievement of the target indicators provided in this Decree; (b) gradual achievement by 2030 of the level at which the share of forest fires on the land of the forest fund, liquidated within the first day from the moment of detection, in the total number of forest fires on the land of the forest fund will be 100 percent; and (c) annually, no later than March 1 of the year following the reporting one, submit to the Government of the Russian Federation a report on the implementation of this Decree.

Policy: Order No. 1.337 of the Ministry of Environment, Water and Forests validating METHODOLOGICAL NORMS from June 10, 2022 on the control of shipments of waste.
Policy_Content: The purpose of these Methodological Rules shall be to organize, supervise and control shipments of waste in such a way as to take account of the need to preserve, protect and improve the quality of the environment and human health. The provisions of the present Methodological Rules shall apply to all authorities, public institutions, as well as economic operators. The import/transfer of any type or quantity of waste in Romania may be carried out only to recovery facilities, as defined in these methodological rules, exclusively for itself, without being able to transfer their ownership to other entities, which it could also carry out capitalization operations before mandatory capitalization operations are carried out. The import/transfer of waste of any kind in Romania, in order to eliminate it, is prohibited. The transfer of waste shall take place only after it has been certified that the recovery facility has the technical capabilities in relation to the types, categories and quantities of waste for which a shipment is planned, in accordance with environmental protection regulations and with the declarations submitted to the ROAFM register. When planning a shipment, the economic operator shall ensure that the waste in its entirety is received at the recovery facilities. The specialized control for waste transfer organized in the designated points of crossing the state border of Romania is mandatory and is carried out by the commissioners of the National Environmental Guard (GNM), at the request of the representatives of the Romanian Border Police regarding the general control of the means of transport in the area of competence.

Policy: Order No. 186 of the Minister of Agriculture validating the Methodology for the creation of electronic soil maps.
Policy_Content: Methodology for the creation of electronic soil maps establishes the process of creating an electronic soil map consisting of the following works: (a) preparation of source materials, including the collection of information about previously work performed on a specific area of the area related to creation of an electronic cartographic information in order to avoid duplication of processes when creating an electronic soil map, systematization and analysis of the collected information (data) coverage of the territory of the object; (b) vectorization of soil contours and formation of a database of electronic soil map; and (c) design of a vectorized electronic soil map. In order to ensure the accuracy and completeness of the vectorization of soil contours shall be performed analysis of information (data) of soil research, during which the classification of soils by granulometric (mechanical) composition, chemical, physical and morphological properties of soils, soil records research, symbols and legend to the soil map are studied. The final electronic soil map contains data on the structure, features, properties of soils in the under study area (percentage of components in the soil complex, size in granules, degree of salinity, presence and amount of crushed stone, stones in soils), symbols and corner stamp.

Policy: Resolution No. 95 of the Cabinet of Ministers on measures to refund part of the cost of agricultural producers for the introduction of water-saving technologies.
Policy_Content: This Resolution establishes the procedure for reimbursement of a part of the cost of agricultural producers for the introduction of water-saving irrigation technologies used for cultivation of cotton, grain crops, vegetables (including potatoes), sugar, oilseeds, legumes and medicinal plants. The Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Uzbekistan - annually, in the formation of the main parameters of the State budget, shall provide for subsidies allocated to cover a part of the costs for the introduction of water-saving irrigation technologies and transfer them to relevant ministries and agencies in the prescribed manner. Agricultural producers who have received subsidies for introducing water-saving irrigation technology must use this technology for otherwise the subsidies will be reduced in the following manner: (a) 80 percent of the subsidy if the technology is not used in the second year; (b) 60 percent of the subsidy if the technology is not used; (c) 40 percent of the subsidy if the technology is not used; (d) if the technology is not used in the fifth year, 20 percent of the subsidy will be returned to the ministry and office that provided the subsidy in the prescribed manner. If the agricultural producers do not use this technology to the full extent for five years, the subsidy will be completely removed.

Policy: Law No.2 of 2022 on the Emergency Support for Food Security and Development.
Policy_Content: This Law consisting of 18 articles aims at allowing the government to transfer public funds to meet the urgent needs of Iraqis for food security, alleviating poverty, achieving financial stability in light of the global emergency developments, by providing services to citizens, raising their standard of living, creating job opportunities, maximizing the benefit from State resources, advancing development, resuming work on projects that have been stalled due to lack of financing, and proceeding with new projects. To this end, the Ministry of Finance created an account and allocated 25 trillion Iraqi dinars ($17.14 billion) for staple food supplies, gas and electricity, as well as payment of public servant salaries. Part of the amount will be destined, among others, to (i) finance the development of the Municipality of Baghdad (30%); (ii) develop regions of governorates that are not organized in a region and distributed according to population ratios and poverty for each governorate; (iii) the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs for programs of social protection and people with special needs; (iv) Ministry of Agriculture for providing support in the following: seeds of wheat, barley, rapeseed, forage barley and yellow corn, fertilizers, feed purchase, combat desertification, pesticides, veterinary medicine, irrigation systems, and agricultural planes, payment of previous dues for seeds; (v) Ministry of Petroleum; (vi) The Ministry of Construction and Housing to rebuild areas destroyed following terrorist attacks; (vii) Ministry of Water Resources; (viii) Ministry of Education.

Equipment such as renewable energy sources and portable generators shall be intended solar, water, wind, and portable generators to provide electricity to pumping stations and irrigation wells for irrigating cotton and sorghum fields with water-saving irrigation technologies and energy generating devices for no less than 10 hectares. The following shall be attached to the application: (a) information on cotton and winter wheat crop fields (in contour sections) where water-saving irrigation technologies have been introduced; (b) certificate and technical passport of purchased renewable energy sources and equipment such as portable generators; (c) documents on the purchase and installation of equipment such as renewable energy sources and portable generators (contracts with the contractor, completed construction, testing and adjustment works); and (d) copies of the applicant's state registration certificate.

Policy_Content: This Decree establishes the Operational Regulation of the Integrated Platform for Dissemination and Communication of Early Warning System for Floods and Cyclones. The Regulation, consisting of 22 articles divided into three Chapters and a Glossary, establishes the objectives of these norms such as: a) guarantee timely access to accurate information and advance warning of floods and cyclones to all people in risk areas through the diversified use of means of dissemination and communication; b) strengthen inter-institutional collaboration between the Ministries that oversee the areas of meteorology, water resources management and the disaster risk management and reduction sector for the effective operation of the Integrated Electronic Platform for Dissemination of Information Flow of Early Warning of Floods and Cyclones; c) strengthen national and local capacity on accessing, interpreting, disseminating and communicating flood and cyclone early warning information to local communities; d) improve the capacity for analysis, interpretation, production and timely dissemination of accurate information on early warning of floods and cyclones by the Ministries that oversee the areas of meteorology and water resources management; e) establish inter-institutional collaboration mechanisms that allow an integrated articulation and rapid assessment of data and information on early warning of floods and cyclones; f) strengthen the production and processing of data and information on early warning of floods and cyclones, based on permanent rules for the dissemination and communication of harmonized and simplified messages; g) ensure that these early warning messages issued by the disaster risk management and reduction sector, contribute to timely prevention and specific response depending on the level of alert and magnitude of the event; and h) establish the Integrated Electronic Platform for the Dissemination of Information Flow for Early Warning of Floods and Cyclones.

The value of the monetary transfer varies between USD 32 and USD 45 per month, allocated according to the magnitude of the shocks.

Policy: Order No. 371 of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Ecology validating the Methodology for quantitative determination of greenhouse gas emissions and greenhouse gas absorptions.
Policy_Content: This Methodology establishes the procedure for quantitative determination of greenhouse gas emissions for the purposes of state accounting of greenhouse gas emissions and is intended for legal entities and individual entrepreneurs whose economic and other activities are accompanied by greenhouse gas emissions. Quantifying greenhouse gas emissions is carried out as a whole for organizations, or for one or more structural divisions thereof, united in a single production chain. In all cases, quantitation limits and criteria for their choice must be precisely and unambiguously determined. In case of branches or separate divisions of the organization located on the territory of several constituent entities of the Russian Federation, quantitative determination of greenhouse gas emissions is carried out separately for branches or separate subdivisions located on the territory of various subjects (regions) of the Russian Federation. Organizations document the boundaries of quantification of greenhouse gas emissions. The emission quantification limits include direct greenhouse gas emissions determined in accordance with Annex No. 2, which are directly reported from the structures of organization and ongoing processes. Sources of greenhouse gas emissions within the quantitative definitions are production and technological processes at the facilities of organizations, resulting in greenhouse gases emission. Each category of greenhouse gas emission sources includes similar production and technological processes leading to the emissions of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, carried out within the boundaries of quantification. List of emission source categories and greenhouse gases is contained in the Annex No. 1. Each source of greenhouse gas emissions must be classified as one of selected source categories or excluded from quantitative determination of greenhouse gas emissions. The list of sources of greenhouse gas emissions is updated by organization in the event of the emergence of new sources of greenhouse gas emissions, changes in technological processes, changes in methods of quantitative determination of greenhouse gas emissions, global warming potentials of greenhouse gases and in other cases that significantly affect on results (more than 5% of total annual emissions). From the quantification of greenhouse gas emissions, the organization excludes sources of emissions, which in total amount to less than 5% per year of the total emissions in the organization, but not more than 50 thousand tons of CO2-equivalent/year. Quantifying greenhouse gas emissions for categories sources listed in the Annex No. 1, carried out using the methods established for the respective categories of greenhouse gas emission sources in Annex No. 2, including: (a) calculation method based on activity data and emission factors; (b) calculation method based on material and raw materials balance; (c) calculation method based on periodic measurements of greenhouse gas emissions; and (d) method for continuous monitoring of greenhouse gas emissions. Input data for quantifying emissions of greenhouse gases are: (a) data characterizing the intensity of production and technological processes at emission sources (e.g., fuel consumption by type, consumption carbon-containing materials, production, commodity-transport work and other); (b) data characterizing the physicochemical properties of fuel, raw materials, materials, products and production and consumption waste, necessary to determine the volumes of emissions in accordance with the selected methods (for example, carbon content in raw materials and products, component composition of gaseous fuel and carbon-containing mixtures, calorific value of fuel capacity, gas density, etc.); (c) emission factors characterizing the specific volume of greenhouse gases emissions in the process of production and technological processes (e.g. emission factors for combustion of various types of fuel in stationary, mobile or flare installations, etc.); (d) conversion factors required for the conversion of one physical or energy units to others (for example, conversion factors for energy units); and (e) global warming potentials used to bring the amount of emissions of various greenhouse gases to a single value – tons CO2 equivalent. The Methodology for quantitative volume determination of greenhouse gas absorption establishes the procedure for calculating the volume of absorption of greenhouse gases by: (a) forest fund land; (b) land transferred to the category of forest fund land; (c) agricultural land; (d) land converted to agricultural land; (e) land of the water fund (related to wetlands); (f) land converted to wetlands; (g) urban land; (h) land transferred to the category of urban land, land of protected areas and facilities, and land of industry, energy, transport, communications, broadcasting, television, informatics, land for ensuring open space activities, land of defense, security and land of other special purpose.

Policy: Order No. 191 of the Minister of Ecology, Geology and Natural Resources validating the Methodology for conducting the analysis of the total environmental benefit.
Policy_Content: This Methodology establishes the procedure for conducting the analysis of the total environmental benefit. The Total Environmental Benefit Analysis is an approach to the selection of best oil spill response methods aimed at maximum protection of human health and the environment. Total Environmental Benefit Analysis process includes the following steps: (a) collection and evaluation of information; (b) predicting the consequences; (c) search for compromise solutions; and (d) choice of optimal methods. At the stage of collecting and evaluating information, the following is required: (a) definition of a spill scenario, based on which shall be identified the following information: about an incident or accident, about the state and movement of oil, about identifying resources at risk; and (b) identification of possible oil spill response methods. For each proposed scenario, the following information is determined about the incident or accident: (a) location; (b) type and properties of oil; (c) spill volume; and (d) the duration of the spill, the prevailing hydrodynamic and meteorological conditions, time of year.

Policy: Regional Decree No. 266-P validating the Regulation on state natural reserve of regional significance “Timonovsky”.
Policy_Content: State natural reserve of regional significance “Timonovsky” shall be classified as complex (landscape) reserve. The reserve is protected area of regional significance considered national patrimony. The objectives of creating the Reserve are: (a) preservation in the natural state of unique, irreplaceable, valuable in ecological, scientific, recreational, historical, cultural and aesthetic relations of high-mountain and valley natural complexes and objects, which are spawning grounds for Pacific salmon, an endorheic alpine lake Costacan with a unique isolated population of Dolly Varden (Salvelinus malma) of Holocene age, as well as natural and natural-anthropogenic hydrothermal ecosystems of the Timonov hot springs, ecosystems of boreal deciduous (stone-birch) forests, floodplain willow forests, lowland floodplain and terraced swamps, creeping forests of cedar and alder elfin, subalpine meadows, mountain tundra and loaches, stony talus, lava and slag fields, preservation of their environment-forming functions and biological productivity; (b) protection of rare and endangered species of animals, plants, fungi and thermophilic organisms listed in the Red Book of the Russian Federation and the Red Book of the Kamchatka Territory, their key habitats (growth); (c) protection and ensuring the reproduction of valuable in the economic, scientific and cultural aspects of hunting resources: black-capped marmot, bighorn sheep, brown bear, sable, river otter; protection of key places their habitats and migration routes; (d) protection of spawning grounds for all types of Pacific salmon, isolated populations of Dolly Varden (Salvelinus malma) of Lake Kostakan, ensuring their reproduction; (e) protection and regulation of use in recreational and balneological purposes of unique hydrothermal ecosystems Timonovsky hot springs; (f)  creation of conditions for the development of the infrastructure of the regulated ecological tourism in accordance with the established recreational capacity of individual natural complexes and objects of the Reserve; (g) implementation of state environmental monitoring (state monitoring of the environment); and (h) environmental education of the population.

Policy: Regional Law No. 80-Z regulating some issues in the field of ensuring radiation safety of the regional population.
Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates legal relations to ensure the radiation safety of the regional population and determines the powers of the regional state authorities in the field of radiation safety. The powers of the regional Legislative Assembly in the field of radiation safety include: (a) adoption of regional laws in the field of radiation safety; (b) control over the implementation of this Regional Law and other regional laws in the field of radiation safety; and (c) exercising other powers in the field of ensuring radiation safety. The powers of the Regional Government in the field of ensuring radiation safety include: (a) adoption of regulatory legal acts in the field of ensuring radiation safety within its powers; (b) development, approval and implementation of the regional state programs in the field of radiation safety; (c) determination of the authorized regional executive body competent in the field of radiation safety; (d) organization of control over the radiation situation in the regional territory; (e) participation in the organization and conduct of operational activities in the event of a threat of a radiation accident on the regional territory; (f) participation in the implementation of measures to eliminate the consequences of radiation accidents; (g) provision of conditions for the implementation and protection of the rights of citizens and the observance of the interests of the state in the field of ensuring radiation safety within their powers; (h) interaction with territorial bodies of federal executive bodies authorized to exercise state administration, state supervision and control in the field of ensuring radiation safety; (i) coordination of decisions on the placement and construction of radioactive waste storage facilities; and (j) determining the procedure for notifying local governments of the regional municipalities, federal executive authorities in the field of state regulation of security and providing assistance to the population if necessary.

Le programme dispose de deux (02) organes : un Comité de Pilotage et une Unité de Coordination qui sont placés sous l'autorité du Premier Ministre, Chef du Gouvernement. Le comité de pilotage est responsable de la coordination et du suivi-évaluation de la mise en œuvre du programme spécial de reconstruction et de développement de la région de l'Extrême-Nord. Policy: Resolution No. 612 of the Cabinet of Ministers validating the Regulation on protection of forests.
Policy_Content: This Regulation defines the mechanism of implementation of a set of measures aimed at preserving forests from fires, illegal felling, damage, weakening and other harmful effects, protection from pests and diseases. It is mandatory for all forest owners, permanent and temporary forest users. Protection of forests from pests and diseases, preservation from weakening and other negative effects is ensured by systematic monitoring of the state of forests, timely detection of foci of pine, leaf, root-gnawing and trunk pests, fruit and seed pests, diseases of needles, leaves, fruits and seeds, trunk and root system, prevention of the occurrence of such foci, their localization and elimination. Observation and timely detection of foci of pests and diseases, weakening and other negative effects is carried out by: (a) pathological examinations; and (b) keeping record and inventory of centers of mass distribution of forest pests and diseases, consequences of accidents and natural disasters, other damage. Forest pathology surveys are carried out by permanent forest users, forest owners. Representatives of territorial bodies of the State Forestry Agency and state specialized forest protection enterprises may be involved in conducting a forest pathology survey. Conducting forest pathology surveys of forest plantations is carried out by visual inspection of the condition of forests and using geo-information technologies, geospatial data and methods of remote sensing of the earth. Forest pathology examinations are carried out: (a) in case of detection of pests and diseases; (b) in forest stands damaged by fires; (c) in forest plantations that are damaged by wind or snow, severe frost and other adverse weather phenomena or are under the influence of insufficient or excessive moisture; (d) in stands damaged by wild animals; and (e) in stands weakened by recreation, economic activity or man-made emissions. Record-keeping and inventory of foci of mass distribution of forest pests and diseases, consequences of accidents and natural disasters, other damages are carried out by permanent forest users, forest owners keeping a record book of forest pest and disease centers using information obtained from: (a) reports on the appearance of signs of deterioration in the sanitary condition of forest plantations; and (b) acts of forest pathology inspections of plantations.

Policy: Order No. 290 of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food validating the Instruction on the detection, localization and elimination of Anoplophora chinensis (Forster) and the pine stem nematode.
Policy_Content: This Instruction defines a complex of phytosanitary measures, which includes detection, localization and elimination of Anoplophora chinensis (Forster). This Instruction is mandatory for state phytosanitary inspectors, other officials of executive authorities and local governments. Detection of Anoplophora chinensis (Forster) is carried out by conducting inspection, examination, including sampling, phytosanitary examination (analyses), examination and/or monitoring in accordance with the legislation. Examination and/or monitoring to detect Anoplophora chinensis (Forster) is carried out in: (a) forest plantations; (b) gardening centers / nurseries; (c) parks; (d) gardens; (e) places of production, marking, and/or storage of wooden packaging material from host plants; (f) populated areas (trees along streets, roads, etc.); (g) places of phytosanitary control of regulated objects imported into Ukraine; and (h) other places where imported host plants may be stored or grown. Survey and/or monitoring on large areas of plantations is carried out along the running lines (clearings, forest roads, etc.), the distance between which can vary from 150 to 1,000 meters. In the absence of obvious signs of Anoplophora chinensis (Forster) activity, samples are taken in the form of wood fragments of the host plants from the above-ground part of the root or tree trunk (at a height of up to 70 cm above the soil surface). In the quarantine zone, the following phytosanitary measures are used to destroy Anoplophora chinensis (Forster): (a) felling of all host plants within a radius of 100 m around infected trees, including infected host plants and host plants with symptoms caused by Anoplophora chinensis (Forster), within the time limits specified in the decision on the introduction of the quarantine regime; (b) removal, visual inspection and destruction by incineration at processing plants or shredding of cut host plants, their stumps, roots; (c) prevention of any export of potentially contaminated material outside the quarantine zone; (d) clarification of the causes of the origin of the infection and tracking of the host plants associated with the occurrence of an outbreak (cell) of Anoplophora chinensis (Forster), followed by their examination for the presence of any signs specified in subparagraph 1 of paragraph 6 of section III of this Instruction; (e) prohibition of planting new host plants in the quarantine zone; and (f) annual monitoring of the presence of Anoplophora chinensis (Forster).

Policy: Resolution No. 8-T of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection validating norms and rules for the rational use and protection of subsoil.
Policy_Content: These norms and rules for the rational use and protection of subsoil establish uniform requirements for the classification of hydrocarbon reserves and projected resources. Hydrocarbon deposit (part thereof) is a natural accumulation of hydrocarbons, in terms of quality, quantity and conditions of their occurrence, suitable for industrial and other economic use. Hydrocarbon reserves and resources are classified based on the results of geological study, exploration of the subsoil separately for each deposit, taking into account their degree of exploration and economic significance. Based on the degree of exploration, hydrocarbon reserves are classified into categories A, B, C1, C2. Hydrocarbon reserves of categories A and B are the basis for preparing explored fields (parts thereof) for development and (or) the basis for their development. Hydrocarbon reserves of category C1 and category C2 are the basis for further work on the geological study of the subsoil at the field (part of it).

Policy: Decree No. 21/2022 approving the Regulation for Inland Water Fisheries (REPAI).
Policy_Content: This Decree approves the basic Regulation on Inland Fisheries (REPAI). The Regulation, consisting of 93 articles divided into nine Chapters and IX Annexes, specifies the requirements to be satisfied in order to perform inland fishing activities. REPAI aims to regulate Law No. 22/2013 of 1 November on the legal regime for fishing activities in continental or inland waters. The Regulation applies to: a) all national or foreign people, who carry out fishing in the inland waters of Mozambique, regardless of the fishing gear and means employees; b) fishing activities and related fishing operations carried out in inland waters; c) foreign fishing vessels sailing in the inland waters; d) fishing in inland waters carried out by Mozambican or foreign fishing vessels; and e) fishing by Mozambican fishing vessels, in the inland waters of third States, without prejudice to the legislation in force in those countries. REPAI extends to complementary fishing activities, namely ship-building and repair, fish processing, fish marketing, port services, manufacture of fishing gear and other accessories intended for fishing activities and related fishing operations.

Policy: Decreto N⁰ 236-22 – Reglamento Orgánico y Funcional del Ministerio de la Vivienda, Habitat y Edificaciones (MIVHED)
Policy_Content: El presente Reglamento tiene por objeto definir las competencias, funciones, estructura interna y organización del Ministerio de la Vivienda, Hábitat y Edificaciones (MIVHED), así como el nivel de autoridad e interrelación de sus funcionarios a nivel interno y con las entidades que le estén adscritas. Se establece la estructura orgánica y funcional del MIVHED. Se establecen las funciones del viceministerio, incluyendo elaborar propuestas para los procesos de formulación de las políticas y regulaciones sobre zonificación y uso adecuado del suelo, con el objetivo de presentarlos al Ministerio de Economía, Planificación y Desarrollo (MEPyD) para adelantar programas de vivienda en lo relativo a los procesos de construcción digna, sostenible y resiliente al cambio climático y a las coyunturas sociales y económicas del país, así como a la promoción del desarrollo de vivienda rural y a su articulación con los aspectos relativos al ordenamiento territorial y la correspondiente incorporación de amenazas y riesgo al desarrollo de proyectos de vivienda. También tienen de función, definir procesos de legalización, reubicación y saneamiento de la propiedad, según sea el estatus de propiedad de los suelos donde se localicen los asentamientos con problemas de propiedad. Se establecen las funciones de la Dirección de Obras de Salud, que incluye promover el uso de tecnologías apropiadas para minimizar los impactos negativos al aire, suelo y agua por afluentes líquidos, sólidos y gaseosos que procedan de las instalaciones de salud.

Policy: Regional Act no. 12 of 2022. Recognition and promotion of the Mediterranean diet.
Policy_Content: This Act, implementing articles 9 and 117 of the Constitution and the UNESCO Convention for the Protection of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, promotes the Mediterranean Diet as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, and enhances it through measures aimed at supporting the development of food and wine sectors characterised by the production and marketing of agricultural products with a short chain, in order to improve rural development and environmental sustainability. The Act concerns: respect and promotion of Sicilian cultural identity through the promotion of the Mediterranean Diet; promotion of Mediterranean Diet as a way to enhance geographical production areas; studies and research on the effects of the Mediterranean Diet on health and lifestyles; promotion of lifestyles based on the Mediterranean Diet as a model of proper nutrition and a prevention of nutrition-related social diseases; the spread of the use of products and specialties of the Mediterranean diet in canteens and in school-feeding; protection and sustainable management of natural, rural and historical landscapes, and the Mediterranean ecosystems; promotion of public-private partnerships in order to enhance the regional territory at national and international level.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. 106/22 on the Regulation for the Licensing of Waste Deposits of Low and Medium Levels of Radioactivity.
Policy_Content: This Presidential Decree establishes the Regulation for the Licensing of Waste Deposits of Low and Medium Levels of Radioactivity. The Regulation, consisting of 30 articles divided into five Chapters and two Annexes, lays down the general criteria and procedures for licensing initial, intermediate, provisional and final disposal of radioactive waste. These provisions do not inhibit legally authorized persons from exercising their responsibilities and performing necessary actions in order to provide the protection and safety of occupationally exposed workers, public health and the environment. Within the scope of the application of this Regulation, provisions on adoption, introduction, suspension, interruption or termination, design, construction, management and decommissioning of the deposit must be considered. The following deposits are exempt from licensing: a) Class 3 Radioactive Waste Deposits that are not stored in packages, but in the form of batteries, as is the case in ore-industrial installations; b) Class 6 Radioactive Waste Deposits; c) Class 2 Radioactive Waste Deposits, Radioactive Waste with a very short half-life, which are located in facilities where they are generated.

Policy: Ley N⁰ 2204 - Por la cual se crea el marco legal para el uso industrial y científico del cáñamo en Colombia y se dictan otras disposiciones.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley crea el marco legal para el uso de la fibra y el grano del cáñamo,  lo cual incluye el uso de semillas para siembra y cultivo destinadas a la producción de grano, semillas para siembra, plantas en estado vegetativo o componente vegetal, la comercialización, importación, exportación, adquisición a cualquier título, almacenamiento, transporte y disposición final de semillas. La presente ley no aplica ni regula aquello relacionado con los fines médicos de semillas ni regula los fines médicos, industriales, científicos o el uso adulto del cannabis y sus derivados.  El Ministerio de Justicia y del Derecho será competente para, evaluar las solicitudes y expedirlas autorizaciones para siembra y uso de la fibra y el grano del cáñamo, cuyo contenido de tetrahidrocannabinol (THC), incluyendo isómeros, sales y formas acidas, sea igual o menor al 0.3% o aquel porcentaje que disponga el Gobierno Nacional, y ejercer el seguimiento a quienes se les haya otorgado la autorización. Se regulan aspectos procesales para la obtención de la autorización. No podrán fabricarse productos de uso o consumo humano o animal de grano o componente vegetal de cáñamo que contengan un porcentaje de THC superior al establecido por el Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social. Se establecen normas sobre la sustitución voluntaria de cultivos de uso ilícito.

Policy: Resolution No. 556 of the Cabinet of Ministers on some issues of submitting a waste declaration.
Policy_Content: This Resolution establishes the procedure for submitting a waste declaration and validates the form of waste declaration. It shall be applicable to economic entities in the field of waste management, whose activities lead exclusively to the generation of waste, for which the indicator of total generation of waste is from 50 to 1000 conditional units. The declaration is submitted by the applicant once a year by February 20 of the year following the reporting year, in electronic form through the Unified State Web Portal of Electronic Services by filling in the established form. The declaration is submitted by the applicant who has been authenticated using an integrated electronic identification system, an electronic signature or other means of electronic identification that enable unambiguous identification of the person. The applicant cannot submit a declaration if it is not filled out in full. The information entered by the applicant during the formation of the declaration is subject to analysis for its completeness, compliance with the format, logic and reliability. Analysis of the completeness of submitted/entered data is carried out by checking the completion of all mandatory fields of the declaration form. The analysis of the submitted/entered data for their compliance with the format is carried out by checking the compliance of the submitted/entered data with the structure requirements established for the corresponding field of the declaration form. The analysis of submitted/entered data for their logic is carried out by checking submitted/entered data on the correctness of arithmetic calculations.

Policy_Content: This Regulation determine the procedure for creating and maintaining the state register of objects that have a negative impact on the environment. The State Register is a state information system, the creation of which is carried out by the Federal Service for Supervision of Natural Resources in accordance with the Federal Law "On Environmental Protection", the legislation of the Russian Federation on data, information technologies and information protection and other regulatory legal acts of the Russian Federation. The state register consists of: (a) the federal state register; and (b) regional state registries. The Federal Service for Supervision of Natural Resources is the operator of the state register and performs the following functions: (a) provides technical support for the functioning of the state register; (b) determines the electronic format of the data (information) contained in the state register; (c) ensures the interaction of the state register with other state information systems; (d) ensures the assignment of codes to objects in the state register; (e) enters into the federal state register information obtained as a result of the performance of state functions and the provision of state services in the field of established competence; (f) organizes information and methodological support for the maintenance by the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation, executive authorities of the subjects of the Russian Federation of the federal state register and regional state registers (including the assignment of a category to an object depending on the level of negative impact on the environment) and their support on technical issues; (g) provides the Ministry of Natural Resources and Ecology of the Russian Federation, as well as the executive authorities of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation, according to their competence, with access to information about objects contained in the state register for the purpose of information support for management and regulatory legal regulation of activities in the field of environmental protection; and (h) monitors the maintenance of regional state registers by the executive authorities of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation.

Policy: Environment Act No. 18 of 2021.
Policy_Content: The objectives of this Act are: (I) to communicate, educate and raise public awareness on the environment and natural resources protection, conservation, management and sustainable use at all levels of society; (II) to provide for and establish integrated systems and environment safeguard system of development control, environmental impact assessment and pollution control; (III) to prevent, control, manage and monitor waste and pollution; (IV) to reduce risks and prevent the degradation of the environment by all practical means, including (i) regulating the discharge of pollutants to the air, water or land; (ii) regulating the import, export, manufacture, use, transport, collection, treatment, storage and disposal of chemicals and wastes; (iii) promoting recycling, re-use, reduction, composting and recovery of materials in an economically viable manner; (iv) protecting, conserving and managing the natural resources threatened by natural and human induced activities, particularly those resources of national and ecological significance as may be classified under the categories of terrestrial vegetation, coral, fish and marine life; (V) to promote and undertake ecosystem approach to protect, conserve, manage sustain and enhance the resilience of the environment; (VI) to comply with and give effect to regional and international conventions and obligations relating to the environment; (VII) to collect, provide, and manage environment data and information for the state of environment report and national report obligations to international conventions relating to the environment; (VIII) to enhance the sustainability, integrity and resilience of the Kiribati environment; (IX) to promote, ensure and support sustainable development; (X) to promote, protect, conserve, manage, and sustainably use of biological diversity and heritage; (XI) to prevent, eradicate, reduce, and manage the impacts of invasive alien species for the protection and conservation of terrestrial and marine biological diversity; and (XII) to enforce and ensure compliance. This Act applies throughout Kiribati islands/land; throughout Kiribati and Kiribati waters; and throughout the exclusive economic zone of Kiribati.

Policy_Content: The sources for setting up the Forest Land Improvement Fund are the following: (a) the equivalent value of the forest ecosystem services provided by maintaining the forest protection functions, which are paid by the direct or indirect beneficiaries of the forest ecosystem services; (b) the amount to be paid in the case of areas smaller than 50 sq m, permanently withdrawn from the national forest fund without compensation; (c) the deposited guarantee and the afferent bank interest; (d) the fee for the final removal of the land from the forest fund; (e) the guarantee for the temporary occupation of the land from the forest fund; (f) the tax equivalent to the tax of definitive withdrawal from the national forest fund, which is paid for the change of the category of forestry use of the land with forestry destination from the use of “forest” to another forestry use; (g) the amounts that represent the value of the unrealized forest functions; (h) the equivalent value of the surplus of detention by seizure/expropriation  (RMU); (i) the amounts that are determined as compensations for damages in forests or in the forest vegetation for which the forest administration/services are not insured; (j) the amount due as compensation for lack of use, in case of non-return of land at the deadline provided in the approval act, calculated according to the specific methodology, until the date of resumption of land in the national forest fund or obtaining a new approval; (k) the amount received from the sale of confiscated timber from the state-owned forest fund, remaining after deducting the costs of custody, auction organization and transport, as the case may be, as well as the amount received from the payment of confiscated timber related to the publicly owned forest fund to the state that cannot be found or that cannot be identified; and (l) interest received on cash, on deposits consisting of income collected from the achievements of the activity related to the provision of forest ecosystem services.

Policy: Agriculture and Agro-processing Master Plan "Social Compact".
Policy_Content: This Agriculture and Agro-processing Master Plan, relying on the full commitment and active participation of stakeholders of agricultural sector, represents a collective social compacting attempt to restructure the South African economy and address the challenges of slow growth, social inequality, unemployment and food security. Policy: Governmental Decree No. 790 validating the Regulation on creating and maintaining a register of carbon units, as well as conducting operations with carbon units in the register of carbon units.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the procedure creating and maintaining a register of carbon units, as well as conducting operations with carbon units in the register of carbon units. The register is an information system that registers climate projects and keeps records of carbon units and operations with carbon units provided for by the legislation of the Russian Federation and international treaties of the Russian Federation. The operator conducts operations in the register after the conclusion of the contract. Information is entered into the register in Russian. The operator, within the framework of maintaining the register, performs the following operations: (a) registration of a climate project; (b) change of information (data) about the climate project and (or) about the participant in the circulation of carbon units; (c) opening and closing of an account in the registry; (d) operations on an account in the register; (e) release into circulation of carbon units; and (f) other operations in accordance with the requirements of the legislation of the Russian Federation in the field of limiting greenhouse gas emissions, international treaties of the Russian Federation and the contract. The register must contain the following information: (a) information about the contractor of the climate project and its other participants, including investors, contractors; (a) individual climate project number; (b) the name of the climate project; (c) place of implementation of the climate project; (d) date of commencement and timing of the implementation of the climate project (including information on the expected (actual) date of commencement and planned date of completion of the implementation of the climate project, as well as information on the period during which the implementation of the climate project results in the reduction (prevention) of greenhouse gas emissions and (or) an increase in their absorption); (e) information on a positive conclusion on the compliance of the project with the criteria for classifying projects implemented by legal entities, individual entrepreneurs or individuals as climate projects; (f) information about the goals, objectives and category of the climate project (reduction (prevention) of greenhouse gas emissions and (or) increase in their absorption); (g) information about the sectoral affiliation of the climate project (in accordance with the All-Russian Classification of Economic Activities); (h) a list of objects of economic and other activities, the operation of which is accompanied by emissions of greenhouse gases and (or) their absorption; (i) description and justification of the scenario of emissions and absorption of greenhouse gases in the absence of a climate project and the scenario of emissions and absorption of greenhouse gases, subject to the implementation of the climate project; (j) a method for quantifying the reduction (prevention) of greenhouse gas emissions and (or) an increase in their absorption and a plan for the implementation of appropriate monitoring; (k) information on the planned amount of reduction (prevention) of greenhouse gas emissions and (or) increase in their absorption as a result of the implementation of the climate project; (l) information on the number of carbon units to be released into circulation when registering a climate project in accordance with paragraphs 34 and 35 of this Regulation; (m) information on the implementation of the climate project (current status); (n) information about the accredited person; (o) information on the total number of carbon units in circulation under the climate project; and (p) information on the assignment of information on the climate project with the status "archived" in relation to the record on the climate project in case of termination of the contract with the contractor of this project, indicating the date and reason for termination of the contract.

Policy: Regional Law No. 21-rz “"On measures of state support for the development of personal subsidiary smallholdings in the Republic of Ingushetia".
Policy_Content: This Regional Law establishes the measures of state support of personal subsidiary smallholdings in order to increase employment and improvement of income of the rural population, assistance to the development of food market, and establishes the powers of the regional state bodies in the field of state support of personal smallholdings. Personal smallholdings shall be conducted by citizens and persons living with him, family members for meeting personal needs on land plot allotted or purchased for conducting personal subsidiary smallholding. Policy: ORDER No. 74 of the National Commission for the Control of Nuclear Activities subordinated to the Government validating the Basic Rules for the safe management of radioactive waste and spent nuclear fuel.
Policy_Content: These Basic Rules establish the procedure for the safe management of radioactive waste and spent nuclear fuel. They set forth the general principles and requirements regarding the application of the safe management of radioactive waste, including spent nuclear fuel, regarding the safe conduct, regulation, authorization and control of nuclear activities. The field of application: (a) all stages of spent nuclear fuel management, when it results from activities carried out exclusively for peaceful purposes; and (b) to all stages of radioactive waste management, from generation to final storage, when they result from activities carried out exclusively for peaceful purposes. These Basic Rules apply both to radioactive waste and orphan sources resulting from current or past practices, as well as to radioactive waste resulting from an intervention in the event of a nuclear accident and also in the case of activities related to the management of radioactive waste that present additional dangers: chemical, biological, pyrophoric, flammable. The objective of the safe management of radioactive waste and spent nuclear fuel is to protect human health and the environment, both now and in the future, without undue transfer of responsibility to future generations. The authorization holder must manage radioactive waste and spent nuclear fuel in such a way as to comply with the following principles: (1) protection of the health of the population; (2) environmental protection; (3) protection beyond national borders; (4) protection of future generations; (5) avoiding the imposition of unnecessary burdens on future generations; (6) the existence of the national legislative framework; (7) control of the generation of radioactive waste; (8) the interdependencies related to the generation and management of radioactive waste and spent nuclear fuel; (9) maintaining the security of the installations; and (10) polluter pays.

Policy: Balochistan Forest Act, 2022 (Act No. VI of 2022).
Policy_Content: The Act consolidate and amend the laws relating to protection, conservation, management and sustainable development of forests, rangelands and other renewable natural resources in the Balochistan Province. The Act describes the power of government to make the whole or any part of the forest-land or waste-land as reserved forest. In case of existence of any objection to constitute any land as reserved forest, a forest settlement board shall treat the claim. In Chapter two the Act outlines the power of government for nominating any forest-land or waste-land as protected forest, and power to close forests and prohibit certain acts and to make rules for the protected forests. The Act further describes the orders that government can make for protection of forests such as prohibiting or regulating the breaking up or clearing of land for cultivation; the pasturing of cattle; or the firing or clearing of the vegetation. The text further provides for the manner on declaration of community forest reserve, management conditions, joint management by local organisations, and prohibited acts. The Act provides as well on constitution of the forest force and the scope of its power and duties.

Policy: Law “On cooperatives.”
Policy_Content: The objective of this Law is to regulate relations regarding the creation of a cooperative, membership, management, organization, assets, control, and termination of operations. It shall be applicable to all cooperatives except for those performing savings and credit operations. The cooperative shall adhere to the following principles in its activities: (a) to have voluntary membership without discrimination based on race, ethnicity, language, race, age, gender, social origin, status, wealth, occupation, religion, opinion, or education; (b) to be independent entity; (c) to have democratic management, collective control, transparency and openness of cooperative members; (d) to ensure equal economic participation of cooperative members and fair distribution; (e) to provide cooperative members and employees with training and information aimed at supporting cooperative development; (f) to support interaction between cooperatives; and (g) to respect the common interests of cooperative members. The founders of the cooperative shall enter into an agreement on the establishment of the cooperative, and the purpose of the cooperative, the amount of capital to be contributed by the founders, rights, duties, and responsibilities shall be included in the agreement. The founders of the cooperative shall enter into an agreement on the establishment of the cooperative, and the purpose of the cooperative, the amount of capital to be contributed by the founders, rights, duties, and responsibilities shall be included in the agreement. The founding agreement shall be terminated upon registration of the cooperative in the state register. The founder of the cooperative shall be registered in the State Register within 30 days of the decision on the establishment of the cooperative. The association of cooperatives is a non-governmental organization serving its members.

Policy: Law on the use of renewable energy sources.
Policy_Content: This Law regulates the use of energy from renewable sources, goals of using energy from renewable sources, methods for determining the share of renewable energy sources in gross final energy consumption, integration of energy from renewable sources into the market, incentive systems for electricity production from renewable sources, guarantees of origin electricity, production of electricity from renewable sources for own consumption, use of renewable energy sources in the field of heat and transport, special procedures related to the construction and connection of energy facilities using renewable energy sources, basics of cooperation mechanisms with other countries in the field renewable energy sources, supervision over the implementation of provisions here adopted, as well as other issues of importance for renewable energy sources. The use of energy from renewable sources is in the public interest of the Republic of Serbia and is of special importance for the Republic of Serbia. Regulation of the use of energy from renewable sources includes measures and activities taken to achieve long-term goals, as follows: 1) reducing the use of fossil fuels and increasing the use of renewable energy sources in order to protect the environment; 2) long-term reduction of dependence on energy imports; 3) creation of new jobs and development of entrepreneurship in the field of renewable energy sources; 4) encouraging research, innovation and competitiveness in the field of renewable energy sources; 5) digitalization, simplicity, economy and efficiency of procedures in the field of renewable energy sources; 6) integration of electricity from renewable sources into the electricity market, which includes the exposure of electricity producers to changes in market prices of electricity in order to maximize their market revenues; 7) ensuring the stability of the electricity market, taking into account the costs of integrating renewable energy sources into the system and the stability of the network; 8) regional development related to the use of renewable energy sources; 9) stability of the system of incentives and application of operational state aid in the form of market premium, except for small plants and demonstration projects; 10) awarding incentives through auctions in a public, transparent, competitive and economical manner, without discrimination which ensures a high level of project implementation, except in the case of small plants and demonstration projects when incentives do not have to be awarded through auctions; 11) sustainable and independent development through the maximum use of national scientific-research, technological-development and human capacities in the process of planning to increase the use of renewable energy sources. Power plants that use renewable energy sources are considered to be: 1) hydroelectric power plant; 2) biomass power plant; 3) biogas power plant; 4) wind farm; 5) solar power plant; 6) geothermal power plant; 7) biodegradable waste power plant; 8) landfill gas power plant; 9) gas power plant from a municipal wastewater treatment plant; 10) power plant that uses other renewable energy sources. A reversible hydropower plant is not considered a power plant that uses renewable energy sources. The Government may, at the proposal of the Ministry responsible for mining and energy, with previously obtained opinion of the Ministry responsible for environmental protection, allow works and activities, i.e. projects on construction of a hydropower plant, if it is a project of public and general interest, or projects of special or national importance for the Republic of Serbia. The construction of hydroelectric power plants in protected areas is generally prohibited.

Policy: Decreto Supremo Nº 4701 - Crea la Empresa Pública Nacional Estratégica denominada Empresa Boliviana de Producción Agropecuaria.

Policy: Decree on conditions of delivery and supply of natural gas.
Policy_Content: This Decree, based on the provisions of the Serbian Law on energy, prescribes the conditions of delivery and supply of natural gas to customers, as well as measures that shall be taken in the event that the safety of natural gas delivery to customers is threatened due to disruptions in the operation of the transport or distribution system or disruptions in the market, namely: 1) conditions and method of granting approval for connecting to the system and connecting the system; 2) place of measurement and place of delimitation of responsibility for delivered natural gas; 3) conditions and method of connection of facilities of a temporary nature, construction sites and facilities in trial operation and other facilities in accordance with the law governing the construction of facilities; 4) measures taken in case of short-term disruptions due to breakdowns and other unforeseen situations that threaten the operational safety of the transport or distribution system, as well as due to unforeseen and necessary maintenance work on energy facilities or necessary work on expanding the system; 5) measures taken in the event of a general shortage, the conditions and manner of taking measures and the sequence of natural gas delivery restrictions, as well as measures of savings and rational consumption in the event of a general shortage of natural gas; 6) conditions and method of suspension of natural gas supply; 7) conditions and method of rational consumption and saving of natural gas; 8) conditions of supply to customers' facilities, which cannot suspend the delivery of natural gas due to unpaid obligations for delivered natural gas or in other cases; 9) the way of regulating mutual relations between the supplier, the system operator and the final customer to whom the delivery of natural gas cannot be suspended; 10) conditions and method of measurement of delivered natural gas; 11) range of quality, chemical composition and other properties of natural gas that is taken into the system and delivered from the system; 12) method of calculation of unauthorized taken natural gas; 13) the procedure, method and deadlines for exercising the end customer's right to compensation due to deviation from the prescribed quality of delivery, i.e. supply of natural gas; 14) method of notifying the end customer; 15) conditions and measures for supplying customers with natural gas; 16) accounting period and mandatory content of invoices for payment of delivered natural gas; 17) content of the plan and deadlines for taking over measuring devices; 18) other issues in accordance with the above mentioned law regulating the energy sector.
Subject: Energy

Policy: Regional Decree No. 176-P validating the Regulation on natural park of regional significance "South-Kamchatsky".

The natural park is a national patrimony and included in the register of UNESCO World Natural Heritage Sites as part of the nomination “Volcanoes of Kamchatyush”. The main objectives of the creation of the Natural Park are: (a) preservation of integrity, natural state, restoration of disturbed natural objects and complexes as part of the World natural heritage of UNESCO; (b) preservation of typical, rare, unique and reference natural historical and cultural complexes and objects, biological diversity of southeastern part of the Kamchatka Peninsula, including conservation in natural state of natural ecological systems, their environment-forming functions and biological productivity, including the preservation of unique coastal Pacific ecosystems, thermal and mineral springs, boreal deciduous (stone-birch) forests, humistratous forest, subalpine meadows, alpine tundra, volcanic plateau, spawning rivers and lakes, formed under the influence of modern volcanism, glaciation, post-volcanic processes, active cyclonic activity, other geological and climatic processes and phenomena; (с) creating conditions for expanding the economic base of Yelizovsky and Ust-Bolsheretsky municipal districts through infrastructure development of regulated tourism and recreation (including mass tourism), development of balneology in accordance with the established recreational capacity of individual natural complexes and objects of the Natural Park; (d) implementation of state environmental monitoring; and (e)  environmental education of the population. The natural park was created without limitation of its term of functioning.

Actual air pollution is considered to be the case when, as a result of emergency situations and/or during martial law, an unorganized release of polluting substances or mixtures of such substances is carried out from the emission source into the atmospheric air. The facts of the unorganized emission of pollutants or mixtures of such substances into the atmospheric air, as well as their scale, are established by authorized persons who exercise state supervision (control) in the field of environmental protection, in particular, but not exclusively, by inspection of the place of the event, the data of remote sensing of the earth, laboratory studies of atmospheric air, processing of the conclusions of any examinations, explanations, references, documents, materials, information received from any sources, operational messages of natural persons and legal entities, etc. This Methodology contains formulas for the calculation of the mass of unorganized emissions of polluting substances or mixtures of such substances into the atmospheric air.

Policy: Law No. HO-84-N “On mercury”.
Policy_Content: This Law regulates the relations related to the use of mercury, mercury compounds, mercury waste and mercury-based compounding materials in the Republic of Armenia, the purpose of which is to protect human health and the environment from man-made emissions of mercury and mercury compounds. This Law shall not be applicable to: (a) laboratory tests; and (b) natural traces of mercury compounds present in ores. The responsibilities of the Government in the field of ensuring ecologically safe conditions for the management of mercury, mercury compounds, mercury wastes and mercury compounding materials are: (a) defining the list of substances with mercury compounding materials prohibited for export from the Republic of Armenia and for import into the Republic of Armenia; (b) defining the procedure for mercury export from the Republic of Armenia; (c) defining the procedure for mercury import to the Republic of Armenia; and (d) assessment of areas contaminated with mercury and mercury compounding materials. Import of mercury to the Republic of Armenia is allowed only in case of having a one-time license issued by the authorized body. In the Republic of Armenia, the manufacturing of the following commodities with mercury compounding materials is prohibited: (a) batteries; (b) circuit breakers and relays; (c) small fluorescent lamps for general lighting of 30 W or less, with a mercury content exceeding 5 mg per lamp burner; (d) tubular fluorescent lamps for general lighting; and (e) cosmetics with a mercury content. This Law contains IV Chapters divided into 12 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II regards trade of mercury containing commodities. Chapter III regards import and export of mercury containing commodities. Chapter IV contains final and transitional provisions.
