Policy: Bangladesh Patent Act, 2022 (Act No. 05 of 2022).
Policy_Content: This Act aims to legislate separately on patent matters by repealing the patent provisions of the Patents And Designs Act, 1911. Any technological product or process invention shall be patentable if it contains novelty and innovative step and is applicable in industry. Novelty shall be deemed to exist in an invention, if it is not conceivable by a known prior. An invention shall be deemed to contain an inventive step if it indicates a substantial technological advance of knowledge, which is beyond the scope of the existing knowledge or prior art and the claimed invention is not clearly apparent to a person skilled in that particular technology. Any work which can be applied or used in industry shall be deemed to be an invention. he patent interests or rights of the inventor shall be reserved. If two or more persons jointly make an invention, such persons shall be jointly entitled to the patent. If two or more persons independently make the same invention, the person who applies for the patent first shall be entitled to the patent and in case of priority claim , the priority date shall be deemed to be the date of patent application. Patent rights shall be assignable or transferable.

Policy: Ley 7/2022, de 8 de abril, de residuos y suelos contaminados para una economía circular.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley tiene por objeto regular el régimen jurídico aplicable a la puesta en el mercado de productos en relación con el impacto en la gestión de sus residuos, así como el régimen jurídico de la prevención, producción y gestión de residuos, incluyendo el establecimiento de instrumentos económicos aplicables en este ámbito, y el régimen jurídico aplicable a los suelos contaminados. Tiene por finalidad la prevención y la reducción de la generación de residuos y de los impactos adversos de su generación y gestión, la reducción del impacto global del uso de los recursos y la mejora de la eficiencia de dicho uso con el objeto de, en última instancia, proteger el medio ambiente y la salud humana y efectuar la transición a una economía circular y baja en carbono con modelos empresariales, productos y materiales innovadores y sostenibles para garantizar el funcionamiento eficiente del mercado interior y la competitividad de España a largo plazo. Asimismo, esta ley tiene por finalidad prevenir y reducir el impacto de determinados productos de plástico en la salud humana y en el medio ambiente, con especial atención al medio acuático. Se contribuye así al cumplimiento de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible, incluidos en la Agenda 2030 y en particular a los objetivos 12 –producción y consumo sostenibles–, 13 –acción por el clima- y 14 –vida submarina–. Asimismo, en el ámbito de su contribución a la lucha contra el cambio climático, esta ley es coherente con la planificación en materia de energía y clima. Entre otras cuestiones, se refuerza la aplicación del principio de jerarquía mediante la obligatoriedad del uso de instrumentos económicos, se fortalece la prevención de residuos incluyendo medidas para contribuir a los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible relativos al desperdicio alimentario y a las basuras marinas, se incrementan a medio y largo plazo los objetivos de preparación para la reutilización y reciclado de los residuos municipales y se establece la obligatoriedad de nuevas recogidas separadas, entre otros, para los biorresiduos, los residuos textiles y los residuos domésticos peligrosos.

Policy: Resolution No. 35/2022 approving the Strategic Plan of the Technological Park for the year 2021 to 2030.
Policy_Content: This Resolution approves the Strategic Plan of the Technological Park for the year 2021 to 2030. The Strategic Plan for Sustainable Development (PEDS) proposes to transform Cape Verde into a “platform country”, capable of growing a “circulation economy”, open to the world and fully inserted in the World Economic System (SEM). Information and communication technologies (ICT) constitute an opportunity for the sustainable economic and social development of the country. The Technological Park was designed and implemented to be the centre of Cape Verde's entire digital strategy, bringing together the interests of the sectors and enhancing competitive advantages in the creation of the Market–Companies–Employment-Training ecosystem. The Technological Park, with hubs in Praia and Mindelo includes the construction of business, training and certification centres, administrative buildings, auditorium, data centre, etc. The Technological Park aims to capture the interest of the regional and international market and foreign investment in order to contribute to its growth, consolidation, international credibility and to speed up the transfer of knowledge to the country.

Policy: Resolution No. 37/2022 creating the Technical Team for the preparation of the National Inventory of Greenhouse Gases (GHG).
Policy_Content: This Resolution creates the Technical Team for the preparation of the National Inventory of Greenhouse Gases (GHG). As part of the ratification of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) on 29 March 1995, and within the framework of the specific obligations established by article 4 of the aforementioned Convention, Cape Verde undertakes to prepare, update and publish a national inventory of anthropogenic emissions by sources and removal by sinks of Greenhouse Gases (GHG) not controlled by the Montreal Protocol. The National GHG Inventory is a transparency mechanism and its results also allow subsidizing action plans to reduce the emission of greenhouse gases. The Technical Team has the mission of supporting in updating the national GHG inventories, as well as supporting the preparation of biannual reports on GHGs and National Communications on Climate Change.

Policy: Decree on the protection of traditional and old crafts.
Policy_Content: This Decree, adopted by the government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, determines the list of traditional and old crafts and the conditions for their performance. The list of traditional and old crafts by types, which can be performed in accordance with the Law on the classification of activities in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina is attached to this text. To perform traditional and old trades, it is necessary to have a secondary school education of the third or fourth level or a school education of a higher level than prescribed. If a special regulation, depending on the activity, prescribes at least elementary school, appropriate vocational training, or additional conditions for performing the activity, these conditions must be met. Craftsmen who perform traditional and old trades may take a master's exam in front of a commission established by a secondary vocational school or adult education institution, which has been verified for these jobs in accordance with current regulations from the field of upbringing and education, in cooperation with the Canton Chamber of Crafts. Exceptionally, craftsmen who have been granted permission to perform traditional and old trades before the date of entry into force of the text, may continue to perform their trades, even though they do not meet the required school education requirement.

Policy: Regional Law No. 57-PK “On regional green areas”.
Policy_Content: This Regional Law, in accordance with the Constitution of the Russian Federation, the legislation of the Russian Federation and the Perm Territory in the field of environmental protection regulates relations in the field of conservation and development of the regional green areas within the boundaries of the cities of the regional and province significance with a population of at least 20,000 people and growing in these territories green plantations, with the exception of protected areas and areas covered by forests. It is aimed at the implementation of the constitutional right of citizens to a favorable environment. Green areas shall be intended land plots or parts thereof, on which green plantations grow (with the exception of territories of forests and protected areas), as well as territories with natural and (or) artificially created landscape gardening complexes (objects). Green spaces shall be intended tree-shrub and herbaceous vegetation of natural and artificial origin, as well as free-standing trees and shrubs, not classified as forest plantations, creating a favorable natural environment in municipal units of the Perm Territory. The following categories of green areas are located on the regional territory: (a) common use of the territory used by the population for recreational purposes (parks, gardens, squares, boulevards, alleys, embankments); (b) territories of limited use  within the residential, civil, industrial buildings, as well as occupied by objects of health and public services, science, education, and used by the population; (c) special purpose green areas -  territories within the boundaries of sanitary protection zones, protective and reclamation zones, cemeteries, along automobile roads and railways, as well as nurseries, flower and greenhouse farms, formed by the owners (users) of objects in accordance with the legislation of the Russian Federation and the regional legislation; and (d) natural and recreational territories - territories of river valleys, water protection zones, as well as spontaneously formed landscaped territories not included in other categories of green areas. The main directions of environmental protection in the field of conservation and development of the regional green areas include: (a) protection of green areas and green spaces; (b) gardening of territories, reproduction of green spaces; (c) compensatory landscaping and compensation for damage caused to environment by demolition, damage, destruction of green spaces; (d) registration of green areas and inventory of green spaces in green areas; and (e) information of the population on issues of conservation and development of green areas.

Policy: Order No. 244 of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Ecology validating the Rules for extinguishing forest fires.
Policy_Content: These Rules are established for the purpose of: (a) organization of management of work to extinguish forest fires; (b) prevention and elimination of emergency situations in forests, resulting from forest fires; (c) organization of interdepartmental interaction in the performance of work to extinguish forest fires. Works to extinguish forest fires are carried out by state (municipal) institutions subordinate to federal executive authorities, executive authorities of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation, local self-government bodies, within the powers of the indicated bodies, and other organizations in conformity with Forest Code. When extinguishing forest fires, the coordination of all forces and means of extinguishing forest fires are assigned to the Federal Forestry Agency, which sets up federal headquarters to coordinate firefighting activities related to the extinguishment of forest fires, as well as the corresponding headquarters in the federal districts. Instructions of the federal headquarters, as well as the corresponding headquarters in the federal districts for the coordination of activities to extinguish forest fires, issued within its competence, are binding. In order to establish the regime and methods of extinguishing forest fires, the territories in which forests are located are divided into areas of application of aviation forces and firefighting equipment and ground forces and firefighting equipment. Areas of application of aviation forces and fire extinguishing equipment are installed in forests located in hard-to-reach and remote areas with underdeveloped or non-existent road networks, where arrival of ground forces and firefighting equipment within 3 hours from the moment the forest fire was discovered is impossible. In the area of application of aviation forces and fire extinguishing equipment in forests located on hard-to-reach and remote territories, forest fires control zones can be established. Forest fire control zones on the forest fund land are established by executive authorities of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation, authorized in the field of forest relations, in the area of performance of forest aviation works in forests located on hard-to-reach and (or) remote territories in agreement with the authorized federal executive body. When allocating forest fire control zones, it is not allowed to include in them forest plots allotted for lease or permanent (open-ended) use or planned for use in accordance with the forest plan of the subject of the Russian Federation for the following types of forest use, as well as protected areas. The aforesaid uses of forests include: (a) timber harvesting; (b) performance of research activities, educational activities; (c) performance of recreational activities; (d) creation of forest plantations and their exploitation; (e) geological study of the subsoil, exploration and extraction of fossils; (f) construction, reconstruction, operation of linear facilities; and (g) creation and operation of timber processing infrastructure facilities. Areas of application of ground forces and fire extinguishing equipment are installed in forests located in areas with developed road network, on which the arrival of ground forces and fire extinguishing equipment is possible within 3 hours from the discovery of a forest fire, regardless of weather conditions. Boundaries of the territory where forest firefighting operations are carried out, are installed at a distance of at least 500 meters from active (localized) forest fire edge and (or) created (planned to be created) mineralized belts, reference lines from which backburning is carried out, the lines at which the stop is made (planned) against spread and localization of the fire. In the forest fire control zone for which a decision has been made on the termination, suspension of work on extinguishing forest fires, is established observation by aviation and (or) space means. Data on the main characteristics of such fires (area, shape, daily dynamics of development) are subject to mandatory accounting (registration) with daily reflection of the specified data in official reporting materials and reports provided by a specialized dispatch service of executive authority of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation in specialized dispatch service of the Federal Forestry Agency. A forest fire survey is carried out using ground, aviation (manned and (or) unmanned aircraft) means, unmanned aerial vehicles and (or) space vehicles for the purpose of assessment of: (a) the type and speed of the spread of the fire, control thereof) and the approximate area; (b) main types of combustible materials; (c) tactical parts of the fire (front, flanks and rear); (d) the most dangerous direction of fire spread (creating a risk to valuable forest plantations and (or) plantations in which is possible the transition from ground fire to crown fire, economic facilities and settlements; (e) the presence of natural and artificial obstacles to the spread of fire; (f) possible strengthening or weakening of the fire due to the characteristics of forest areas and terrain on the path of its distribution, as well as due to changes in the meteorological situation; (g) the possibility of approaching, approaching the edge of the fire and using mechanized fire localization and extinguishing means; (h) availability of water supply sources and the possibility of their use; (i) the presence of support strips for backburning and possibility of laying mineralized bands; (j) safe parking places for vehicles, location of people; and (k) escape routes for persons performing fire extinguishing, in case of the danger of increased fire, possible places of shelter.

El título I contempla medidas en el ámbito energético y se estructura en 7 capítulos. En particular, el capítulo  III  recoge  medidas  para  la  agilización  de  los  proyectos  de  energías renovables  con  la  finalidad  de  acelerar  la  descarbonización  y  reducir  la  dependencia energética. El título III, de apoyo al tejido económico y empresarial, se compone de 4 capítulos, que  contienen,  respectivamente,  medidas  para  reforzar  la  liquidez  de  empresas  y autónomos, para mitigar el incremento de costes en el tejido empresarial de actividades críticas del sector primario, y para apoyar al sector agrario, ganadero y pesquero. Policy: Resolution No. 4-T of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection validating norms and rules for the rational use and protection of subsoil.
Policy_Content: This Resolution validates norms and rules “Environmental protection. Subsoil. Classification of deposits and forecasted resources of solid combustibles, ore, non-metallic minerals”, which establish uniform requirements for the classification of reserves and forecast resources of solid combustibles, ore, non-metallic minerals. Mineral reserves are classified according to the results of the geological exploration of the subsoil, for each type of minerals, taking into account their degree of exploration and economic significance. According to the degree of exploration, mineral reserves are classified into categories A, B, C1, C2. Mineral reserves of categories A, B are the basis for the preparation of explored deposits (their parts) of the first complexity group and deposits (their parts) of the second complexity group for development and (or) the basis for their development. Category C1 mineral reserves are the basis for the preparation of explored deposits (their parts) of the third complexity group and deposits (their parts) of the fourth complexity group for development and the basis for their development. Mineral reserves of category C2 are the basis for setting further work on the geological study of the subsoil at the field (its part).

Policy_Content: Le présent décret annonce la création d’une unité de gestion par objectifs pour la réalisation du projet de « développement agricole intégré à Joumine, Ghezala et Sejnane (phase 2) » et qui est placée sous l’autorité du ministre de l’agriculture, des ressources hydrauliques et de la pêche maritime. Ce décret précise qu’une commission au sein du ministère de l'agriculture est créée et présidée par le ministre qui est chargée du suivi et de l'évaluation des missions attribuées à l'unité de gestion par objectifs conformément aux critères fixés à l'article 4 du présent décret présidentiel et détermine son fonctionnement.

Policy: Governmental Decree No. 455 validating the Rules for verifying the results of the implementation of climate projects.
Policy_Content: These Rules establish the procedure for verifying the results of the implementation of climate projects. The subject of verification is the verification and confirmation of information on the reduction (prevention) of greenhouse gas emissions or the increase in the absorption of greenhouse gases as a result of the implementation of the climate project, which are contained in the report on the implementation of the climate project. The report on the implementation of the climate project is prepared in the form established by the Ministry of Economic Development of the Russian Federation. Verification is carried out by a legal entity or an individual entrepreneur accredited in the national accreditation system as a body for the validation and verification of greenhouse gases and is not affiliated with the climate project executor or another person with whom the climate project executor has concluded an agreement on preparation of a report on the implementation of the climate project. The basis for verification is a verification contract concluded between the verification body and the climate project contractor or another person. The term for the implementation of verification, the term for submitting the verification report to the verification customer, and the obligations of the parties are established by the agreement.

Policy: Resolución Nº 99/2022 - Reglamento para la gestión y disposición final de la basura de los buques en las aguas interiores, puertos y bahías, aguas jurisdiccionales y en la zona económica exclusiva de la República de Cuba.
Policy_Content: El presente Reglamento tiene el objeto de establecer los procedimientos y normas operacionales que garanticen cumplir con los requerimientos fundamentales para prevenir la contaminación de las aguas cubanas por la basura de los buques, en correspondencia con las Directrices establecidas en el Anexo V revisado (Reglas para prevenir la contaminación por las basuras de los buques) del Convenio Internacional para Prevenir la Contaminación por los Buques, en lo adelante, Convenio MARPOL. El Reglamento es de aplicación a todos los buques de pabellón nacional o extranjero que operen en las aguas jurisdiccionales de la República de Cuba. El Reglamento no se aplica específicamente a las aguas grises, de sentina u otras descargas similares que son esenciales para la explotación del buque. Otras descargas similares esenciales para la explotación del buque estan contempladas en el Artículo 4.1. Los artículos 8.1, 9.1, 10.1, 11, 13 y 14 del Reglamento disponen los casos en que se puede descargar basuras al mar. A reserva de lo dispuesto en el Artículo 15 del presente Reglamento, se excluye la posibilidad de descargar en el mar materia plástica, incluidas la cabuyería y redes de pesca de fibras sintéticas, las bolsas de plástico para la basura y las cenizas derivadas del proceso de incineración de productos de plástico. Se excluye la posibilidad de descargar en el mar aceite de cocina.

Policy_Content: La presente Resolución aprueba la “Guía de valoración económica de daños por delitos ambientales de minería ilegal y tráfico ilegal de fauna silvestre.” El objetivo de la Guía es brindar orientación sobre el alcance y la aplicación de la valorización económica de los daños ocasionados por los delitos ambientales de Minería Ilegal, Tala Ilegal y Tráfico Ilegal de Fauna Silvestre contemplados en los artículos 307 A, 308, 310 del Código Penal. La Guía tiene como finalidad establecer el marco metodológico para que la Procuraduría Especializada en Delitos Ambientales del Ministerio del Ambiente, MINAM pueda estimar los daños generados por la comisión de los delitos ambientales de Minería Ilegal, Tala Ilegal y Tráfico Ilegal de Fauna Silvestre.

Policy: Resolution No. 4 of the Ministry of Forestry validating the Regulation on the procedure for transferring payments for forest use.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the procedure for transferring payments for forest use to the national budget, calculated according to the payment deadlines in 2022, by organizations subordinated to the Ministry of Forestry. Payments for forest use (fee for forest use, determined on the basis of the tax value established by the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Belarus, rent for the use of a plot of the forest fund) are transferred by forest users to the accounts of the main departments of the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Belarus of the regions and the city of Minsk, open for crediting payments, control over the payment of which is carried out by the tax authorities at the place of registration of forestry enterprises (payment code 4007). The fee for forest use is transferred at a time before the issuance of a logging license, felling permit, forest land plot usage permit and authorization. Payments for timber harvested in excess of the volumes specified in the felling permit and authorization, are transferred within ten calendar days after the drawing up of the cutting site inspection report in accordance with the established procedure on the basis of data on the actual harvesting of wood. Transfer of additional accrued payments for timber in case of completion of its harvesting earlier than the period specified in the felling permit and authorization, is carried out within ten days from the date of receipt of the relevant notification from the forestry enterprise.

Keyword: Forest management/forest conservation, Public forest, Timber, Timber extraction/logging, Tax/levy, Access-to-information, Data collection/reporting

Policy_Content: Por cuanto el Decreto 35 “De la comercialización de productos agropecuarios”, de 19 de abril de 2021, establece en sus artículos 21 y 23, que los mercados agropecuarios mayoristas son fuente de suministro para el turismo y que las entidades acopiadoras en su gestión cuentan con centros o naves de acopio que comercializan sus productos con destino al turismo, respectivamente; la presente Resolución establece que las empresas, cooperativas agropecuarias, propietarios y usufructuarios de tierras y otros productores agropecuarios, pueden vender directamente la totalidad de sus producciones agropecuarias a las entidades que pertenecen al sistema del turismo o contribuyen al aseguramiento de este. No están contemplados en la Resolución, los productos que se incluyan en el balance nacional anual aprobado por el Ministerio de Economía y Planificación y aquellos que se gestionen por empresas especializadas del sistema de la Agricultura, según lo establecido en el citado Decreto 35. Los productos cárnicos elaborados y sus derivados se adquieren en los establecimientos autorizados, previo cumplimiento de las disposiciones sanitarias y veterinarias vigentes.

Transboundary transportation of hazardous waste across the territory of the Republic of Kazakhstan is carried out on the basis of the conclusion of the authorized body in the field of environmental protection. Import into the territory of the Republic of Kazakhstan from countries that are not members of the Eurasian Economic Union, and export from the territory of the Republic of Kazakhstan to these countries of hazardous waste for the purpose of their further recovery are carried out on the basis of a license issued by a state body determined by the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan. Policy: Geographical Indications Act 2022 (Act 836).
Policy_Content: This Act consisting of 101 articles divided into XV Parts aims to provide for the protection and registration of Geographical Indications (GIs) in relation to goods, and for the implementation of relevant treaties and related matters. To this end, the Act seeks to provide a broader scope of protection to GI proprietors and more clarity concerning the examination procedure for registering GIs. According to Article 8(5), eligible to apply to register a GI is the following (i) a person who carries on an activity as a producer, manufacturer, or trader in the geographical area specified in the application concerning the goods and includes an association of such person; (ii) a competent authority, namely (a) any government or statutory body that carries out the functions of, on behalf of, or sanctioned by, the Malaysian Government or a State Government; (b) a government other than the Malaysian Government; or (c) an authority which is competent to certify the goods. It is essential that a competent authority must have responsibility for the GI in question. As for the registration procedures, the registration of a GI can only be sought in respect of any goods falling within one or more of the categories of goods as set out in the guidelines or practice directions issued by the Registrar of Geographical Indications. The Registrar shall carry out a search of any earlier geographical indications or earlier trademarks. If the GI application does not meet any registration requirements, the Registrar will issue a provisional refusal notice in writing to the applicant on the grounds of provisional refusal. The applicant will have the opportunity to respond to the aforementioned provisional refusal. While, if an application for a geographical indication is accepted, the Registrar shall issue a notice of acceptance requiring the applicant to pay the prescribed fee within a prescribed time limit. Article 10 lists the reasons for the rejection of the registration application. Upon receipt of the payment, the acceptance of the application, along with all of its conditions, amendments, modifications, or limitations, will be published in the Intellectual Property Official Journal which shall contain (a) all matters relating to geographical indications which are required to be published under this Act; and (b) any information relating to geographical indication as the Registrar thinks necessary.

Policy: Law 281/2022 - Competition Law.
Policy_Content: Comprising 66 articles across four chapters, this Law is designed to promote and regulate free competition while prohibiting trusts, monopolies, and cartels. Its objectives extend to protecting consumer rights, achieving economic efficiency, fostering production, innovation, technical development, and maintaining high product quality. The impetus for developing Competition Law stems from recognizing the crucial interrelation between competition policy and economic policies, particularly in trade and their connections to international trade liberalization and development. As a pivotal defense mechanism, the law shields developing countries from potential adverse impacts resulting from the globalized commercial behavior of multinational companies. Given Lebanon's market challenges, including a small economic size and the prevalence of privileges and monopolies, the need for laws to organize and restructure becomes imperative. This legal framework aims to create an environment fostering fair competition, ensuring the protection of investors and small to medium enterprises from dominance. The Competition Law is deemed essential for stimulating investment, promoting innovation, and contributing to the national economy. It is also envisioned as a tool to address collusion and inappropriate practices in public procurement, aligning with proposed economic and legal reforms by the government. Ultimately, the law seeks to establish a comprehensive system that regulates competition, prohibits anti-competitive behaviors, and exercises control over economic concentration operations to ensure market balance and cultivate freedom of competition.

Policy_Content: This Executive Council Resolution approves the articles of Association of the Dubai Electricity and Water Authority PJSC ((DEWA), a public joint-stock company owned by the Government of Dubai. The company, as outlined in Article 4, is responsible for the following objectives (i) establishing, managing, operating, maintaining, and owning the public water and electricity network, including power generation and water desalination stations, reservoirs, and transportation and distribution networks; (ii) establishing, managing, operating, maintaining, and owning electricity and water networks, power stations, water desalination plants, reservoirs, and transmission and distribution networks outside the Emirate; (iii) developing all water sources, treating reservoir water for potability, and storing, transporting, and distributing water to consumers; (iv) initiating and managing projects related to power generation and water supply to meet public needs and development requirements in the Emirate. For the achievement of these objectives, the Company is empowered to (i) purchase electricity and water at suitable prices and conditions; (ii) contract with others for the construction, management, and operation of power generation and water desalination plants, as well as establish, operate, and dissolve subsidiaries; (iii) establish wholly or partially owned companies and contribute to entities within or outside the Emirate in the water and electricity sector; (iv) purchase, sell, and supply fuel to entities permitted for power generation and water supply; (v) acquire, own, rent, and lease land and other real property as needed. Invest funds in commercial, financial, service, or industrial fields directly, indirectly, or through subsidiaries; (vi) borrow and lend money in accordance with Emirate legislation; (vii) grant rights on owned land to entities contributing to power generation and water supply; (viii) execute and oversee projects as determined by the Board of Directors.

Policy: Federal Law No. 34-FZ “On conducting an experiment to limit greenhouse gas emissions in certain constituent entities of the Russian Federation”.
Policy_Content: In order to create the necessary conditions for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and increasing their absorption, the constituent entities of the Russian Federation shall have the right to conduct an experiment on their territories to limit greenhouse gas emissions in accordance with this Federal Law and the legislation of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation in whose territories an experiment is being carried out. The experiment shall be carried out in the following constituent entities: (a) on the territory of the Sakhalin Region from September 1, 2022 to December 31, 2028 inclusive; and (b) in the territories of other subjects of the Russian Federation included in experiment by amending this Federal Law - within the time limits established by amending this Federal Law. The goal of the experiment is to achieve carbon neutrality: (a) on the territory of the Sakhalin Region - until December 31, 2025; and (b) in the territories of other subjects of the Russian Federation included in the experiment in accordance with amendments to this Federal Law - within the time limits established by amending this Federal Law. The objectives of the experiment shall be as follows: (a) stimulating the introduction of technologies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and to increase their absorption; (b) formation of an independent verification system; and (c) creation of a system for the circulation of carbon units and performance units’ quotas. The experiment shall be based on the following principles: (a) the priority of sustainable socio-economic development of the participant in the experiment with low greenhouse gas emissions in achieving the goals of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and building an economy with low greenhouse gas emissions; (b) transparency of data on the mass of greenhouse gas emissions and removals thereof; (c) absence of double accounting of carbon units and performance units quotas; (d) circulation and offset of carbon units and performance units quotas on the territory of the Russian Federation and at the international level; (e) participation of regional regulated organizations in the formation of proposals for setting quotas; (f) differentiated consideration of carbon intensity indicators of regional regulated organizations when setting quotas; and (g) compliance of verification with the documents of the national system of standardization in the field of limiting greenhouse gas emissions.

Policy_Content: The President, in order to eliminate existing shortcomings and problems in the implementation of water-saving technologies, mitigate the negative impact of the observed water shortage in the region, as well as improvement of the efficient use of water resources in the cultivation of crops, decrees as follows: (a) to establish from 2022 the procedure for state support for the introduction of water-saving technologies in the cultivation of agricultural crops, providing for the provision of subsidies to cover: part of the costs of agricultural producers for the introduction of water-saving irrigation technologies in accordance with Appendix No. 2; part of interest expenses on bank loans allocated for the purchase and construction of water-saving irrigation systems, in accordance with Appendix No. 3; after calculating the subsidy funds in accordance with Appendix No. 2 to this Presidential Decree, distribute from the calculated amount: 50 percent - in the year of system introduction; and (b) to establish that: the subsidy funds provided for in paragraph 4 of this Presidential Decree are allocated subject to the use of the introduced water-saving irrigation systems for at least five years; land areas on which water-saving irrigation systems have been introduced are not subject to optimization for at least 5 years, the withdrawal of a land plot or part of it for state and public needs is allowed only with the consent of the land user after full reimbursement of the funds spent; in the event that agricultural producers who received subsidy funds from the State budget for the introduction of water-saving irrigation systems in 2021, but were not in time to use the introduced water-saving irrigation systems during the irrigation season, do not put these systems into operation before the irrigation season 2022, the received subsidy funds in accordance with the established procedure are subject to return to the State budget.

Policy: ORDER No. 28 of the National Commission for the Control of Nuclear Activities subordinated to the Government validating the Nuclear Safety Rules regarding the registration, reporting, analysis of events and the use of operating experience for nuclear facilities.
Policy_Content: Nuclear Safety Rules establish the procedure for the registration, reporting, analysis of events and the use of operating experience for nuclear facilities applicable to the safe conduct, regulation, authorization and control of nuclear activities. Fulfilling the provisions of these rules is a necessary condition for the authorization by the National Commission for the Control of Nuclear Activities (CNCAN), of the activities of construction and assembly, commissioning, operation and decommissioning of a nuclear facility. The provisions of these rules apply both to holders and applicants for authorization for the phases of construction and assembly, commissioning, operation and decommissioning of a nuclear facility. These rules apply to the following categories of nuclear facilities: (a) nuclear power plants, including those equipped with modular reactors; (b) research reactors, nuclear test reactors, zero power reactors and subcritical assemblies; (c) demonstration reactors; (d) nuclear fuel plants; (e) spent nuclear fuel storage facilities; (f) nuclear reactors for the production of energy and isotopes for medical purposes; (g) uranium enrichment facilities; (h) spent nuclear fuel processing/reprocessing facilities; and (i) intermediate or final radioactive waste storage facilities and treatment facilities of radioactive waste, located on the same site and directly related to the nuclear facilities. The authorization holder must establish and implement, within the management system, a systematic process for identifying, reporting, collecting, recording, sorting, processing, analyzing and documenting operational experience and events at the nuclear facility for which he is responsible, as well as relevant external operational events and experience reported by other nuclear facilities, nuclear organizations and organizations from other industrial sectors, at national and international level.

Policy_Content: Le présent arrêté spécifie les modalités de suivi et d’évaluation du compte d’affectation spéciale n° 302-131 intitulé « Fonds national pour la maîtrise de l’énergie, pour les énergies renouvelables et de la cogénération » et cela en application des dispositions de l’article 4 du décret exécutif n° 15-319 du Aouel Rabie El Aouel 1437 correspondant au 13 décembre 2015. Ce fond intervient en matière d’énergies renouvelables et de la cogénération. Cet arrêté reprend tous les éléments entrant dans le cadre de ce sujet et cela en trois chapitres (art2). Le premier chapitre indique le financement des dotations et traite le sujet en deux sections : la première section : Les énergies renouvelables et la cogénération raccordées au réseau électrique national et qui indique les modalités de la demande de l’opérateur, le montant de la compensation ainsi que les actions et projets concernés par la compensation des surcoûts induits par la production d’électricité à partir de sources d’énergies renouvelables et/ou systèmes de cogénération (art3-12). La deuxième section traite de la décision des actions et des projets d’énergies renouvelables non raccordées au réseau électrique national en matière d’intervention, d’évaluation des besoins et des modalités de mise en œuvre ainsi que les responsabilités des bénéficiaires des dotations du Fonds (art13-17). Le deuxième chapitre détermine le rôle et les attributions de l’agence nationale pour la promotion et la rationalisation de l’utilisation de l’énergie (APRUE) qui sont fixés par le ministre de la transition énergétique et des énergies renouvelables (art18-22).  Le troisième chapitre traite des dispositions finales où il est indiqué que le suivi et le contrôle de l’utilisation des dotations accordées sont assurés par les services du ministère de la transition énergétique et des énergies renouvelables et que le ministre doit fixer un programme et suivre une situation semestrielle des engagements et des paiements sur les crédits alloués(art23-27).

Policy: Prime Minister’s Decision No. 722 of 2022 issuing the Executive Regulations for the Law regulating Waste Management promulgated by Law No. 202 of 2020.

Chapter three outlines a key policy mandating that waste generators or owners must ensure the secure disposal of waste from their facilities, projects, or operations upon the delivery, initiation, or conclusion of any new, refurbished, or existing projects. Policy: Governmental Decree No. 206 “On measures of state regulation of consumption and circulation of substances that destroy the ozone layer.”
Policy_Content: This Governmental Decree validates the list of substances that destroy the ozone layer, the circulation of which is subject to state regulation. It determines that: (a) the consumption of substances that destroy the ozone layer, the circulation of which is subject to state regulation in the Russian Federation is carried out in the volumes determined by international treaties of the Russian Federation; (b) the permissible volume of consumption of ozone-depleting substances in the Russian Federation, specified in group I of list C of the list approved by this resolution, determined in accordance with subparagraph "i" of paragraph "a" of Article 3 of the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer, dated September 16, 1987 g., should not exceed 19.98 tons of ozone-depleting potential annually in 2022-2029; (c) from 2030, the consumption of ozone-depleting substances specified in group I of list C approved by this resolution is carried out in the volumes determined by international treaties of the Russian Federation; (d) the calculation of the amount of specific ozone-depleting substances in the allowable volume of consumption of ozone-depleting substances in the Russian Federation, established in accordance with subparagraph "b" of this paragraph, is carried out annually by the Ministry of Natural Resources and Ecology of the Russian Federation, taking into account the amount of ozone-depleting substances produced in the Russian Federation and imported into the Russian Federation substances; (e) the permissible volume of production of ozone-depleting substances in the Russian Federation is established annually, taking into account the permissible volume of their consumption in the Russian Federation; (f) the manufacturing of ozone-depleting substances specified in groups I and III of list C and list E of the list approved by this resolution is carried out if they are used exclusively as raw materials for the manufacturing of other chemicals, as well as in cases stipulated by international treaties of the Russian Federation, in the allowable volume of production of ozone-depleting substances in the Russian Federation; (g) the import of ozone-depleting substances into the Russian Federation is carried out taking into account the established permissible volumes of their consumption in the Russian Federation and the quantitative restrictions established annually in accordance with the law of the Eurasian Economic Union, except for cases when these substances are imported into the Russian Federation to ensure the main types of use of ozone-depleting substances defined in accordance with international treaties of the Russian Federation; (h) it is prohibited to design facilities for economic and other activities that produce ozone-depleting substances and products containing them; (i) it is prohibited to build facilities for economic and other activities that produce ozone-depleting substances and products containing them; (j) the circulation of ozone-depleting substances is allowed only in reusable containers, with the exception of the circulation of ozone-depleting substances in containers with a volume of less than 3 liters for laboratory and analytical uses, as defined by international treaties of the Russian Federation; and (k) the consumption of substances included in list F of the list approved by this Decree is carried out in the amounts determined by international treaties of the Russian Federation.

The park was created for the purpose of preservation, reproduction, and effective use of natural complexes and objects of Ukrainian Polissia, which have a special environmental, healthcare, historical, cultural, scientific, educational, and aesthetic value. The main tasks of the park are: (a) preservation of valuable natural, historical and cultural complexes and objects; (b) creation of conditions for organized tourism, rest and other types of recreational activities in natural conditions with observance of the regime of protection of protected natural complexes and objects; (c) conducting scientific studies of natural complexes and their changes under conditions of recreational use, development of scientific recommendations on issues of environmental protection and effective use of natural resources; and (d) carrying out ecological educational work. In accordance with nature protection legislation, the following zones are distinguished on the territory of the park: (a) protected area; (b) zone of regulated recreation; (c) zone of stationary recreation; and (d) economic zone. For each zone, taking into account its nature protection, health, scientific, recreational, historical and cultural and other values of natural complexes and objects and their features, a differentiated regime is established regarding their protection, reproduction and use.

Policy: Decree of the Chief State Sanitary Doctor of the Russian Federation N 3 "On approval of sanitary rules and norms SanPiN 2.1.3684-21" Sanitary and epidemiological requirements for the maintenance of the territories of urban and rural settlements, for waterbodies, drinking water and drinking water supply, atmospheric air, soils, residential premises, operation of industrial, public premises, organization and implementation of sanitary and anti-epidemic (preventive) measures.”
Policy_Content: This Decree validating sanitary and epidemiological requirements for the maintenance of the territories of urban and rural settlements, for waterbodies, drinking water and drinking water supply, atmospheric air, soils, residential premises, operation of industrial, public premises, organization and implementation of sanitary and anti-epidemic (preventive) measures are binding on the executive authorities of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation, local authorities, legal entities and citizens, including individual entrepreneurs. On the territories of urban and rural settlements, in accordance with the territorial waste management scheme, must be organized container sites for the accumulation of municipal solid waste or underground municipal solid waste accumulation systems with automatic lifts for lifting containers and (or) special sites for the accumulation of bulky waste. Atmospheric air must meet hygienic standards for maximum allowable concentrations of pollutants, approximate safe levels of exposure, maximum allowable levels of physical impact, as well as biological factors that ensure their safety for human health. The quality and safety of drinking and hot water must comply with hygienic standards. Drinking water supplied to clients using water supply systems is recognized as high-quality drinking water, if, at the established frequency of control during the year, are not revealed: (a) radiological indicators exceeding the levels of hygienic standards (except for total microbial count, total coliforms, thermotolerant coliform bacteria and Escherichia coli) parasitological, virological indicators, intervention levels by radiological indicators; (b) exceeding the levels of hygienic standards for total microbial count, total coliforms, thermotolerant coliform bacteria and Escherichia coli  in 95% or more of samples taken at water intake points, with the number of samples being studied at least 100 per year; and (c) exceeding the levels of hygienic standards of organoleptic, generalized indicators, inorganic and organic substances by more than the error of the method for determining indicators. The quality of water in surface and underground waterbodies used by the population must comply with hygienic standards depending on the type of use of waterbodies or their sections: (a) as a source of drinking and household water use, as well as for water supply to food industry enterprises; and (b) for recreational water use, as well as areas of waterbodies located within the boundaries of populated areas. The content of chemical and biological substances potentially hazardous to humans, biological and microbiological organisms in soils at different depths, as well as the level of radiation background, should not exceed hygienic standards. An economic entity carrying out work with pesticides and agrochemicals must, prior to the treatment with pesticides and agrochemicals, ensure that the population living on the border with the territories to be treated is notified through the media about the planned work no later than 5 calendar days before the day of application of pesticides and agrochemicals. With the ground method of treatment with pesticides and agrochemicals, the distance from settlements, sources of household and drinking and cultural and domestic water use, places of recreation for the population and places for manual work on caring for crops should be at least 300 meters, taking into account the wind rose.

Policy: Regional Law No. 13-oz “On the delimitation of powers of state authorities of the Leningrad Region in the field of organization, protection and use of specially protected natural areas in the Leningrad Region.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law delimits the powers of the bodies of state authorities of the Leningrad Region and regulates certain relations in the field of organization, protection and use of the regional protected areas. Regional Government shall have the following powers in the field of organization, protection and use of the regional protected areas: (a) adoption within its competence of normative legal acts; (b) making decisions on reserving land in cases related to the creation of protected natural areas of regional significance; (c) making decisions on the creation of natural parks, state natural reserves of regional significance, dendrological parks and botanical gardens of regional significance, approval of the boundaries of the indicated protected natural areas and regulations related thereto; (d) making decisions on the declaration of natural objects and complexes monuments of nature of regional significance, and the territories occupied by them - protected areas of regional significance, approval of boundaries and certificates of the indicated protected areas of regional significance; (e) making decisions on the establishment (change) of the regime of special protection of natural parks, state nature reserves of regional significance, dendrological parks and botanical gardens of regional significance, natural monuments of regional significance; (f)  establishment of the procedure for the protection of territories of natural parks, state nature reserves of regional significance and other protected areas of regional significance; (g) approval of the regulation on regional state control (supervision) in the field of protection and use of protected areas of regional significance; (h) approval of state programs of the Leningrad region in the field of organization, protection and use of protected areas of regional significance; and (i) setting the amount of fees for natural persons visiting protected areas of regional significance.
Subject: Environment gen., Wild species & ecosystems
Keyword: Policy/planning, Protected area, Management/conservation
Geographical_area: Arctic, Asia and the Pacific, Black Sea, Caspian Sea, CIS (Commonwealth of Independent States), Eastern Europe, Europe, Europe and Central Asia, North Pacific, North-West Pacific

Policy: Governmental Decree No. 168 “On approval of the Regulation on licensing of space activities.”
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the procedure for licensing of space activities carried out by legal entities on territory of the Russian Federation and other territories over which the Russian Federation exercises jurisdiction in accordance with the legislation of the Russian Federation and the norms of international law, and also the procedure for organizing and implementing the federal state license control (supervision) of space activities. Licensing of space activities is carried out by State Corporation for Space Activities "Roscosmos". It establishes licensing terms and conditions. Federal state licensing control (supervision) for space activity is carried out by licensing authority. When exercising license control, the following preventive actions are carried out: (a) informing; (b) generalization of law enforcement practice; (c) announcement of a warning; (d) counseling; and (e) preventive visit. Licensing activities include services for the environmental survey of spaceports and fall areas of separating parts of space rockets.

Policy: Law No. 8.980 approving the Coastal Ecological-Economic Zoning of the Southern Coasts of Sergipe, as mentioned in Law No. 8.634 of 27 December 2019.
Policy_Content: This Law, consisting of 32 articles divided into five Chapters, establishes the Coastal Ecological-Economic Zoning of the Southern Coasts of Sergipe, as mentioned in Law No. 8.634 of 27 December 2019 and amended by Law No. 8.924 of 22 November 2021. The Southern Coasts of Sergipe are considered to be the land strip that comprises the stretch that goes from the Vaza-Barris River to the Real River and the marine strip that extends for 12 nautical miles. The licensing and inspection of projects to be developed in each Zone must be carried out based on the norms, guidelines and criteria recommended in this Law, without prejudice to other Federal, State and Municipal legal provisions and international treaties, to which Brazil is a signatory, specific protection of the environment and the territorial rights of traditional peoples and communities. The Coastal Ecological-Economic Zoning of the Southern Coasts of Sergipe aims to regulate the territorial planning necessary for the sustainable development of the coastal zone, dividing it into territorial zones identified from the needs of protection, conservation and recovery of natural resources, in addition to the recognition, appreciation and respect for the socio-environmental and cultural diversity of the peoples of traditional communities in all aspects addressed in Federal Decree No. 6.040 of 7 February 2007.

Policy_Content: Regulation on the procedure for determining the periodicity of planned measures of state control of compliance of operators (facilities) with the requirements of legislation in the field of organic production, circulation and labelling of organic products by the State Service for Food Safety and Consumer Protection, and criteria for assessing risk from its implementation establishes the procedure for determining the frequency of planned measures of state control of compliance of operators (facilities) with the requirements of legislation in the field of organic production, circulation and labelling of organic products, which are carried out by the State Service for Food Safety and Consumer Protection. Criteria for assessing the degree of risk from the operator's economic activity in the field of organic production, circulation and labelling of organic products are: (a) type of operator's activity; (b) the period of the operator's economic activity in the field of organic production, circulation and labelling of organic products; (c) the number of sectors in which the operator produces and/or trades in organic products; (d) the number of violations by the operator of the requirements of the legislation in the field of organic production, circulation and labelling of organic products, identified as a result of state control measures carried out during the last three years preceding the planning year; (e) the number of cases in which the operator applied exceptions to the requirements for organic production during the last three years preceding the planning year; and (f) availability of information from the certification body on violations of the legislation in the field of organic production, circulation and labelling of organic products detected during the last three years preceding the planning year.

Policy: Resolution No. 885 of the Cabinet of Ministers validating the Procedure for the use of funds provided for in the state budget for compensation of losses from damage to agricultural crops as a result of man-made and natural emergencies.
Policy_Content: This Procedure defines the mechanism of using the funds provided by the Ministry of Agrarian Policy in the state budget under the program "Financial support of agricultural commodity producers", which are directed to agricultural commodity producers to compensate for losses from completely lost (destroyed) crops as a result of man-made and natural emergency situations. Budgetary funds are used for the purpose of providing support to agricultural producers whose crop crops have been completely lost (destroyed) as a result of man-made and natural emergencies, to stabilize the gross production of agricultural crops and ensure the food security of the state. The main administrator of budget funds and responsible executor of the budget program is the Ministry of Agrarian Policy. The administrators of lower-level budget funds are the structural units of regional state administrations that ensure the performance of functions in matters of agro-industrial development. Compensation for losses from completely lost (destroyed) crops of agricultural crops as a result of man-made and natural emergency situations at the expense of budget funds is provided by paying a subsidy per unit of land on which crops are completely lost (destroyed). Subsidies shall be provided to agricultural commodity producers - legal entities regardless of their organizational and legal form and form of ownership and to natural persons - entrepreneurs: (a) in relation to which are not subject to bankruptcy proceedings and/or which have not been declared bankrupt, and/or which are not at the stage of liquidation; (b) who do not have, as of the 1st of the month in which the decision is made to include in the consolidated information of subsidy recipients, more than six months overdue payment arrears, the control of the payment of which is entrusted to the State Tax Service bodies; (c) which are not classified as legal entities or individuals subject to special economic and other restrictive measures (sanctions); (d) who did not receive insurance compensation for completely lost (destroyed) crops; and (e) which are included in the list of affected economic entities, in accordance with the decision of the Expert Commission for Determining the Levels and Classes of Emergency Situations of the Emergency Situations of Ukraine regarding the determination of the level and class of natural emergencies that occurred in the region. The subsidy is paid once a year.

Policy: Law No. 5/2022 against Theft on Agricultural Plots.
Policy_Content: This Law aims to sanction practices of theft and destruction of products on agricultural properties. The Law in particular establishes that whoever, with the illegitimate intention of appropriating for themselves or others, enters other people's agricultural properties, subtracts, transports and keeps agricultural and forestry goods, as well as species of poultry, goats, sheep, pigs and cattle or other species intended for human consumption, whose financial value is less than the minimum wage of the Civil Service, is punished with imprisonment for up to one year or a fine. Anyone who illegitimately appropriates, for their own benefit or for others, agricultural, forestry or livestock goods entrusted to their custody, is punished with imprisonment from one to three years or a fine.

Policy: Order No. 106 of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Ecology validating the Methodology for determining high and very high air pollution.
Policy_Content: This Methodology is aimed at determining high and very high air pollution in order to identify urban settlements and city districts additionally inserted in experiment for setting quotas for pollutant emissions to the atmospheric air on the basis of summary calculation of air pollution. Determination of high and very high air pollution shall be based on state air monitoring data. To determine high and very high atmospheric air pollution, data from the observation network of the state monitoring of atmospheric air are used, which make up homogeneous series of observations of the state and pollution of atmospheric air. In order to determine high and very high atmospheric air pollution, measurement data of concentrations of at least five pollutants are used with the number of observations of at least 500 for each pollutant per calendar year at each observation point with discrete sampling and at least 20,000 with continuous measurement methods.

Policy: Regional Law No. 47 “On organizing and ensuring the protection of the rights, primordial habitat and traditional way of life of the indigenous peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East of the Russian Federation living in the Kamchatka Territory.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates issues related to the organization and ensuring the protection of rights, indigenous habitats and traditional way of life of small indigenous peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East of the Russian Federation, living in the Kamchatka Territory, to which, in accordance with the Unified List approved by the Government of the Russian Federation of indigenous peoples of the Russian Federation include the Aleuts, Alyutorians, Itelmens, Kamchadals, Koryaks, Chukchis, Evens (Lamuts), eskimos. This Regional Law shall apply to persons belonging to small indigenous peoples conducting traditional way of life, carrying out traditional economic activities and engaged in traditional crafts. The principles of organizing and ensuring the protection of rights, the original habitat and traditional way of life of small indigenous peoples are: (a) the complexity of solving problems of socio-economic and cultural development of small indigenous peoples; (b) the need for the participation of representatives and associations of small indigenous peoples in decision-making on issues affecting their rights and interests in the development of natural resources in places of traditional residence and traditional economic activity of small indigenous peoples; (c) recognition of the right of small indigenous peoples to priority use of wildlife in the places of their traditional residence and traditional economic activities; (d) maintaining a balance of interests of small indigenous peoples, other population of the Kamchatka Territory, as well as economic entities, carrying out business activities in places of traditional residence and traditional economic activities of small indigenous small peoples; and (e) differentiation of state support for small indigenous peoples, depending on living conditions and economic activities, other factors that determine the specifics of life of small indigenous peoples. State support for persons belonging to small indigenous peoples and their associations is carried out in accordance with federal and regional legislation in the form of cash payments, including subsidies, grants, compensation, other payments, assistance in kind, provision of services in various fields on the terms of partial payment or free of charge, providing advice. Territories of traditional nature management of the regional significance are formed by decrees of the Regional Government on the basis of appeals of persons belonging to small indigenous peoples, and communities of small indigenous peoples or their authorized representatives. The procedure for the formation of territories of traditional nature management of regional significance and a list of documents required for making decisions on the formation of territories of traditional nature management of regional significance, are established by a resolution of the Regional Government.

Policy: Governmental Order No. 9 regarding port facilities for taking over waste from ships.
Policy_Content: This Governmental Order aims to protect the marine environment against the negative effects of waste discharges and cargo residues in navigable national waters, from ships using Romanian ports, ensuring, at the same time, the smooth operation of maritime traffic, by improving the availability and use of appropriate port facilities for taking over, as well as the delivery, of waste in the respective facilities. This Order applies to all ships, regardless of the flag they fly, that call or operate in one of the Romanian ports, with the exception of: (1) ships engaged in services ports military ships; (2) military auxiliary ships or of other ships owned or operated by the state and which are used exclusively for governmental non-commercial purposes. Port administrations must ensure the adequate equipment and permanent availability of port facilities for receiving waste from ships, in accordance with the needs of ships calling at the port, without producing unjustified delays to them. Port administrations must ensure the following requirements: (a) the port reception facilities are able to receive the types and quantities of waste from ships that normally use the respective port, taking into account: (i) the request to hand over the waste from the ships; (ii) the size and geographical position of the respective port; (iii) the type of ships calling at the respective port; (b) the formalities and practical aspects related to the use of port reception facilities should be simple and quick, in order to avoid unjustified delays caused to ships; (c) the fees charged for handover should not be a disincentive for ships requesting to use the port reception facilities; (d) port reception facilities to ensure the management of waste from ships in a rational way from an ecological point of view.

Policy: Decree determining the financing programme of activities and energy efficiency improvement measure in 2022.
Policy_Content: This Decree, based on the provisions of the Serbian Law on energy efficiency and rational use of energy, establishes the programme of financing activities and improvement measures aimed for energy efficiency in 2022, which is part of this publication. Activities and measures to improve energy efficiency, which will be financed in 2022, as well as the amount of funds for carrying out those activities and measures are also determined in this programme. Improving energy efficiency, both in the production sectors and in sectors of energy consumption is recognized as one of the key elements of the energy policy of the Republic of Serbia, given that it contributes to security energy supply, reducing energy consumption in private and commercial sector, increasing the competitiveness of the industry and increasing the standards of citizens, that is, it contributes to the reduction of import dependence and the reduction of negative effects of the energy sector on the environment, especially the gas emissions they create the greenhouse effect. Considering the tendency towards energy decarbonisation efficiency in the coming period will have an even more significant role that it will be reflected by a set of strategic documents whose preparation is underway. The main goal of the Programme is financial support for measures and mechanisms for improvement of energy efficiency. The Programme should achieve the following specific goals: 1) achieving energy savings and its rational use through application of proven modern technologies and products, the use of which is economical justified; 2) use of renewable energy sources for own needs; 3) employment of business entities; 4) environmental protection through reduced emissions of gases that create the effect greenhouses (GHG gases); 5) increasing public awareness of the importance of energy efficiency.

Policy: Law on consumer protection.
Policy_Content: This Law governs the protection of the basic rights of consumers when buying products and in other forms of acquisition of products on the market, namely: 1. the right to protection of economic interests of consumers; 2. the right to protection from threats to life, health and property; 3. the right to legal protection of consumers; 4. the right to consumer information and education; 5. the right of consumers to organise themselves to safeguard their interests; 6. the right to consumer representation and participation of the consumer representatives in the work of bodies dealing with issues of interest to consumers. This Law further transposes into the Croatian legislation all regulations of the European Union that are listed in article 2. The official meaning of terms and related definitions are provided in article 4. The product offered to consumers in the territory of the Republic of Croatia shall contain the following information on its packaging, tags, labels or on the product itself: 1. the basic features of the product to the extent necessary to the consumer to make an informed decision, such as name, type and model of the product, the name under which the product is marketed, and its composition, properties and technical characteristics; 2. the name and the head office of the manufacturer or the importer with the head office in the territory of the European Union.

Policy: Order No. 54 of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Ecology validating the Rules for the use of forests for the creation and operation of timber processing infrastructure facilities.
Policy_Content: These Rules establish the requirements for the use of forests for the creation and operation of timber processing infrastructure facilities. Using forests to build and operate forest processing infrastructure and facilities is an entrepreneurial activity related to the creation of timber processing facilities and processing facilities for other forest resources, manufacturing of products obtained from timber. Forest plots located in the state or municipal property, are allotted to citizens, legal entities on lease for creation and operation of timber processing infrastructure facilities. In order to locate timber processing infrastructure facilities, first of all, non-forest lands are used, and in the absence of such lands on a forest plot, forest lands are used: (a) areas of non-renewed cuttings, burnt areas, sparse areas, wastelands, clearings, as well as areas where low-density and least valuable forest plantations are growing. The use of forest lands not specified in the afore-mentioned paragraph for the purpose of locating timber processing infrastructure facilities is allowed if there are no other options for locating these facilities. When using forests for the creation and operation of timber processing infrastructure facilities, the following cases should be excluded: (a) pollution (including radioactive and oil) of forests and other negative impact on forests; and (b) the entry of vehicles into forest areas in the event of restrictions on the stay of citizens in the forests.

Policy_Content: This Act is ratified with the purpose of developing rural areas and poverty reduction through providing energy to all. Policy: Decree No. 35 of the Cabinet of Ministers validating the Regulation on land conservation.
Policy_Content: This Decree determines the organizational grounds for conservation of degraded and unproductive lands, including reserve land, land plots, which tenure and management are ecologically unsafe and economically inefficient, as well as technogenically polluted land plots, on which it is impossible to obtain ecological production, while stay of persons on such land puts at risk their health. Conservation of land is carried out by terminating or restricting their economic use in the manner prescribed by law for a certain period and grassland renovation, afforestation or renaturalization thereof. Conservation of land is carried out independently of the form of ownership thereof by the initiative of the owner, or on the basis of the submission of a respective territorial body of the territorial authorities of the State Geological Cadastre and/or the territorial body of the State Ecological Inspection. Conservation of privately owned land is carried out by the decision of the relevant village, settlement, city council, on the territory of which the land plot is located, on the basis of a land conservation contract. The contract on conservation of privately owned land is concluded between the owner of the land plot and the relevant village, settlement, city council in writing and contains the following information about the land plot: (a) cadastral number (if any); (b) location and size; (c) type and method of land conservation; and (d) cost and term of land conservation. Other terms of the contract are determined by agreement of the parties.

Policy: Second Ordinance on the Implementation of the Wind Energy at Sea Act.
Policy_Content: This Ordinance is enacted by the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency and provides for the suitability, project specification and the capacity to be installed based on the Offshore Wind Energy Act. The Regulation provides for determination of eligible areas including exclusive economic zone of the North Sea for project. The effects of project on the marine environment are considered including avoidance and reduction of emissions, noise emissions, waste, sewage, plant cooling, oil content of the drainage water and diesel generators. The Ordinance further lays down regulations on the general rules for the safety and ease of ship and air transport, traffic safety, vehicles and work equipment, flight corridors and navigation safety. Subsection 6 of the Ordinance determines safety and health protection principal, rescue and emergency medical supply and monitoring of compliance with health and safety regulations. Other obligations refer to compatibility with existing and planned cables, distance to wind turbines in neighbouring areas, feed-in and connection point and other obligations for the project sponsor. The Regulation consists of 41 Articles and 4 Parts.

Policy_Content: The Cabinet of Ministers, in order to improve the ecological situation of the country, prevention of rising of sand, salt and dust from the drained bottom of the Aral sea and mitigation of the negative impact of global climate change, decrees that State administration of Forestry of the Republic of Uzbekistan shall be responsible for planting permanent "green cover" protective forests on the dry bottom of the Aral sea and in the Aral region with a view of restoration of ecosystem, monitoring progress of planting and environmental restoration. Policy: Real Decreto 47/2022, de 18 de enero, sobre protección de las aguas contra la contaminación difusa producida por los nitratos procedentes de fuentes agrarias.
Policy_Content: Este real decreto tiene por objeto establecer las medidas necesarias para reducir la contaminación de las aguas superficiales continentales, las aguas de transición, las aguas costeras y las aguas subterráneas, causada por los nitratos procedentes de fuentes agrarias, y actuar preventivamente contra nuevas contaminaciones de esa clase. El decreto contiene normas para la transposición al Derecho español de la Directiva 91/676/CEE, de 12 de diciembre, relativa a la protección de las aguas contra la contaminación producida por nitratos de origen agrícola, ya transpuesta por el Real Decreto 261/1996, de 16 de febrero, que ahora se deroga mediante la disposición derogatoria única del decreto. En esta norma se recogen una serie de definiciones que buscan determinar el alcance de determinados conceptos técnicos. Aunque se refiere principalmente a nitratos, también aparecen algunas otras sustancias esenciales para seguir el procedimiento operativo de lucha contra esta contaminación, entre las que se considera el fósforo y sus compuestos.

Logging operations are carried out in accordance with the technological map of logging operations, compiled by legal entities, individual entrepreneurs engaged in logging or forest conservation measures. When performing logging operations, the terms of the lease agreement for a forest plot, the agreement for the sale of forest plantations, the contract, the right of permanent (unlimited) use, the forest development project, the forest declaration, the technological map of logging operations, the requirements of forest legislation, regulatory legal acts regulating forest relations.
