Policy: Decree-Law No. 82/2021 establishing the Integrated Management System for Rural Fires in continental territory and defining its operating rules.
Policy_Content: This Decree-Law, consisting of 81 articles divided into seven Chapters, establishes the Integrated Management System for Rural Fires (SGIFR) in the entire National continental territory and defines its operating rules. SGIFR is a set of structures, norms and processes of institutional articulation in the integrated management of rural fire, organization and intervention, relating to planning, preparation, prevention, suppression and relief and post-event, carried out by competent public entities in the integrated management of rural dwellings and by private entities in rural or urban land. SGIFR comprises the following intervention: a) Protection against rural fires, aimed to the safety and safeguard of people, animals and goods; b) Management of rural fire, aimed to the defense and promotion of the value of rural territories, considering their protective role by reducing the conditions for the occurrence and progression of rural fires. SGIFR is based on the principle of specialization of knowledge, using resources with adequate qualification and training for each of the axes of intervention above mentioned, ensuring the concerted action of all resources.

Policy: Governmental Decree No. 641 validating some legislative acts on seed production of agricultural crops.
Policy_Content: This Governmental Decree establishes the procedure for conducting a competition between farms and other agricultural organizations for the right to grow seed of cotton and grain crops of the original, elite and next generations, the procedure for submittal of applications for participating in the competition, questionnaire accompanying the application, selection procedure. The duties of the winners of the competition for the right to grow seeds of cotton and grain crops shall be as follows: (a) cultivation of seeds of plant variety belonging to one generation; (b) preservation of valuable characteristics of the breeding variety; (c) cultivation of offspring seeds with high quality and variety purity; (d) follow the procedure and rules for seed breeding; and (e) carry out the agrotechnical activities in prescribed manner and in conformity with the established standards. The following are the functions of the winners of the competition entitled to grow seeds of cotton or seeds of grain crops: (a) placement of crops grown for seed in high-yielding, mechanized, well-watered, non-saline and flat fields; (b) plan for timely implementation of crop rotation and agrotechnical activities creating and implementing a schedule; (c) ensuring that the farm has an agronomist specialized in seed production (this is not required when the head of the farm is an agronomist specialized in seed production); (d) planting of seed material processed (sterilized) with chemicals approved for use (except for special elite seed farms); (e) prevention of alien varieties and plants in areas sown for seed cleaning; (f) prevention of mix up with other plant varieties, particularly with disease-causing weeds; (g) defoliation after complete harvesting of seed cotton in seed cotton fields; and (h) transportation and delivery of cotton seeds and grain seeds by specialized vehicles. The procedure for premium payment for seeds of varieties of spiked grains envisages payment of premium payment at the expense of the State Support Fund for Agriculture under the Ministry of Finance. The cost of premiums paid for grain seeds is included in the cost of finished grain. Farms and other agricultural organizations growing grain with seed heads in order to have the right to grow grain with seed heads belonging to the original, elite and next generations are determined on the basis of a competition in accordance with the regulation on the procedure for holding a competition. Based on the legislation, a contract on the purchase of grain with seed heads is concluded between the seed grain producing entities determined on the basis of the competition and grain enterprises, grain production clusters and seed production clusters, and the acceptance of seed grain is carried out in the prescribed manner. In the contract, grain grown for seed, selection type, generation and quantity and other conditions are indicated. Variety originators, scientific research institutes, breeders and other subjects involved in seed production shall have the following obligations: (a) to stimulate seed scientists and organizations involved in seed quality assurance; (b) to create and introduce high-yielding, early, disease- and pest-, and drought-resistant varieties of grain crops suitable for different soil and climate conditions; (c) to grow and multiply primary seeds of new and promising varieties of grain crops suitable for different soil and climate conditions; (d) to carry out the testing of varieties of new grain crops at variety testing stations and plots located in different regions under high agrotechnical conditions, to comprehensively and objectively evaluate varieties, to isolate promising varieties resistant to pests; (e) to test the varieties of new spiked grain crops in large-scale production, to include those with valuable economic characteristics in the state register of agricultural crops recommended for planting in the territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan; and (f) to ensure the authenticity of conclusions confirming the compliance of the state standard

The text further refers to strategies and approaches for mainstreaming BDFAP technical consideration for BDFAP such as terrestrial farm, aquaculture, marine and coastal ecosystem. The Order provides for general consideration for BDFAP within protected areas that relates to conservation of native species, protected areas for indigenous peoples and local communities.  The Order further discuss on institutional support to on-farm conservation and forest lands, capacity building, establishment of demo farms for extension of support, research and development and monitoring. The Order consists of 14 Sections.

Policy: Regional Law No. 103-ZSO “On healthcare areas and resorts of regional significance.”
Policy_Content: Healthcare areas and resorts of regional significance on the regional territory are intended for treatment and rest of the population and are respectively classified as protected areas and territories that have their own characteristics in use and protection. This Regional Law establishes the powers of the regional state bodies related to rational use, development and protection of healthcare areas and resorts of regional significance. The territory is acknowledged as a healthcare area or a resort of regional significance by the Regional Government by agreement with the relevant federal executive authorities. Healthcare areas and resorts of the regional significance, as well as their land in accordance with Federal law are respectively acknowledged as protected areas. Their protection is carried out through the establishment of districts of sanitary (mountain and sanitary) protection with a special management regime established therein, including special residence regime and nature management, providing protection and preservation of healthcare areas and resorts of the regional significance with adjacent territories, from pollution and premature exhaustion. Boundaries and regime of districts of sanitary (mountain and sanitary) protection of healthcare areas and resorts of regional significance are established by the authorized body in the manner determined by the Regional Government.

Policy: Ley 240 – Regula la actividad de agroturismo en Panamá
Policy_Content: La presente Ley tiene por objeto impulsar el agroturismo, dentro del turismo rural, como una alternativa para el desarrollo sostenible del sector productivo agropecuario, de manera que tanto turistas como visitantes puedan tener una experiencia auténtica de interiorización de los procesos productivos, de contacto con las costumbres y tradiciones, y de exploración de la naturaleza autóctona, de manera sana, segura y con calidad diferenciada, con un alto grado de satisfacción, lo cual redundará en la generación de empleos e ingresos complementarios a la actividad primaria, principalmente en el entorno rural. Se establecen objetivos específicos: 1) Dar a conocer el agroturismo a nivel nacional y su importancia para el desarrollo sostenible; 2) capacitar y mantener actualizados a los emprendedores agroturísticos con los nuevos protocolos sanitarios del Ministerio de Desarrollo Agropecuario; 3) Fomentar el valor, rescate y desarrollo de los productos típicos y su comercialización; 4) facilitar la permanencia del hombre de campo en su territorio; 5) promover la asociatividad como mecanismo de acción para el logro de objetivos comunes; 6) adoptar las medidas necesarias para profundizar la educación ambiental y la sensibilización en los aspectos ecológicos; 7) incentivar, gestionar y asesorar al emprendedor agroturístico en métodos de tecnologías más limpias y procesos productivos amigables con el ambiente; 8) establecer coordinaciones de trabajo interinstitucional a fin de crear las condiciones necesarias para que el turista pueda compartir, experimentar y valorizar la cultura e identidad de las tradiciones del hombre del campo; 9) brindar asesoría y capacitación técnica al emprendedor agroturístico y colaboradores para el buen manejo y desarrollo de las fincas agroturísticas, especialmente en temas como la agricultura orgánica; 10) apoyar a los emprendedores agroturísticos a fin de que puedan obtener la certificación orgánica de sus fincas, otorgada por la Dirección Nacional de Sanidad Vegetal del Ministerio de Desarrollo Agropecuario; 11) promover el agroturismo para que sea una marca de turismo exitosa y bien evaluada por los visitantes, consolidándola, a fin que sea el mismo turista quien ayude a promoverla; 12) exaltar el rol de la mujer rural y los jóvenes dentro del negocio agroturístico; y 13) fomentar la protección y conservación de los recursos naturales.

Policy: State of Palestine’s First Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) - Updated Submission.
Policy_Content: These Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) is a 20-year nationwide multi-sectoral document aiming at including amendments and additions to actions than those proposed in the previous document of 2017. It is focused on climate adaptation actions, while not neglecting climate mitigation and the global objective of the UNFCCC and Article 2.1 (a) of the Paris Agreement. In comparison to the first NDC, the new conditional actions are gender responsive, time-bound, and contain measurable targets. in fact, the Palestine’s key climate goal is to reduce its climate vulnerabilities, primarily through increasing adaptive capacities, and, thereby, enhance the climate resilience of the national development process and local communities. The document follows a holistic approach: considering that the NDC actions in each sector have both positive and negative impacts on NDC mitigation and adaptation actions in other sectors, it has been developed a NDC Partnership Plan that  provides for development of NDC implementation action plans addressing the nexus between sectors, in particular  between: (a) agriculture, waste, energy, water, and food; (b) waste, water, energy, and infrastructure; and (c) transport and energy (particularly regarding electric vehicles).

The Programme will be managed by the Secretariat for Social Protection, Justice, Citizenship, Women and Human Rights (SPS). The general objective of the State Programme is to promote the integrated development of the craft sector and to value artisans, raising their cultural, professional, social and economic level. The Program specifically seeks to: recognize and strengthen the artisan profession; provide strategic and permanent support to artisans, especially through the promotion of professional qualification; promote and strengthen the handicraft activity and production chain, developing instruments and tools to improve the handicraft sector; implement sales channels for artisanal products, bringing artisans closer to the consumer market; promote handicrafts as an expression of Ceará's cultural diversity. The Programme is structured according to the following axes: strengthening State artisans and handicrafts; market access; craftsman qualification and training; strengthening of artisan women, through specific incentives, etc.

Policy: Structural Regulations of the forest protection stations.
Policy_Content: These Regulations, based on the provisions of the Bulgarian Law on forests, determines the structure, functions, tasks and organization of activity of the forest protection stations. The Forest Protection Station shall be a legal entity of budget support/third-level spending unit with a budget under the budget of the Ministry of Agriculture and Food, a specialized territorial unit of the Executive Forest Agency (EAG). The forest protection station shall assist the executive director of EAG in exercising its powers in the field of protection of the forest territories from diseases, pests and other damages, including the use of plant protection products (PPP), such as: 1. render methodical and practical guidance, consult, give prescriptions and control over the protection of the forest territories from diseases, pests and other damages in its defined scope of activity; 2. assist the executive director in exercising his / her powers, ensure his / her technical activity and perform activities for administrative servicing of the citizens and the legal entities. The forest protection station shall be established and closed by an order of the executive director of EAG after coordination with the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Forestry. The forest protection station shall be financed by: 1. the state budget through the budget of EAG; 2. targeted funds provided by other financing institutions and organizations under programs and projects previously agreed with EAG; 3. donations.

Policy: Biodiversity Act (SNS 2021, c 3).
Policy_Content: The purpose of this Act is to provide for the stewardship, conservation, sustainable use and governance of biodiversity in the Province, as part of an integrated framework of legislation, while recognizing (a) biodiversity has inherent value; (b) conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity is a responsibility shared by all Nova Scotians; (c) the importance of reducing the direct pressures on biodiversity and promoting restoration and sustainable use; and (d) the importance of implementation of this Act through participatory planning, education, sharing of information and capacity building. The Minister is responsible for the supervision and management of this Act and its powers are listed under section 8, these include develop, co-ordinate, adopt and implement policies, standards, guidelines and programs for the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity; establish or adopt goals and targets; co-ordinate and implement biodiversity policies and programs. The Minister may also enter into an agreement with any person, including the Government of Canada, the government of a province of Canada or a municipality, or with an agency of any of the foregoing, for any purpose related to this Act or the regulations, including an agreement respecting  the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity; the conduct of biodiversity or ecological investigations; development and implementation of collaborative programs for the classification, inventory and assessment of biodiversity; research, programs and measures, etc. The Minister may cause studies,  retain experts with expertise in the areas of natural science, etc.

Policy: Decree-Law No. 57/2021 establishing structure, organization and functioning of the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAA).
Policy_Content: This Decree-Law, consisting of 38 articles divided into five Chapters and one Annex, establishes the structure, organization and functioning of the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAA). It establishes composition, duties and responsibilities of the above mentioned Ministry, entitled to: government department whose mission is: to design, coordinate, control, execute and evaluate the specific policies defined by the Government for the sectors of agriculture, forestry, livestock, agribusiness, food and nutrition security, environment and natural hazards, climate, water and sanitation; conceive, coordinate, control and evaluate public policies for the agrarian economy; design, coordinate, control and evaluate public policies for the environment and climate change. The MAA, namely in the sectors of agriculture, forestry, livestock, agribusiness, food and nutrition security, environment, climate, water and sanitation, is responsible for: defining, formulating and implementing policy guidelines on food and nutrition security, agriculture , of the environment, climate, water and sanitation in close collaboration with the collegiate bodies established exclusively for this purpose; promote and coordinate the sectoral planning process in its areas of action and ensure its implementation; propose, disseminate and ensure the effective application of legislative, regulatory and administrative measures relating to the sectors within its competence; ensure the articulation of public economic and social policies, aimed at promoting food and nutrition security; encourage applied research, innovation and technology transfer with the aim of structuring and developing agricultural value chains, protecting the environment and improving household income; promote and facilitate the development of organic agriculture and agro-ecological practices; participate in the formulation of agricultural credit policy and norms, the modalities and conditions of insurance for agro-forestry and agro-industry production, and the pricing policy; participate in the promotion of professional training in the areas of agriculture, forestry, livestock and agribusiness, stimulating young entrepreneurship through incentives and tax benefits; combat desertification through reforestation and management, by promoting methods and techniques suitable for the use of soils, by carrying out rural engineering works and by the protection and correct use of soils and forests; participate in the definition and implementation of policy measures that contribute to the optimization of marketing systems for production factors, agricultural and forestry products, etc.

Policy: Order No. 621 of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Natural Resources validating the Instructions for keeping electronic records of timber.
Policy_Content: This Instruction establishes the procedure for keeping electronic records of timber by forest owners and permanent forest users. The main tasks of electronic wood accounting are: (a) timely and reliable display of information on the movement of timber; (b) monitoring the use of forest resources; (c) confirmation of the origin, procurement and sale of unprocessed timber, prevention of its illegal circulation; and (c) systematization and generalization of information about the origin, procurement and sale of timber by forest users. The main sources of wood supply are: (a) logging for main use; (b) felling for the formation and improvement of forests and other measures related to forestry management; and (c) other measures not related to forestry management (clearing of forest areas covered with forest vegetation in connection with the construction of waterworks, pipelines, roads, etc.). Harvested timber shall be classified as follows: (a) round timber; (b) long timber; (c) fuelwood for industrial use; (d) fuelwood for non-industrial use; (e) brash; and (f) Christmas trees. The following forms of accounting are used for keeping electronic records of timber: (a) specification of acceptance of timber from harvesting (Appendix 1); (b) diary of acceptance of wood from harvesting (Appendix 2); (c) diary of the acceptance of timber from long-term splitting timber (Appendix 3); (d) specification-bill of acceptance of timber after quality change (Appendix 4); (e) specification-bill of lading for shipment of timber by rail (Appendix 5); and (f) consignment note (forest) (Appendix 6).

Policy_Content: This Decree approves the Regulation of the National Fisheries Administration Commission (RECNAP). This Regulation, consisting of three Chapters, under Fisheries Law No. 22/2013, establishes, composition, duties and responsibilities of the National Fisheries Administration Commission (CNAP). The CNAP is the consultative body of the system of participatory management of fisheries resources at the central level, in which all interest groups involved are represented. The purpose of CNAP is to coordinate efforts for the protection, conservation and sustainable and responsible use of fishery resources and respective ecosystems. In particular CNAP is responsible to give its opinion on matters relating to: a) fisheries and aquaculture development policies and strategies; b) establishment and implementation of fisheries and aquaculture management measures; c) measures for the management of aquaculture, fishing activities and complementary to fishing; d) state of exploitation of fishery resources; e) strategies and mechanisms for monitoring, controlling and inspecting fishing and aquaculture activities; f) strategies for preventing and combating marine, river, lake and ecosystem pollution, including coastal areas.

Policy: Climate Change Act (No. 43 of 2021).
Policy_Content: This Act lays down a detailed framework for a whole of government approach to addressing the climate emergency in Fiji. The objectives of this Act are: (I) the development and implementation of long-term climate change measures and policies; (II) effective implementation of UNFCCC, Paris Agreement and its Nationally Determined Contribution to meet its international obligations; (III) the achievement of regional commitments and aspirations relating to climate change including the Suva Declaration on Climate Change; (IV) establishment of institutional and governance structures for the implementation of this Act; (V) the evidence-based consideration of climate change issues in specified areas of government and private sector decision-making; (VI) articulation of risk reduction responsibilities and formulation of resilience-building objectives across all sector plans and strategies; (VII) integration of climate change considerations into related policies with a gender sensitive and socially inclusive manner; (VIII) establishment of a transparent framework for the monitoring, reporting and verification of anthropogenic emissions by sources and anthropogenic removals by sinks of greenhouse gases; (IX) establishment of data management systems and the publicly accessible Information Platform to enhance government transparency and enable informed private and civil sector decision-making and risk management; (X) reduction of greenhouse gas emissions consistently in the long term; the implementation, operation and administration of regulations, measures and actions to provide for a strategic response to the climate-related emergencies; (XI) the development of emissions reduction projects, programs and activities and access to international carbon markets; (XII) enhancement of adaptive capacity to the impacts of climate change with respect to the communities, environment and ecosystems; (XIII) the relocation of at-risk communities and safeguard their rights; (XIV) conservation of oceans and enhancing their ability to respond to the adverse impacts of climate change; (XV) safeguarding Fiji’s national security and sovereignty including with respect to Fiji’s sovereignty over its maritime zones such as internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial seas, contiguous zone and exclusive economic zone within the meaning of UNCLOS and in the alignment with the Declaration on Preserving Maritime Zones in the Face of Climate Change Related Sea Level Rise; (XVI) establishment of a framework for securing nationally and internationally derived finance for the implementation of this Act; and (XVII) financial measures against the impacts of climate change on the business environment. This Act recognizes that climate change is a threat to the rights and freedoms recognized in Chapter 2 of the Constitution, including the right to a clean and healthy environment and the right to adequate food and water. To this end, this Act underlines that while taking action to address climate change, Fiji will respect, promote and consider the sustainable development goals, gender equality and responsiveness, women’s human rights and the empowerment of women, rights of people living with disabilities and disability inclusive approaches, the elderly, children’s inalienable right to a healthy environment, youth, and vulnerable and marginalized groups and communities, including in the areas of formal sector employment and livelihoods, participation in decision-making and access to services, health, education, water, sanitation, housing and transport.

Policy: Federal Decree-Law No.33 of 2021 regarding the Regulation of Employment Relationship.
Policy_Content: This Decree, consisting of 74 articles, aims at (i) ensuring the efficiency of the UAE labor market by supporting the attraction and retention of future skills and talents and providing an attractive business environment for employers; (ii) regulating employment relationships and defining the rights and obligations of the parties; (iii) enhancing the flexibility and sustainability of the UAE labor market; (iv) improving the capabilities and skills of workers in the private sector, in a manner that enhances the efficiency and productivity of the Emirates' workforce; (v) providing protection to both parties to the employment relationship and enabling them to obtain their rights. The provisions of the Decree apply to all establishments, employers, and workers in the UAE private sector. Government workers, employees of the armed forces, police and security, and domestic workers are therefore excluded. Article 4 regards Equality and Non-discrimination provision and bans any discrimination based on race, color, sex, religion, national or social origin, or disability which would have the effect of nullifying or impairing equality of opportunity, or prejudicing equal treatment in the employment, the maintenance of a job, and the enjoyment of its benefits. The article establishes also that (i) rules and regulations that aim to enhance the participation of UAE citizens in the labor market shall not constitute discrimination; (ii) all provisions regulating the employment of workers without discrimination, shall apply to working women; (iii) a woman is granted a wage equal to the wages of a man if she performs the same work or an alternative work of equal value. Further measures in favor of female work are those contained in Article 30 on maternity leave which regulates absences from work (with full, half, or no wage) after the birth of the child and breaks per day to breastfeed. Furthermore, article 14 adds that the employer shall not use any means that would oblige or force the worker, threaten him with any penalty to work for it, or compel him to undertake work or provide a service against his will, and prohibits any sexual harassment, bullying, or any verbal, physical, or psychological violence committed against the worker by the employer, his superiors at work, colleagues or the persons who work with him.

Policy: Law on packaging and packaging waste management.
Policy_Content: This Law regulates the requirements for protection of environment and human health that should be met by packaging during production, placing on the market and handling of packaging waste that covers the obligations of economic operators and other entities participating in related processes. This text defines necessary procedural rules and obligations as regards the production and placing on the market of packaging, requirements for collection, reuse, processing, recycling and disposal, as well as other conditions for handling packaging waste, reporting and economic instruments for achieving the objectives of collection, processing and recycling of such packaging. Main goals of this Law are: reduction of the negative impact of packaging and packaging waste on environment and human health; promotion of environmental protection standards by economic operators during the life cycle of packaging, and in particular treatment, reuse, processing and disposal of packaging waste. In addition to these basic objectives, the following goals should be achieved: to prevent the generation of packaging waste; to reduce and limit the use of harmful metals and substances and other toxins substances in the packaging, and thus achieve a reduction in the toxicity of the waste from packaging; to achieve a separate collection of packaging waste at its place creation; to achieve a high level of reuse, recycling and other types of processing of packaging waste, thereby reducing the disposal of wastes deriving from packaging; to provide favorable conditions for the establishment and development of the market of related reuse, recycling and other ways of processing of packaging waste; to ensure the functioning of the market without barriers to trade and ensuring an equal position on the market of domestic and foreign legal entities and individuals, as well as avoiding trade barriers that may disrupt the necessary market competition; to reduce energy consumption and use of primary raw materials in the production of packaging and encouraging the treatment of packaging waste; to encourage the use of the best available treatment technologies, processing and recycling of packaging waste; to encourage the production of reusable packaging that is biodegradable. The packaging in terms of its convenience for processing of materials that are used, should meet the following requirements: 1) packaging that can be recycled through recycling operations made in such a way that when it becomes packaging waste it will be possible to recycle a certain weight percentage of materials used in the manufacture of the product that are intended for sale, in accordance with applicable standards (determining this percentage may vary depending on the type of material of the package); 2) packaging that can be processed through energy operation processing, when it becomes packaging waste should have a minimum caloric value to enable optimal energy production; 3) packaging that can be processed through composting operations, must be made in such a way that when it becomes packaging waste there is biodegradable property that will not interfere with the individual collection and processing of composting or other activity in which it is involved; 4) packaging produced from biodegradable materials must be made in such a way that when it becomes packaging waste it is of such nature that it can be subjected to physical, chemical, thermal or biological decomposition so that most of the final compost will decompose into carbon dioxide, biomass and water. In terms of this point, oxo-degradable plastic packaging is not considered biodegradable.

Policy_Content: This Resolution approves the increase in the number of beneficiary families of conditional Social Monetary Transfers, through the so-called “Vulnerable Families Programme” of the Social Protection - regular PFV for 4,500 households. Policy_Content: La presente Ley es de orden público e interés social y tiene por objeto fomentar la creación, promoción y desarrollo de la agricultura familiar. Son finalidades de la presente Ley: I. Procurar el bienestar social y económico de las unidades de producción familiar, reducir la pobreza del sector rural y orientar la acción coordinada de los organismos competentes con un enfoque multisectorial e intergubernamental; II. Contribuir al ejercicio pleno del derecho humano a una alimentación adecuada y suficiente, al desarrollo integral de las personas, familias y comunidades y al sostenimiento de las pautas culturales y recursos naturales de cada región del estado; III. Desarrollar la agricultura familiar a través del uso de conocimientos, tecnología y buenas prácticas, respetando la cultura, las tradiciones y los hábitos de las comunidades agrícolas, contribuyan al crecimiento y desarrollo de las personas y unidades familiares, especialmente de aquellas que se encuentren en situación de vulnerabilidad; IV. Fortalecer la producción agrícola familiar rural a partir del derecho al acceso equitativo a todos los recursos naturales y su uso sustentable, respetando los derechos de las comunidades y pueblos indígenas; y V. Coadyuvar con la suficiencia autoalimentaria de los núcleos familiares rurales, con el derecho a una efectiva y justa retribución por los excedentes y demás productos que comercialicen.

Policy: Law No. ZRU-713 “On ensuring seismic safety of the population and territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan”.
Policy_Content: The scope of this Law is to regulate relations in the field of ensuring seismic safety of the population and the territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Seismic safety shall be intended the state of life security of the population and infrastructure facilities by state bodies and organizations in the field of seismic safety from the dangers caused by earthquakes. Seismic safety facilities by importance are classified into the following categories: I category - objects with a low hazard factor; Category II - objects with an average hazard factor; Category III - objects with a high hazard factor; Category IV - objects with a very high hazard factor. The list of seismic safety facilities by category is determined in accordance with the annex to this Law. The main directions of state policy in the field of ensuring seismic safety are: (a) improvement of the legal framework for providing seismic safety; (b) taking measures to improve the level of seismic safety; (c) monitoring and control of seismic resistance of buildings and facilities in operation, as well as leased into operation; (d) instrumental seismological  and seismometric observations on reservoirs located on the national territory; (e) monitoring the seismic resistance of reservoirs and other hydraulic structures located on the national territory; (f) introduction of modern information and communication technologies in this field; (g) improvement of scientific foundations and technologies for providing seismic safety; (h) implementation by state bodies of measures aimed at reducing harm to health and life of people and property of the population, as well as the risk of losses (material, economic and other) as a result of earthquakes; (i) development of research work and implementation in practice of modern methods of seismic hazard prediction, seismic risk and the probability of occurrence of earthquakes, as well as strengthening the seismic resistance of structures; and (j) development of international cooperation in this area. Natural and legal persons have the right to: (a) receive complete and reliable information about the level of seismic hazard in the relevant territory; (b) receive information about the rules of conduct in case of earthquakes and how to prepare for them; and (c) if necessary, to involve specialists to protect personnel and organization and teaching thereof for correct behavior during earthquakes. This Law contains V Chapters divided into 26 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II regards state regulation in the field of ensuring seismic safety. Chapter III regards organization of activity in the field of ensuring seismic safety. Chapter IV establishes rights and obligations of natural and legal persons in the field of ensuring seismic safety. Chapter V lays down final provisions.

Policy: Resolution of the Council of Ministers No. 120/2021 approving the action plan of the National Strategy for the Sea 2021-2030.
Policy_Content: This Resolution of the Council of Ministers approves the action plan of the National Strategy for the Sea 2021-2030. The Council of Ministers Resolution No. 68/2021 of 4 June approved the National Strategy for the Sea 2021-2030 (ENM 2021-2030), which is the main guiding legislation for maritime policies in Portugal. The ENM 2021-2030 aligns its guiding principles with the 2030 Agenda for sustainable development of the United Nations, with the European Ecological Pact, with the Integrated Maritime Policy of the European Union (EU), with the Common Fisheries Policy and with subsidiary policies, namely, the EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030, the Prado à Prato Strategy and the Estrelado-Sea Mission 2030: Recovering our Ocean and Waters, recently presented by the European Commission. Additionally, similarly to the EU's Integrated Maritime Policy, ENM 2021-2030 incorporates all areas and sectors related to sustainable management and the economy of the sea. The action plan of ENM 2021-2030 includes 185 measures, 30 of which are considered emblematic due to their scope and high potential for multiplying effects. Some of these cover the following areas: Combat climate change and environmental pollution and protect ecosystems; Convert national fisheries by 2030 into one of the most sustainable low-impact sectors in the world, stimulating the allocation of subsidies to promote sustainable fisheries and the conservation of the marine environment; Investing sustainable food security; Facilitate access to drinking water; Promote health and well-being, etc.

Policy_Content: This Regulation defines the procedure for the organization and activity of the Commission of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy for the compensation of losses from completely lost (destroyed) agricultural crops as a result of man-made and natural emergencies to agricultural producers - legal entities regardless of their organizational and legal form and form of ownership and natural persons - entrepreneurs, whose crops have been completely lost as a result of man-made and natural emergency situations. The main task of the Commission is to process the summary information of subsidy recipients received from the regional commissions, and to carry out by November 15 of the current year, taking into account the available budget allocations, according to the relevant direction, the proportional distribution of budget funds for the provision of subsidies to each recipient, which is approved by the order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy. Decisions of the Commission are adopted at its meetings in the presence of not less than two-thirds of its members by open voting by a simple majority of votes. In the case of an equal distribution of votes, the vote of the chairperson at the meeting is decisive. Decisions of the Commission are formalized in a protocol, which is signed by all members of the Commission present at the meeting, and approved by an order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy. A member of the Commission who does not agree with its decision signs the protocol with a separate opinion, which is an integral part of the protocol. Annex 1 contains application form for receiving a subsidy to agricultural producers through state support for compensation for losses from completely lost (destroyed) agricultural crops of as a result of man-made and natural emergencies. Annex 2 contains the form of the act of inspection of agricultural crops for compensation of losses from completely lost (destroyed) agricultural crops as a result of man-made and natural emergency situations. Annex 3 contains the form of the act on the write-off of agricultural crops. Annex 4 contains the form of summary information of recipients who have the right to receive state support for compensation for losses from completely lost (destroyed) agricultural crops as a result of man-made and natural emergencies.

Policy_Content: The Regulations on the organization and functioning of the Ministry of the Environment regulate the mission, functions, areas of activity and rights, as well as the organization of its activities. Policy: Loi no 2021-1104 du 22 août 2021 portant lutte contre le dérèglement climatique et renforcement de la résilience face à ses effets
Policy_Content: En cohérence avec l’accord de Paris adopté le 12 décembre 2015 et ratifié le 5 octobre 2016, et dans le cadre du Pacte vert pour l’Europe, l’Etat rappelle son engagement à respecter les objectifs de réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre, tels qu’ils résulteront notamment de la révision prochaine du règlement (UE) 2018/842 du Parlement européen et du Conseil du 30 mai 2018 relatif aux réductions annuelles contraignantes des émissions de gaz à effet de serre par les Etats membres de 2021 à 2030 contribuant à l’action pour le climat, afin de respecter les engagements pris dans le cadre de l’accord de Paris et modifiant le règlement (UE) no 525/2013. Entre autres, la loi règlemente affichage de l’impact environnemental des biens et services ; publicité sur les produits et services ayant un impact excessif sur le climat ; accélérer le développement de la vente en vrac et de la consigne du verre ; outils de bricolage et de jardinage motorisés ; articles de sport et de loisirs, bicyclettes à assistance électrique et engins de déplacement personnel motorisés ; adapter l’emploi à la transition écologique ; protéger les écosystèmes et la diversité biologique ; principes généraux de la protection des sols et des sous-sols ; principes régissant le modèle minier français ; politique nationale des ressources et des usages du sous-sol pour une gestion minière durable ; substances soumises à un régime particulier ; favoriser les énergies renouvelables ; les certificats de production de biogaz ; promouvoir les alternatives à l’usage individuel de la voiture et la transition vers un parc de véhicules plus respectueux de l’environnement ; infrastructure collective de recharge dans les immeubles collectifs ; améliorer le transport routier de marchandises et réduire ses émissions ; développer le fret ferroviaire et fluvial ; limiter les émissions du transport aérien et favoriser l’intermodalité entre le train et l’avion ; réductions d’émissions issues de projets de compensation des émissions de gaz à effet de serre ; compensation des émissions de gaz à effet de serre des vols effectués à l’intérieur du territoire national ; rénover les bâtiments ; diminuer la consommation d’énergie ; lutter contre l’artificialisation des sols en adaptant les règles d’urbanisme ; artificialisation des sols ; lutter contre l’artificialisation des sols pour la protection des écosystèmes ; interdiction des atterrissages à des fins de loisirs ; adapter les territoires aux effets du dérèglement climatique ; droit de préemption pour l’adaptation des territoires au recul du trait de côte ; soutenir une alimentation saine et durable pour tous peu émettrice de gaz à effet de serre ; développer l’agroécologie ; information sur la saisonnalité des fruits et légumes frais ; renforcer la protection judiciaire de l’environnement ; des atteintes générales aux milieux physiques ; conseil supérieur de la prévention des risques technologiques et enquêtes techniques ; et dispositions relatives à l’évaluation climatique et environnementale.

Policy: Order No. 1766 of the Ministry of Health validating the Procedure for carrying out epidemiological surveillance of antimicrobial resistance.
Policy_Content: This Procedure defines the mechanism for organizing epidemiological surveillance of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) of invasive pathogens, their interaction with each other in the process of its implementation, and the transfer of information to the Ministry of Health and health care institutions for the development of measures to combat the spread of microorganisms with resistance. It is intended for medical workers of health care institutions and natural persons - entrepreneurs who have received a license for the right to conduct economic activity from medical practice, as well as for public health institutions. Coordination, organizational-methodical and informational advisory support for the implementation of sentinel epidemiological surveillance of antimicrobial resistance is entrusted to the state institution "Public Health Center of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine". Epidemiological surveillance of AMR shall be intended a systematic ongoing process of data collection and analysis for quantitative assessment of the prevalence of AMR and its dynamics over time. The obtained epidemiological data, depending on the level and nature of resistance, should be used for: (a) assessment of time trends, forecasting the probability of occurrence and spread of AMR, taking into account its mechanisms, ways of transmission, species affiliation of microorganisms with AMR, nosological forms of infectious diseases, caused by them, risk factors and characteristics of patients that contribute to the emergence of infectious diseases caused by microorganisms with AMR, their consequences for the patient and the health care system (for example, ineffectiveness of therapy, prolongation of hospitalization, increased cost of treatment); (b) informing the authorities of the health care system at the appropriate level about the situation, with the aim of developing a strategy to curb the spread of AMR and carrying out appropriate measures; (c) implementation of technologies, procedures and methods for the timely and reliable detection of microorganisms with AMR into the work practice of microbiological/bacteriological laboratories; (d) update of recommendations on empiric antimicrobial therapy, changes of standards of clinical protocols; and (e) integration of data into the system of epidemiological surveillance of resistance to antimicrobial drugs in Central Asia and Europe and into the system of global monitoring of resistance to antimicrobial drugs.

Policy_Content: This Regional Decree establishes the procedure for collection and exchange of information in the field of protecting the regional population and the territory from natural and man-made emergencies. Collection and exchange of information shall be performed by the authorized regional territorial bodies and municipal authorities in the field of protection of the regional population against natural and man-made emergencies and disasters. Policy: Royal Decree No. M/3 of 2021 issuing the Waste Management System.
Policy_Content: This Law consisting of 38 articles divided into X Chapters aims at regulating the transport, segregation, storage, import, export, safe disposal of waste, and all other activities related to it, including aftercare of waste disposal sites and it does not apply to radioactive, nuclear, and military waste. The regulatory authority is the National Waste Management Center (NWMC) which (i) issues the licenses for engaging in any activity related to waste management; (ii) has the right to dispose of waste in a manner that achieves financial sustainability and covers the operational costs of the competent authorities that may dispose of the waste after the approval of the Center; (iii) prepares the comprehensive strategic plan for waste management in coordination with the relevant authorities, and successively each competent authority shall develop operational plans for waste management that are compatible with the comprehensive strategic plan; (iv) prepares contingency plans.

Policy: Order MMA No. 414 establishing the Floresta+ Bioeconomy modality, under Order MMA No. 288 of 2 July 2020.
Policy_Content: This Order creates the Floresta+ Bioeconomy modality under the Order MMA No. 288 creating the National Programme for Environmental Services Payment (Floresta+), which will promote: recognition of the direct contribution of sustainable forestry management activities, whether timber or non-timber, for the protection of forests; the creation of commercial arrangements and encouragement of innovation to highlight, recognize and remunerate the environmental services performed by those who work in forest conservation; encouraging timber and non-timber forest production from native forests in Brazil, fostering innovation, structuring and development of this chain through Payment for Environmental Services; the incentive to pay for monitoring, conservation and recovery activities of native vegetation, enabling the guarantee of income, generating stability and incentives for the maintenance of forest areas; and entrepreneurial actions that have the potential to enhance the market for payments for environmental services. The Floresta+ Bioeconomy modality has as a guideline to encourage the bioeconomy focused on payment for the provision of environmental services, understood as a set of activities for the improvement, recovery, monitoring and conservation of native vegetation in all biomes. The strategic objectives of the Floresta+ Bioeconomy modality are: I - prospect reports, and research already available that demonstrate potential opportunities for the biomes, as well as carry out complementary diagnoses and analyzes to enrich the mapping of opportunities for the bioeconomy; II - mobilize, qualify and integrate agents of the bioeconomy, impacting sustainable regional development through payment for environmental services; III – encourage the registration of bioeconomy projects on the Floresta+ Platform to facilitate access by interested parties to financial resources originating from international cooperation, financing, aiming at boosting the bioeconomy; IV - foster the development of a bioeconomy component within the Floresta+ Programme Digital Platform; and V - recognize initiatives that generate added value to sustainable forest management activities, whether timber or non-timber.

Policy: Order No. 541 of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Natural Resources validating the Procedure for burning dry vegetation or its remains.
Policy_Content: This Order defines the main provisions regarding the burning of dry vegetation or its remains on the territory of Ukraine. In this Order, the terms are used in the following sense: (a) burning of dry vegetation is the controlled burning of vegetation cover on land plots, which leads to its destruction; (b) burning the remains of dry vegetation - burning specially collected planting material in places designated for this purpose; (c) dry vegetation - a set of plant organisms with a dead aerial part on a certain area of their natural growth, including after mowing; and (d) plant cover - a set of plant communities in a certain area. Burning the remains of dry vegetation is allowed in the following cases: (a) for cooking (in the oven, on the barbecue or with the help of other equipment), heating the house (firewood, brushwood, briquettes); and (b) for traditional and cultural purposes (fire on Ivan Kupala, etc.). Such burning is carried out after prior agreement of the place and time with local self-government bodies. It is forbidden to carry out any burning in windy weather, except for burning the remains of dry vegetation in closed rooms.

Policy: Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 2021.
Policy_Content: This Nationally Determined Contribution is a nationwide sectoral document that updates the NDC of 2015 by enhancing ambition by the State of Qatar towards reducing its overall emissions in response to the guidance set forth in Article 4.4 of the Paris Agreement. Qatar intends to reduce 25% of its GHG emissions by the year 2030. The document is intended for the following sectors: Energy including transport and downstream industries; building and construction industry, water management, waste, and infrastructure. To maintain development and sustainable growth, a national vision was adopted to diversify the economy. The key areas for diversification with mitigation co-benefits are as follows (i) Oil and Gas, to enhance energy efficiency as a key measure to reduce GHG emissions; (ii) Power and Water, to continue creating awareness over the issue of water and energy wastage, especially among the youth, and in reducing consumption of electricity and water per capita; (iii) transportation; (iv) Building, Construction and Industry to achieve a circular economy in the sectors by implementing recycling and re-using construction waste; (v) Research and Development focusing on key topics of sustainability in Qatar’s energy sector and in management of environmental, food and water resources and the impact of climate change on them; (vi) Education as a key player in the steering and implementation of the national long-term climate change strategies via research, technology development, policies and regulatory frameworks, monitoring, measurements, evaluation, and incentive schemes; and (vii) Tourism.

Policy: Law No. ZRU-706 “On transport”.
Policy_Content: This Law regulates relations in the field of transport. Transport activities shall be intended activities related to the implementation of organizational and technological operations for the transportation and servicing of passengers, baggage, cargo luggage, cargo, postal and courier shipments by road, rail, air, water or a combination of these modes of transport and other services performed on a contractual basis or other legal grounds. The main principles of transport activity are: (a) legality; (b) safety; (c) environmental friendliness; (d) availability and accessibility of transport services; (e) openness and transparency. The authorized state body, its territorial subdivisions, subordinate organizations are bodies of state supervision in the field of transport, which exercise state supervision over safety of navigation and operation of ships in accordance with their designation. Licensing and authorization procedures in the field of transport are used to protect the interests of clients of transport services, transport security, compliance with environmental, sanitary-epidemiological and other requirements. Transport organizations and carriers are required to plan, organize and finance environmental activities, conduct departmental and production control in the field of environmental protection and subsoil, ensure compliance with established norms for the protection of the environment and subsoil, rational use of natural resources and other criteria, regulating the maximum permissible loads on the environment and subsoil. For damage caused to the environment and subsoil, transport organizations and carriers are liable in the manner established by law.

Policy: Decreto-Ley Nº 50 - Sobre la conservación, mejoramiento y manejo sostenible de los suelos y el uso de los fertilizantes.
Policy_Content: El presente Decreto-Ley tiene por objeto establecer las regulaciones generales para la conservación, el mejoramiento y el manejo sostenible de los suelos agropecuarios y forestales y el uso de los fertilizantes. El marco regulatorio para la conservación, el mejoramiento y el manejo sostenible de los suelos y el uso de los fertilizantes se rige por los principios siguientes: a) Sostenibilidad: constituye un deber del Estado y de toda persona natural o jurídica asegurar el manejo sostenible de los suelos agropecuarios y forestales, su fertilidad y el uso integrado de los fertilizantes, de manera tal que no comprometa la seguridad alimentaria de las presentes y futuras generaciones; b) prevención: evitar los efectos negativos que se puedan producir en los suelos mediante la adopción de medidas en correspondencia con la naturaleza del suelo y los estudios científico técnicos; c) progresividad: el manejo sostenible de los suelos y el uso de los fertilizantes se logra de forma gradual, a través de metas intermedias y finales; d) responsabilidad: el generador de efectos degradantes en los suelos es responsable de los costos de las acciones preventivas y correctivas de rehabilitación; e) subsidiariedad: el Estado, a través de las distintas instancias de la administración pública, tiene la obligación de colaborar y, de ser necesario, participar en forma complementaria en el accionar de las personas naturales y jurídicas para la preservación y protección del suelo; y f) cooperación: el manejo sostenible de los suelos y el uso de los fertilizantes es una actividad intersectorial en la que deben actuar de forma cooperada las empresas, las formas no estatales de producción, los centros de educación media y superior, los institutos de ciencia, tecnología e innovación, el Estado Mayor Nacional de la Defensa Civil, las organizaciones no gubernamentales, los medios de difusión y cada uno de los ciudadanos, en su marco de actuación.

Policy: Decree No. 499 of the Cabinet of Ministers “On comprehensive measures to prevent reduction of vegetative cover in mountain and foothills around the Charvak reservoir.”
Policy_Content: In landscapes around the Charvak Reservoir, vegetation cover has been declining sharply over the last decade as a result of climate change. This process affects the strength of the soil layer and causes the amount of dust to rise rapidly into the air. In the context of global climate change, the number of recurrences of dangerous meteorological processes is characterized by rising dust and sand particles from the ground under the influence of strong winds in spring and summer and moving horizontally and vertically in its atmosphere, reducing visibility to 500 meters and causing air pollution. The scope of this Decree shall be to prevent deforestation of mountainous and foothill areas around the Charvak Reservoir, limiting anthropogenic factors affecting the reduction of vegetation cover, mitigating the negative impact of natural factors and climate change on the health of the population and creating the necessary environment for recreation with a view of increasing the tourist attractiveness of mountainous areas. The Government resolves to approve the Program of complex measures for the prevention of reduction of vegetation cover in the Charvak reservoir and the surrounding mountainous and foothill areas setting forth the following objectives: (a) to increase the number of local species of trees and shrubs in order to prevent deforestation of mountain and foothill areas and land erosion; (b) establishment of shelter trees to mitigate the effects of strong winds and dust storms; (c) regulation of livestock grazing areas and waste zones; (d) organization of large-scale scientific research aimed at studying the systemic factors influencing the reduction of vegetation cover; (e) ecology and environmental protection, public health; and (f) implementation of complex measures aimed at landscaping.

El Gobierno nacional, a través del Ministerio de Minas y Energía y sus entidades adscritas, dictará normas que garanticen el abastecimiento y la confiabilidad en el suministro de gas combustible en el mercado, como eje de la transición energética. Para efectos de incrementar la oferta, establecerá mecanismos que viabilicen y promuevan la producción nacional, siguiendo criterios de eficiencia, seguridad energética y responsabilidad ambiental. Para ello tendrá en cuenta la implementación de nuevas tecnologías e infraestructura disponibles que garanticen la protección del medio ambiente. No obstante, para garantizar el abastecimiento de la demanda potencial, los costos de la infraestructura de regasificación e importación que sea impulsada por el Gobierno nacional a través del Plan de Abastecimiento de Gas Natural y GLP serían asumidos por la demanda que se beneficie de la misma. Policy: Ley N⁰ 2138 - Por medio de la cual se establecen medidas para la sustitución de vehículos de tracción animal en el territorio nacional y se dictan otras disposiciones.
Policy_Content: La presente ley tiene por objeto la creación de una normatividad tendiente a establecer parámetros para la sustitución de vehículos de tracción animal y la consagración de medidas que propenden por el bienestar de los animales, pertenecientes a las familias de los équidos y bóvidos que son utilizados para este fin, así como ofrecer las garantías necesarias para que las personas que derivan el sustento de este tipo de vehículos puedan acceder a programas de reconversión sociolaboral. Las autoridades distritales, municipales y departamentales en cuyos territorios circulen vehículos de tracción animal deberán iniciar programas de sustitución. Quedan exceptuados de esta medida los vehículos de tracción animal destinados a: actividades turísticas, agrícolas, pecuarias, forestales y deportivas. Se establecen normas sobre la financiación de los programas de sustitución de vehículos de tracción animal. La sustitución de vehículos de tracción animal deberá hacerse por vehículos automotores listos para circular, nuevos y homologados para transporte de carga. Se regulan los requisitos de los beneficiarios de la sustitución de vehículos de tracción animal. Durante el tiempo de proceso de sustitución, el propietario deberá velar porque el equino esté en buenas condiciones físicas y de salud. El animal deberá estar sano o ser recuperado en materia de salud y zoonosis, y deberá cumplir con el protocolo de adopción implementado, para que sea entregado a un adoptante diferente a su dueño inicial, quien deberá cumplir con requisitos básicos como tener un predio propio para la tenencia y contar con recursos para el mantenimiento del animal. Una vez concluido el proceso de sustitución contemplado en esta ley, no podrán circular vehículos de tracción animal por las vías del territorio nacional.

Policy_Content: This Order is drafted in light of government's policy to ensure the sustainable utilization, development, management, protection and conservation of the country’s forest and other natural resources including Non-Timber Forest Products. This Order aims to encourage the establishment of bamboo plantations and to promote the sustainable use of bamboo as wood substitute in support of the development of bamboo-based industries in the Philippines. This Order shall cover all naturally grown bamboo stands, backyard farms and plantations found within forest lands, agricultural lands (alienable and disposable), mineral lands, private titled lands, and ancestral lands. The text further provides for establishment of Bamboo plantations, registration of Bamboo plantation and backyard farms, required documents and process, applicable fee, certification and grounds for suspension/cancellation of certificate, monitoring and provision of incentives to Bamboo plantation development owners and Bamboo processing enterprises. The text consists of 21 Articles and has 3 attachments.

Policy: Resolution No. 26 of 2021 subjecting table grapes, apples, citrus fruits and almonds to tests for pesticide residues after the picking process or in packaging centers.
Policy_Content: This Resolution, comprising 14 articles, mandates that exporters or farmers intending to export products such as grapes, apples, almonds, and citrus fruits must register with internationally accredited control companies approved by the Ministry of Agriculture. These approved companies will collect samples of the goods, whether packed in the field or packaging centers, and send them to a laboratory accredited by the Ministry of Agriculture. The laboratory will conduct pesticide residue analyses on the samples and provide the results within a maximum period of four working days. An official product conformity certificate for pesticide deposit tests will be issued to the interested party for goods intended for export. Export of the specified products without the accompanying certificate of conformity is prohibited. Export of products is allowed if they do not exceed the permitted percentages of pesticide residues outlined in the standards issued by the European Union. If the analysis results indicate the presence of pesticides not registered with the Ministry of Agriculture, the laboratory conducting the analysis will notify the drug control committees in the relevant regions, and appropriate procedures will be implemented. Article 12 establishes a technical committee responsible for creating a unified operational mechanism with internationally accredited monitoring companies, following the provisions outlined in this Resolution.

Policy: Ley N⁰ 2111/2021 por medio del cual se sustituye el título XI “De los delitos contra los recursos naturales y el medio ambiente” de la Ley 599 de 2000 (Código Penal), se modifica la Ley 906 de 2004 y se dictan otras disposiciones.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley modifica la normativa sobre los delitos contra los recursos naturales y el medio ambiente del Código Penal, expedido por la Ley Nº 599 del 2000. Se define delitos contra los recursos naturales: aprovechamiento ilícito de los recursos naturales renovables, tráfico de Fauna, caza ilegal, pesca ilegal, manejo ilícito de especies exóticas, deforestación, promoción y financiación de la deforestación, manejo y uso ilícito de organismos genéticamente modificados, microrganismo y sustancias o elementos peligrosos, y la explotación ilícita del yacimiento minero y otros materiales. Además, se definen los delitos de los daños en los recursos naturales y ecocidio. También se definen los delitos de contaminación ambiental, contaminación ambiental por explotación de yacimiento minero o hidrocarburo y la experimentación ilegal con especies, agentes biológicos o bioquímicos, la invasión de áreas de especial importancia ecológica, financiación de invasión a áreas de especial importancia ecológica, apropiación ilegal de baldíos de la nación, y la financiación de la apropiación ilegal de los baldíos de la nación. Se define cuándo aplica la agravación punitiva y la modalidad culposa. Se crea en la fiscalía general de la Nación, la Dirección de Apoyo Territorial adscrito a la delegada para la Seguridad Ciudadana, la que tendrá como función principal liderar la estrategia de apoyo regional de la Fiscalía General de la Nación, con miras a aumentar la presencia efectiva de la Entidad con un trabajo interdisciplinario en territorios apartados o de difícil acceso. Se definen las funciones del Apoyo Territorial. Se crea la Dirección Especializada para los Delitos contra los Recursos Naturales y el Medio Ambiente en la fiscalía general de la Nación.

Policy: Decision on declaring the project "Hydropower system Kosinj" a strategic investment project of the Republic of Croatia.
Policy_Content: This Decision, based on the provisions of the Law on strategic investment projects of the Republic of Croatia, upon the received proposal from the Commission for the evaluation and determination of strategic project proposals, declares the project entitled "Hydropower system Kosinj" as a strategic investment project of the Republic of Croatia. This project (public investment) includes the construction of the Kosinj Reservoir with Kosinj, Sedlo and Bakovac dams, injection curtains, Kosinj hydropower plants with accompanying facilities, reconstruction of the existing Sklope hydropower plant, construction of replacement roads and connection to the electricity transmission network. The goal and effects of this project are to increase electricity production. The construction of the Kosinj Reservoir is expected to increase the level of utilization of water quantities in the Lika and Gacka rivers by reducing overflow losses. This achieves a high level of flood protection in the downstream area, Lipovo polje and Kosinj valley, which in the current flood conditions almost every year.

Policy: Law No. 3.804 providing for the environmental licensing in the State of Tocantins.
Policy_Content: This Law establishes general standards for the licensing of activities or enterprises that use environmental resources, which are actually or potentially polluting or capable, in any form, of causing degradation to the environment, in accordance with art. 10 of Federal Law No. 6.938 of 31 August 1981. It applies to environmental licensing carried out before the bodies of the municipalities that are part of the National Environmental System (SISNAMA), observing the attributions established in Federal Complementary Law No. 140 of 8 December 2011. The principles of environmental licensing are: public participation, transparency and social control; precaution; preponderance of public interest; speed and procedural economy; prevention of environmental damage, mitigation and compensation of environmental impacts, to be adopted in that order within the scope of the analysis of environmental impacts; integrated analysis of environmental impacts and risks; maximized use of computer systems and electronic monitoring; standardization of standards, analysis procedures and information systems to be adopted by the state agency and municipal environmental bodies as a measure of equality for entrepreneurs and enterprises in the State of Tocantins, respecting regional differences; user-pays and polluter-pays; promotion of sustainable socioeconomic development in the State of Tocantins; compliance with ecological and economic zoning indications; analysis of the synergistic impact of individual ventures; respect the indications of the Management Plans for Environmental Protection Areas; integration and linking of environmental licensing acts with the control instruments provided for in state policies for water resources, protection of native vegetation, and the state system of conservation units; the responsibility for environmental damage, of the entrepreneurs and those responsible for the project. The construction, installation, expansion and operation of enterprises and activities that use environmental resources, which are actually or potentially polluting or capable, in any form, of causing environmental degradation will depend on prior environmental licensing.

Policy: Regional Law No. 194 “On the organization of environmental education and the formation of ecological culture”.
Policy_Content: This Regional Law establishes legal foundations for the organization and development of environmental education and formation of ecological culture in the regional territory, and defines the powers of the regional bodies of state power in this field. Environmental education shall be intended dissemination of knowledge about environmental security, environmental information and use of natural resources in order to form the foundations of ecological culture, as well as informing the population about legislation in the field of environmental protection and environmental security. Ecological culture is an integral part of the universal culture, including moral values, norms of behavior, ways of interactions between people in the field of environmental protection, manifested in environmentally oriented behavior of people, awareness of personal and overall responsibility for the quality of the environment and high social importance of preventing the negative anthropogenic impact on environment. Main objectives of environmental education and formation of ecological culture shall be as follows: (a) improving environmental culture, educational level of the regional population, including improvement of professional skills and knowledge in the field environmental protection and environmental security; (b) formation of respect for the nature of the region; and (c) preservation of a favorable environment, biological diversity and natural resources. Regional state policy in the field of  environmental education and the formation of environmental culture shall be based on the following principles: (a) creating favorable  environmental education and the formation of environmental culture; (b) universality, consistency, complexity and continuity of environmental education; (c) focus on environmental education and ecological awareness for solving problems to improve the quality of life and health of citizens, preservation and restoration of the environment, resource-saving nature management; (d) openness and availability of information about the state of the environment; (e) consistency of actions of regional state authorities, bodies of local self-government, educational organizations, public associations, non-profit organizations and citizens;(e) consideration of regional characteristics, including natural conditions and resources, ecological situation, demographic situation, cultural and historical traditions of the regional population in the implementation of the regional state policy in the field environmental education and formation of ecological culture; (f) the use of historical experience in solving environmental problems of environmental education, as well as the experience of other constituent entities of the Russian Federation and foreign states; and (g) international environmental cooperation in the field of environmental education and environmental awareness in various forms.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. PP-5200 “On additional measures for the introduction of the cluster system in the development of viticulture, state support for attracting advanced technologies in this field.”

Policy: Petroleum Commission Act - Act no. 13 of 2021.
Policy_Content: This Act, consisting of 27 articles, divided into five parts, provides for: the establishment of the Petroleum Commission; the regulation and management of midstream and upstream petroleum activities and the utilisation of petroleum resources. The Act defines the relevant terms, including: local content and local content fund; petroleum activities; petroleum infrastructure; petroleum resources; petroleum reserves. The Act establishes the Petroleum Commission as a body corporate which regulates petroleum activities, manages petroleum resources, ensures compliance with policies and laws for the petroleum sector and promotes local content for sustainable national development. The Act defines the functions of the Commission, including: planning, monitoring and coordinating petroleum activities, recommending national policies to the Minister and advising the Minister on matters related to petroleum activities, preparing documentation necessary to regulate petroleum sectors,   collecting and analysing data and economic information, with the aim to achieve optimal levels of resource exploitation and improve the overall welfare and the compliance with the healthy and environmental standards.

Policy: Law on Provision of Nationwide Fast-charging Infrastructure for Pure Battery Electric Vehicles.
Policy_Content: The Law provides for implementation of the EU Regulations regarding infrastructure of fast charging points for pure battery electric vehicles of classes M and N. According to the Law the Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure is in charge to provide comprehensive and need-based fast charging information and structure, determining the charging locations, number of fast charging points, the equipment and ancillary systems. The Law further provides for responsibility of this Ministry to define technical, economic and legal conditions for provision of the services through the contracts for supply, coverage, accessibility and performance of this service. The contracts shall be granted through tenders in several lots on federal or state bases. The Law further provides for the Ministry to provide every two years, starting from the year 2024, report on the area coverage, the operation and the technical equipment of the fast charging locations. The Law consists of 10 Articles as: 1. Scope of application; 2. Definitions; 3. Tasks of the Federal Ministry of Traffic and Digital Infrastructure; 4. Selection and assignment of contractors; 5. Ancillary businesses on federal motorways; 6. Existing infrastructure provider; 7. Authorisation to issue ordinances; 8. Loan; 9. Reporting; 10. Entry into force.

Policy: Presidential Order No. 476s on the implementation of the Presidential Decree No. 1400 on a number of measures for the development of production and processing industry in the agriculture sector, dated July 15, 2021.
Policy_Content: This Order lays down the duties of the relevant ministries for the implementation of the Presidential Decree No. 1400 on a number of measures for the development of production and processing industry in the agricultural sector. The duties of the Ministry of Economy include to submit proposals on (I) the classification of lands, their transfer from one category to another and the improvement of the regulatory framework for changing their purpose, (II) the improvement of the regulatory framework for the management and protection of lands, prevention of their illegal use as well as the protection, restoration and increase of fertility, (III) the application of customs and tax exemptions for agricultural products for export purposes, (IV) determining the scope of products that will replace imported goods with local goods and reducing the cost of local products to provide tax incentives to agricultural processing enterprises, (V) simplification of procedures for the export of agricultural products, (VI) improvement of the regulatory framework for the construction of residential, irrigation infrastructure and temporary structures for processing by agricultural producers on agricultural lands, (VII) improving the regulatory framework for regulating the activities of agro-parks, and (VIII) expansion of opportunities for enterprises operating in the field of agricultural production. Moreover, the duties of the Ministry of Agriculture include to submit proposals on (I) the improvement of the mechanism of lease and use of agricultural lands for the purpose of efficient use of agricultural lands, application of the practice of land consolidation, and (II) provision of state support to micro, small and medium enterprises engaged in agricultural production and processing, as well as the application of new financing instruments on credit guarantees.

Policy: Climate Action and Low Carbon Development (Amendment) Act 2021 (No. 32 of 2021).
Policy_Content: The Act amends the Climate Action and Low Carbon Development Act 2015 (No. 46 of 2015) (the Principal Act) in several sections, in particular it reformulates under section 3 "the National Climate Objective"; the State shall, so as to reduce the extent of further global warming, pursue and achieve, by no later than the end of the year 2050, the transition to a climate resilient, biodiversity rich, environmentally sustainable and climate neutral economy. For the purpose of enabling the State to pursue and achieve the national climate objective, the Minister shall make and submit to the Government for approval (a) carbon budgets;  (b) a sectoral emissions ceiling; (c) a climate action plan; (d) a national long term climate action strategy; (e) a national adaptation framework. It also provides for the role of local authorities; each local authority shall prepare and make a  "local authority climate action plan" which shall specify the mitigation measures and the adaptation measures to be adopted by the local authority.
