Policy_Content: La presente Resolución aprueba el Documento Técnico denominado “Contenido, Alcances y Generalidades del Módulo de Control del Sistema Nacional de Información Forestal y de Fauna Silvestre”. El objetivo del documento es establecer la definición, alcance, estructura y procesos del Módulo de Control del Sistema Nacional de Información Forestal y de Fauna Silvestre (MC-SNIFFS), como un marco general de organización de los procesos que garanticen su funcionalidad. Está conformado por un conjunto de datos, usuarios, procesos y tecnologías cuya interacción, bajo el cumplimiento de la normativa forestal y de fauna silvestre, provee la información que coadyuva al desarrollo de las acciones de control, supervisión, fiscalización y sanción en materia forestal y de fauna silvestre. Además de interactuar con los demás módulos y componentes del SNIFFS, así como con otros sistemas relevantes. Se establece el alcance del Módulo de Control, la estructura del Módulo de Control, y los procesos del Módulo de Control. Policy: Law of Georgia on Environmental Liability (No. 244-IVMS-XMP of 2021)
Policy_Content: The purpose of this Law is the legal regulation of issues related to environmental damage based on the 'polluter pays' principle. This law regulates legal relations related to the prevention of significant environmental damage, the mitigation of environmental damage or significant environmental damage, the measures to be taken in the event of environmental damage (including the implementation of remedial measures, and compensation for environmental damage and significant environmental damage). This Law shall apply to cases that are regulated by the international treaties of Georgia, unless otherwise provided for by the same international treaties. The further provides for prevention/mitigation of significant damage; measures to be implemented in the case of damage/significant damage; assessment of damage and making decisions by the Department; remedial measures; determining remedial measures; determining compensatory/adequate remedial measures at a site adjacent to the damaged area or at an alternative site; participation of interested parties in the process of determining remedial measures in the case of significant damage; coordinating with the Agency a plan of remedial measures and making amendments to it; implementation of remedial measures and supervision over the fulfilment of a plan of remedial measures; financial security for the risks of environmental damage; main goals of the environmental programme and the administration of its funds; the source of financing of the environmental programme; implementing and supervising measures financed from the environmental programme; and administrative offences, administrative proceedings and criminal liability. Additionally, the Law provides for the criteria for determining significant damage, including to biodiversity, land, water, and also provides for the particularly hazardous activities for the environment.

Policy: Loi n°2021‐23 du 02 mars 2021 relative aux contrats de Partenariat Public‐Privé.
Policy_Content: La présente loi a pour objet de régir les contrats de partenariat public‐privé. Les dispositions de la présente loi s’appliquent aux contrats de partenariat public‐privé  conclus dans tous les secteurs de la vie économique et sociale à l’exception des contrats  suivants: a) les contrats de partenariat public‐privé, tels que définis à l’article 3 de la présente  loi, régis par des dispositions législatives et réglementaires spécifiques aux secteurs  suivants :  -  les énergies ;  -  les mines ;  -  les télécommunications, au sens des activités régulées et soumises au régime de la  licence et de l’autorisation par le Code des communications électroniques; b) les contrats passés entre autorités contractantes, à l’exception des contrats de  partenariat public‐privé passés entre une société anonyme à participation publique  majoritaire dont le capital social n’est pas exclusivement détenu par des autorités  contractantes et une autre autorité contractante qui restent régis par la présente loi; c) les contrats ayant pour objet des besoins de défense et de sécurité nationale  exigeant le secret ou pour lesquels la protection des intérêts essentiels de l’État est  incompatible avec des mesures de publicité; d) les contrats attribués aux opérateurs économiques en vertu de droits exclusifs  octroyés par des dispositions législatives ou réglementaires nationales ; e)  les  contrats  conclus  avec  un  opérateur  économique  avec  lequel  l’autorité  contractante entretient une relation de quasi‐régie lorsque les conditions suivantes  sont réunies :  -  l’autorité contractante exerce sur l’opérateur économique un contrôle analogue à  celui qu’elle exerce sur ses propres services ;  -  l’opérateur économique contrôlé réalise au moins 80 % de son activité dans le  cadre des tâches qui lui sont confiées par l’autorité contractante qui le contrôle ou  par d’autres personnes morales que cette autorité contractante contrôle ;  -  l’opérateur économique contrôlé ne comporte pas de participation directe de  capitaux privés, à l’exception des formes de participation de capitaux privés sans  capacité de contrôle ou de blocage ; et f) les contrats portant sur la privatisation ou la cession des entreprises, biens et  équipements en infrastructure des autorités contractantes.

Policy: Law on climate change.
Policy_Content: This Law regulates the system for the limitation of greenhouse gas emissions (or GHG) and for adaptation to changed climatic conditions, monitoring and reporting on the strategy of low-carbon development and its improvement, the program of adaptation to changed climatic conditions, adoption of the strategy of low-carbon development and the program of adaptation to changed climate conditions, issuing permits for GHG emissions to the plant operator, issuing approval to the aircraft operator's monitoring plan, monitoring, reporting, verification and accreditation of verifiers, administrative fees, supervision and other issues of importance for the limitation of GHG emissions and adaptation to changed climatic conditions. The provisions of the Law apply to the procedure for issuing, revoking, amending and supplementing the GHG emission permit, the procedure for granting approval and approval for changes to the GHG emission monitoring plan, the procedure for granting approval for reports on improvements in the GHG emission methodology, and the procedure for keeping records and registers, among other general administrative procedures as here specified. The goal of this Law is to establish a system to reduce GHG emissions in a cost-effective and economically efficient manner, thus contributing to reaching the scientifically necessary levels of GHG emissions in order to avoid dangerous climate changes at the global level and adverse impacts of climate change. The goal of this Law is to reduce GHG emissions and adapt to changed climate conditions also by adopting and implementing public policy documents. The aim of this Law is further defined in order to establish necessary mechanisms for timely, transparent, accurate, consistent, comparable and complete reporting and verification of information on the fulfillment of obligations under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, Kyoto Protocol Doha Amendments to the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and Paris Agreement, as well as for monitoring and reporting on human-caused GHG emissions from sources and removed through sinks and adaptation activities to changed climate conditions undertaken in a cost-effective and economically efficient manner. To achieve the goals of this law, state authorities and organizations should adopt appropriate sector policies and measures within the scope of their competence. In the area of climate change prescribed by this law, the following documents are adopted: 1) low-carbon development strategy; 2) action plan for strategy implementation; 3) programme of adaptation to changed climatic conditions. The Ministry responsible for environmental protection in cooperation with other competent ministries and relevant state institutions and bodies is preparing the Low Carbon Development Strategy in order to determine the strategic directions of action and public policy related to restrictions GHG emissions from sources, as well as transparent and accurate monitoring of reaching those emission limits. The Government shall prescribe related levels of GHG emissions: from sources at the national level, for facilities and aviation activities and for GHG emissions from sectors and categories in which fuel combustion and fugitive emissions from fuel, industrial processes and product use, agriculture and waste occur.

Policy: Décret modifiant le décret du 5 avril 1995 contenant des dispositions générales concernant la politique de l’environnement et le décret du 23 décembre 2011 relatif à la gestion durable de cycles de matériaux et de déchets
Policy_Content: Ce décret, composé par 4 chapitres, modifie le décret du 5 avril 1995 contenant des dispositions générales concernant la politique de l'environnement et le décret du 23 décembre 2011 relatif à la gestion durable de cycles de matériaux et de déchets. Quant au premier, l'article 10.3.3, § 2 est complété par des points 20°, 21° et 22°. Quant au deuxième, l'article 2 est modifié pour l'adapter à la transposition de la normative européenne en vigueur. Dans l'article trois sont insérées ou modifiées les définitions de biodéchets, déchets alimentaires, déchet non dangereux, régime de responsabilité élargie des producteurs et déchets municipaux ainsi que les définitions de unité de bâtiment et de logement. L'article 4 est révisé dans sa phrase introductive qui définit l'objectif du décret comme celui d'arrêté des mesures pour promouvoir une économie circulaire et pour réaliser des cycles de matériaux par lesquels, entre autre, au point 1 est prévu que la santé de l’homme et de l’environnement soient protégées en prévenant ou en réduisant la production de déchets et les incidences négatives de la production et de la gestion des déchets. L'article 9 est conséquentement complété par un paragraphe 3 prévoyant que le collecteur de déchets propose au producteur de déchets une formule de collecte qui incite le producteur de déchets à offrir les déchets de manière à ce que les objectifs visés à l’article 4 puissent être maximisés lors du traitement des déchets. L'article 10 est révisé pour régler le coûts de la gestion des déchets, y compris ceux relatifs aux infrastructures nécessaires et à leur exploitation en conformité au principe du pollueur-payeur. Aussi l'article 17 est révisé relativement aux programmes de prévention et aux mesures minimales qu'il comportent en termes de modèles de production et de produits satisfaisant certaines conditions. L'article 18 est modifié dans son paragraphe 6 relativement aux éléments que les plans d'exécution doivent comporter au moins en mentionnant les grandes installations d'élimination ainsi que une évaluation de la nécessité de fermeture d’installations de déchets existantes, de la nécessité de mettre en place des infrastructures supplémentaires d'installation de gestion des déchets (points 2 et 3 par.6) L'article 21, concernant l'attribution de responsabilité financière pour la gestion des déchets est aussi revu ainsi que les pratiques que cette attribution mire à obtenir quant au développement, à la fabrication et à la commercialisation de produits avec certaines caractéristiques.Dans l'article 21 est aussi inséré un article 21/1 qui prévoit que, face au régime de responsabilité qu'il établit, le Gouvernement flamand fixe une série de paramètre auxquels se conformer. L'article 33 relatif au protocole d'inspection de l'inventaire d'amiante est aussi révisé quant à la détermination déterminer des constructions d'années à risque qui doivent faire partie de l'inventaire d'amiante. Les articles 36, 39 et 40 relatifs à ce que peut être considéré comme déchet (déchets qui ont subi un traitement en vue de leur recyclage, matériaux pour lesquels n'ait été établi aucun critère européen etc.) sont aussi modifiés.

Policy_Content: This Regional Decree is designed to detect and suppress violations by legal entities, individual entrepreneurs and citizens of the mandatory requirements of forestry legislation, as well as in in order to participate in ensuring measures to eliminate the consequences of the identified violations in the implementation of the federal state forestry supervision (forest protection measures) and federal state fire supervision in forests. Control (patrolling) activities in forests can carried out constantly and at any one time. Forest patrol routes are being developed by forestry departments of the Main Directorate within the boundaries of the territory of forestry, taking into account the places of the supposed, systematic or actual violations of the requirements of forest legislation: forest areas, which are places of mass recreation of citizens; forest areas that are the most fire hazardous (young conifers, forest areas where previously there were forest fires); forest plots available for entry of vehicles for hunting purposes; forest areas where young conifers grow in order to protect them during the harvesting of spruce trees and (or) trees of other conifers for the New Year holidays; forest sites on which the development of minerals is carried out, linear objects are located; forest areas adjacent to land of agricultural purposes, peatlands, borders of populated points, horticultural, vegetable gardening and suburban farming associations of citizens; forest plots provided to citizens and legal entities in use, including for the purpose of checking existing cutting areas, located on the forest patrol route, for compliance with requirements of forest legislation by forest users.

Policy: System No. 10 of 2021 regarding the Partnership between the Public and Private Sectors in the Kurdistan Region - Iraq.
Policy_Content: This System, comprising 10 articles, is designed to incentivize private sector involvement in financing partnership projects with the public sector. It operates within a legal framework that prioritizes competition and transparency, aiming to enhance public utility services and production. The main objectives include (i) developing a comprehensive legal framework to regulate public partnerships; (ii) ensuring fairness and transparency in contract conclusion and implementation; (iii) facilitating the establishment, rehabilitation, operation, maintenance, and development of public infrastructure and facilities, with risk distribution between the two sectors; (iv) providing public services and financing for government projects; (v) leveraging the private sector's technical expertise to enhance project efficiency, performance, and financial support for partnership projects. The provisions of this Law apply to the funded partnership projects, whether directly or jointly with the public sector, if approved by the Supreme Council for PPP, established by Article 4 of this System. Its main functions are (i) drawing up the general policy for partnership projects, the general objectives, and determining the most important aspects and priorities; (ii) select eligible partnership projects based on reports prepared by the Ministry of Planning and the Ministry of Finance and Economy; (iii) approval of preliminary feasibility studies, feasibility reports, terms of reference and appointment of project experts; (iv) final approval of the tender referral and the partnership contract in its final form. Article 5 establishes at the Ministry of Plannig the Unit for PPP Projects with the main task of helping government institutions to define the projects presented and define their priorities. While the Ministry of Finance and Economy will follow and control the financial process of the project, ensuring the supply of the necessary financing.

Policy: Order No. 142 of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Natural Resources validating the Regulation on National Natural Park "Royal Beskydy".
Policy_Content: The National Natural Park "Royal Beskydy" is located on the territory of Starosambir district of Lviv region. The park is a budgetary, non-profit, nature conservation, recreational, cultural and educational, scientific research institution and is part of the nature reserve fund of Ukraine, protected as a national property, with a special regime of protection, reproduction and management. Land plots and water areas, including those of other landowners and tenants, with all natural resources and objects shall be withdrawn from economic use and shall be transferred to the park on condition of permanent tenure in accordance with acting legislation. On the territory of the park, the necessary state information and security signs of the approved model, in particular landmarks, are installed in designated places. The main tasks of the park are: (a) conservation of valuable objects of historical and cultural heritage; (b) creation of conditions for organized tourism, rest and other types of recreational activities in natural conditions with observance of the regime of protection of protected natural complexes and objects; (c) conducting scientific studies of natural complexes and their changes under conditions of recreational use, development of scientific recommendations on issues of environmental protection and effective use of natural resources; and (d) carrying out ecological educational work. In accordance with nature protection legislation, the following zones are distinguished on the territory of the park: (a) protected area; (b) zone of regulated recreation; (c) zone of stationary recreation; and (d) economic zone. For each zone, taking into account its nature protection, healthcare, scientific, recreational, historical and cultural and other values of natural complexes and objects and their features, a differentiated regime is established regarding their protection, reproduction and use.

Policy: Regional Decree No. 78-p “On the regional early warning system of the population.”
Policy_Content: The scope this Regional Decree shall be to coordinate activities related to setting up and maintenance of early warning system in a state of constant readiness. The Regulation defines the purpose and tasks of the regional public early warning systems, the procedure for their activation and maintenance in alert. Notification of the population in emergency situations is early warning of the population - delivery of notification signals and urgent information to the population about dangers arising in the case of natural and manmade emergencies, military activities or as a consequence of the aforesaid actions and the necessity to perform protective arrangements. A warning signal is a command to carry out activities for civil protection and protection of population from emergencies, natural and man-made disasters by management bodies and forces of civil protection and unified state system of emergency prevention and mitigation of the consequences thereof, as well as for the use by the population of means and methods of protection. Emergency information about actual and forecasted hazardous natural and anthropogenic phenomena, environmental pollution, diseases that may put at risk life or health of citizens, as well as rules of conduct and methods of protection shall be immediately transmitted via the public notification system.

Policy: Regional Law No. 10-oz “On regulation of some issues in the field of management of domestic and non-domestic waste.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law, with a view of preventing negative impact of domestic and non-domestic waste on environment and human health, saving natural resources, regulates some issues of domestic and non-domestic waste management on the regional territory. Transportation of waste shall be performed with the consideration of the requirements set forth by the federal legislation and in accordance with the regional waste management scheme. Authorization for transportation of waste shall be issued to legal or natural persons performing transportation (movement) of waste, including construction and solid waste. Waste accumulation on the regional territory, including through separate storage by type of waste, groups of wastes, groups of homogeneous wastes (separate accumulation) with due consideration of the requirements established by the federal and regional legislation. Organization of unauthorized waste disposal sites, as well as accumulation, storage, dumping of waste outside the places (sites) of waste accumulation sites that meet the requirements of the sanitary, epidemiological and hygienic well-being of the population and other legislation of the Russian Federation, including forest fund land, agricultural land, lands of protected areas shall be prohibited.

Timber harvested on the lands of the forest fund, its transportation and trade are subject to accounting in the unified state automated information timber accounting system and transactions with it (EGAIS). Legal entities and individual entrepreneurs carrying out harvesting, and (or) logging, and (or) transportation and (or) trade of timber harvested on lands not included in the lands of the forest fund, have the right to keep records of it in the unified state automated information timber accounting system and transactions with it (EGAIS). Transportation and (or) sale by legal persons and individual entrepreneurs, as well as transportation by natural persons of timber harvested on the lands of the forest fund and not recorded in the unified state automated information timber accounting system and transactions with it (EGAIS) shall be prohibited.

Policy: Law on environmental protection.
Policy_Content: This Law regulates: a) the principles of environmental protection; b) protection of environmental components; c) competence in the field of environmental protection; d) information and education on the environment; e) access to environmental information and public participation in the field of environmental protection; f) environmental planning; g) strategic environmental impact assessment; h) establishment of environmental quality standards; i) environmental impact assessment; j) environmental permit; k) prevention of large-scale accidents; l) financing of environmental protection; m) civil liability for environmental damage; n) eco-labelling and environmental management system; o) inter-entity cooperation in the field of environmental protection; p) administrative and inspection supervision and r) misdemeanor provisions. General objectives of this Law are: a) reduced use, prevention of pollution and environmental pollution, prevention of disturbances, as well as improvement and restoration of the damaged environment; b) improvement of environmental conditions, protection of human health, including the right to a healthy life; c) conservation and protection of natural resources, rational use of resources and such a way of doing business which ensures the renewal of resources; d) harmonization of social, economic and other interests of the Federation of BiH with the requirements for environmental protection; e) realization and improvement of international cooperation in environmental protection; f) public animation and public participation in activities aimed at environmental protection; g) coordination of the economy and integration of social and economic development in accordance with the requirements of environmental protection; h) establishment and development of institutions for protection and preservation of the environment. The provisions of this Law apply to: a) all components of the environment (air, water, soil, world of plants, animals and fungi, landscape, built environment); b) all types of activities whose purpose is the use and burdening of natural resources, i.e. the impact on the environment that means the risk of pollution during the activity, or have a negative impact on the environment (such as noise, vibration, radiation, excluding nuclear radiation, waste, light pollution , etc.); c) rights and responsibilities of legal and natural persons performing activities determined by law; d) tasks in the field of environment arising from international conventions. Everyone has the right to a healthy and environmentally sound environment as a fundamental human right and it is a general duty to protect and improve the environment for the benefit of present and future generations. Entities that ensure environmental protection are the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, cantons and local self-government units in accordance with this Law and other regulations.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. 43/21 approving the Regulation for the Independent Electric Energy Production.

Policy: Parliament Resolution No. HP15/2021 validating the Declaration of the Parliament of the Republic of Moldova on the current and future impact of hydropower facilities on the Dniester River, as well as on the prevention of an imminent environmental catastrophe.
Policy_Content: In 2011, the Government, by Resolution No. 205 of March 31, initiated the procedure ratification, and Parliament, by Law No. 171 of July 28, ratified the Moldovan-Ukrainian protocol, on the basis of which to Ukraine was transferred full ownership of Novodnistrovskaya pump-storage hydroelectric power station. Scientists and environmentalists note deteriorating hydrological, hydrochemical and hydrobiological regime of the Dniester River, 80-percentage decrease over the past 7-8 years in the potential for self-cleaning (the river is no longer capable of self-cleaning), the disappearance of valuable fish species, intensive siltation of the river, a sharp drop in volume, debit and level of water, replacement of plants characteristic of rivers with plants, characteristic of marshes and wetlands, and many other problems indicating the risk that our citizens will soon be left without a source of drinking water, while catastrophic environmental consequences can become irreversible not only for Republic of Moldova, but also for Ukraine. Parliament expresses deep concern about Kiev's intention to establish and put in operation of new turbines and expansion of the Novodnistrovsk pump-storage hydroelectric power plant, as well as the planned construction on the Dniester of a cascade of six hydroelectric power plants, which we consider disastrous for the Republic of Moldova. We believe that proposals for new environmental impact assessments due to the expansion of the Dniester hydropower complex are relevant and will allow solving serious problems of the lower reaches of the Dniester River. In this regard, we call on international and European organizations in the field of environmental protection, development partners and diplomatic missions, accredited in the Republic of Moldova, representatives of civil society and mass media in the country and abroad to be more actively involved in solving the problem of Dniester River.

Policy: Food Vision 2030.
Policy_Content: This Food Vision 2030 is a nationwide strategic document aiming, as a primary purpose, at providing a vision and policies for the Irish agri-food sector over the coming decade following the path of transition experienced by the sector over the past years. As for the aforementioned Vision, Ireland aims to become a world leader in Sustainable Food Systems (SFS) over the next decade, meeting the highest standards of sustainability – economic, environmental, and social - and producing safe, nutritious, and high-value food, while protecting and enhancing the natural and cultural resources and contributing to vibrant rural and coastal communities and the national economy. The Strategy is based on the concept of 4 high-level Missions underpinned by a series of 22 key goals and actions. Policy: Energy and Natural Resources Sector Strategy 2021-2023.
Policy_Content: This Energy and Natural Resources Sector Strategy is a nationwide sectoral document that falls within the broader National Development Plan 2021 - 2023 endorsed by Prime Minister's Office. The energy sector in Palestine aims to advance in all its branches: generation, transmission, and distribution to achieve the Energy Authority’s mission of (i) preparing and developing appropriate policies and legislation to achieve sustainable energy security under international best practices; (ii) building an energy system capable of meeting the needs of the Palestinian citizen; (iii) achieve a comprehensive and sustainable development at reasonable prices that reflect the true cost of production, transportation, distribution, and consumption; (iv) utilizing all locally available energy sources, especially renewable and environmentally friendly energy sources, with high efficiency, quality, and reliability that meet internationally approved specifications and comply with internationally approved environmental standards. Among the most important goals to be achieved through this Strategy (i) increasing the amount of locally produced capacity, exploiting local resources and reducing dependence on imports as much as possible; (ii) increasing the share of energy produced from new and renewable energy sources in the energy balance to mitigate negative environmental impacts; (iii) efficient production, transmission, distribution and consumption of energy, and adopting a policy of rationalizing consumption and reducing waste; (iv) diversifying energy sources to ensure energy security by increasing the proportion of energy produced locally and from all sources, and increasing the proportion of imported energy through regional connectivity and energy exchange with neighboring countries; and (v) building specialized and effective institutions in the energy sector capable of implementing development programs and developing the energy sector, and separating the sector’s activities from the policymaker, executor of these policies, and the supervisory body to implement these policies. Achieving these goals helps to secure energy at competitive prices which in turn contributes to lowering the cost to the consumer. The aforementioned goals can be achieved through the following (i) provision of strategic energy reserves; (ii) energy exchange with neighboring countries; (iii) developed transmission and distribution system; (iv) applying modern technologies and automating the monitoring and control of the energy transmission and distribution system; (v) energy efficiency and rationalization of consumption; (vi) intervening on the institutions operating in the energy sector; (vii) integrated and comprehensive planning for the energy sector within a single policy framework; (viii) efficiency of the cadres working in the energy sector; (ix) increasing the economic efficiency of the sector; (x) supplying natural gas to the Gaza power station and providing natural gas resources to build power stations in the West Bank; (xi) exploitation of natural gas discovered in the Gaza Sea and potential oil resources in the West Bank; (xii) the completion of the drafting of the commercial agreement with the Israel Electricity Company regarding the import of electricity.

Policy: Governmental Decree No. 36 validating the Regulation on the procedure for determining the norms of livestock pressure on grazing land of the Kyrgyz Republic.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the procedure for determining the norms of livestock pressure on grazing land of the Kyrgyz Republic with a view of preventing degradation and desertification of agricultural land. It shall be applicable to grazing grounds, including forest pastures. The scope of determining the norms of livestock pressure on grazing land shall be to maintain ecological balance, natural grass stand, implementation of calculations according to the norm of pressure on rangelands for the rational use of rangelands. Rates of livestock pressure on grazing land shall be calculated per hectare expressed in the number of conventional head of livestock that can provide forage for a unit of pasture area. The pressure is determined depending on the typological composition of vegetation, the utilization rate of rangelands (herbage by seasons) and yield. The rate of load on pastures of the Kyrgyz Republic for the territory of the corresponding rural district is established by local authorities of self-government, taking into account natural and climatic conditions, productivity, daily feed rates that cannot be lower than baseline indicators.

Policy: Presidential Decree UP No. 25 “On measures for the development of agro-industrial complex.”
Policy_Content: The President recommends to the Government to adopt the following measures: (a) to increase the efficiency of use and market turnover of agricultural land; (b) to consider the possibility of transferring to the management of the authorized body for agriculture part of land of the State Fund of Agricultural Land for the development of cooperatives, seed and breeding farms; (c) to introduce cluster farming methods in the agro-industrial complex at the national and regional levels, including organizing agroclusters for the processing of milk, meat, walnuts, medicinal herbs, fish products, textile crops, wool and leather; (d) to create conditions for: large land users (100 hectares and more) with the provision of opportunities for them on their land plots for the construction of farms necessary for the functioning and development of farming, including fiscal measures and incentives; (e) to introduce agricultural insurance system in areas of risky farming and distant cattle breeding; (f) to develop halal agricultural products; (g) to create conditions and mechanisms to stimulate industrial enterprises, including residents of free economic zones, as well as enterprises of textile and clothing industry for the use of agricultural raw materials and materials (spinning crops, leather, wool, etc.) in the manufacturing of finished products; (h) to create mechanisms of cooperation with industrial science and cluster alliances to improve farmers' access to innovation and ensure introduction of modern technologies, including resource-saving technologies in agriculture; (i) to determine the list of public services and functions in the field of agro-industrial complex and agriculture on the basis of mechanisms of Public Private Partnership; (j) to abolish the licensing of artesian wells used for needs of agriculture; (k) to take measures for the effective use of undeveloped and unproductive agricultural land and pastures, consider the possibility of development on these land plots for agroforestry, horticulture and viticulture; (l) to create an information and reference system for peasants and farmers; (m) to ensure traceability of agricultural commodities; (n) to ensure agribusiness access to land, water and pasture resources for the transformation of agricultural land into production goals; (o) to create conditions for organizing and expanding fish production in water reservoirs, including infrastructure for production and processing of fish products; (p) to take measures to overcome small-scale production by developing cooperation in agriculture; (q) to improve the access of agricultural cooperatives to local and national agricultural markets and trade networks of the country; and (r) to introduce technologies aimed at improving water accounting in irrigation networks.

Policy: Ley Nº 196 - Crea el Régimen Especial para el establecimiento de Empresas Operadoras y Desarrolladoras de Agroparques.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley crea el Régimen Especial para el establecimiento de Empresas Operadoras y Desarrolladoras de Agroparques, con el propósito de desarrollar un marco regulatorio para cumplir los siguientes objetivos: 1) Incentivar la inversión y el establecimiento de agroparques que contribuyan a la creación de polos de desarrollo que, al tiempo que fomenten la generación de agronegocios, promuevan el establecimiento de cadenas de valor a partir de bienes nacionales, en un entorno geográfico y bajo condiciones idóneas; 2) Promover la producción agroalimentaria, agroindustrial y de servicios afines, así como también industrias relacionadas con el sector forestal, productos del mar y materias primas para la industria farmacéutica en un entorno eficiente que promueve la innovación; 3) Desarrollar cadenas productivas de valor con la adopción de altas tecnologías sostenibles con el ambiente, agregando valor a través de la transformación y/o procesamiento de la materia prima y sus subproductos; 4)  Identificar promotores con capacidad de creación de mercado, para fomentar el desarrollo de una oferta exportable apegada a las necesidades globales; 5) Incentivar la participación de empresas desarrolladoras nacionales e internacionales, con experiencia probada en modelos similares, quienes asesoraran a los agroempresarios y agroindustriales poniendo a su disposición tecnología de punta, experiencias de producción, transformación, procesamiento y reciclaje; 6) Cumplir con los estándares nacionales e internacionales y observar las normas sanitarias y ambientales que garanticen la inocuidad, seguridad y trazabilidad de la producción; 7) Implementar el uso de la agrotecnología de forma eficiente y sostenible con el ambiente, adoptando conceptos de producción más limpia y sostenible, buenas prácticas de estándares globales de producción, manejo postcosecha y asegurar una gestión integrada de residuos generados del proceso productivo agropecuario, de conformidad con la legislación vigente; 8) Establecer mecanismos de asociatividad entre los agroempresarios, empresarios de servicios y agroindustriales que faciliten relaciones de negocios entre ellos y el acceso a beneficios redistributivos a la mayor cantidad de personas y sujetos del sector agropecuario y de exportación; 9) Garantizar la modernización de los procesos, trámites y permisos que faciliten la investigación, financiamiento y promoción de la agroindustria nacional; 10) Promover las inversiones en agua, energía y comunicaciones que tiendan a impactar en el desarrollo de las cadenas de valor; 11) Apoyar con servicios agrosanitarios y de inocuidad, y el desarrollo de productos de valor a partir de la agroindustria nacional; 12)  Optimizar el recurso hídrico de forma sostenible, promoviendo el aumento de la resiliencia del sector agropecuario frente al cambio climático.

Policy: Ley Nº 21.305 - Sobre eficiencia energética.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley establece la obligación del Ministerio de Energía de elaborar, cada cinco años, un Plan Nacional de Eficiencia Energética, el que deberá comprender, al menos, las siguientes materias: eficiencia energética residencial; estándares mínimos y etiquetado de artefactos; eficiencia energética en la edificación y el transporte; eficiencia energética y ciudades inteligentes; eficiencia energética en los sectores productivos y educación y capacitación en eficiencia energética. Este Plan deberá establecer una meta de reducción de la intensidad energética para el país de, al menos, 10% al año 2030, respecto del año 2019. El Ministerio de Energía deberá someter al Consejo de Ministros para la Sustentabilidad el primer Plan Nacional de Eficiencia Energética, en un plazo no superior a dieciocho meses contado desde la publicación de esta ley (13 de febrero de 2021). La Ley establece los lineamientos para la elaboración del Plan, incluyendo mecanismos que aseguren la participación ciudadana. Asimismo, se establecen normas sobre la calificación energética para obtener permisos de edificación, se crea el Registro Nacional de Evaluadores Energéticos, se establecen las obligaciones y responsabilidades de los evaluados energéticos, se establece la obligación de los gobiernos locales de velar por el buen uso por el buen uso de la energía en los inmuebles que ocupen y/o administren, entre otras materias relacionadas con la eficiencia energética.  La presente Ley modifica el Decreto Ley N° 2.224, de 1978, del Ministerio de Energía, con tal de incluir al hidrógeno y combustibles a partir de hidrógeno dentro de las competencias en el sector energía de este Ministerio; y se agregan nuevos párrafos referidos a los nuevos estándares de eficiencia energética.

Policy: Somaliland Special Economic Zones Law, No: 93/2021
Policy_Content: This law is made for the following purposes; 1) To regulate the establishment, development, operation and maintenance of Special Economic Zones in the Republic of Somaliland. 2) To establish the legal framework and mechanisms for the regulation and administration of activities within the special economic zones with due regard to the principles of openness, competitiveness and transparency, and 3) To enable environment for the development of all aspects of special economic zones including; development of integrated infrastructure facilities, creation of incentives for economic and business activities and to remove of impediments to economic or business activities that generate profit for enterprises in areas designated as special economic zones. Furthermore, the specific purpose for designating special economic zones include; a) to promote and facilitate local and foreign investment in the Republic of Somaliland; b) to create and expand employment opportunities; c) to stimulate economic growth in existing and new business sectors through the sustainable development of new Special Economic Zones; d) to develop new infrastructure and rehabilitate existing infrastructure; e) to encourage the private sector to participate in the development, operation and maintenance of Special Economic Zones including the development of Infrastructure; to promote an investment and trade environment in-line with international best practices; f) to create an attractive regulatory framework and conducive business environment for local and foreign investors, including through the creation of a one stop shop and entitlement to a package of fiscal and non-fiscal incentives; g) to promote financial and industrial cooperation between the Republic of Somaliland and foreign countries through technology-intensive industries that will modernize the country’s industrial sector and improve productivity levels by utilizing new technological and managerial know-how; and h) To enable the Special Economic Zones to operate outside the Customs Territory, within the framework of the Constitution and the national sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Republic of Somaliland. The law provides that, among others, all Special Economic Zones (SEZ) in the Republic of Somaliland shall be operated on a common user basis without any unfair or discriminatory practice against any actual or prospective SEZ User or SEZ Resident. The law establishes the  Somaliland Special Economic Zones Authority, which shall have exclusive regulatory jurisdiction over all Special Economic Zones. The commercial activities which may be carried out within a Special Economic Zone include industrial, logistics, retail, residential, commercial, and any other activities permitted under the applicable License.

Policy: Governmental Decree No. 117 “On rates of export customs duties on grain crops exported from the Russian Federation outside the states - parties to the agreements on the Customs Union.”
Policy_Content: Starting from April 1, 2021, the Ministry of Agriculture of the Russian Federation will monitor grain prices by observing price indicators: daily exchange quotations for wheat and meslin, barley and corn, or, if they are absent, indices calculated on the basis of over-the-counter contracts. So, with regard to wheat at a world price of up to 200 US dollars per ton, the duty will not be levied. At a price exceeding 200 US dollars per ton, the duty will be 70% of the difference between the world and this base price of 200 US dollars. For barley and corn, the indicator is set at 185 US dollars per ton. The monitoring period is 7 calendar days preceding the date of calculation of the rates of export customs duties for the specified grain crops. On the last working day of the week, the Ministry of Agriculture of the Russian Federation calculates the rates of export customs duties on grain crops and posts information about the calculated rates on its official website on the Internet.

Policy: Islamabad Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act 2020.
Policy_Content: The Act provides rules for registration of the real estate project before the Real East Regulatory Authority with the purpose of protecting the interest of buyers in the real estate sector; to regulate mega projects in the real estate sector by any developer and providing a mechanism for speedy dispute settlement. The Act requires as well registration of the real estate agents that shall facilitate the sale or purchase of or act on behalf of any person.  The Act further lays out for functions and duties of developer, and rights and duties of allottees. Chapter V of the text provides for the real estate regulatory authority establishment, composition, and functions that include measures to encourage construction of environmentally sustainable and affordable housing; measures to facilitate digitalization of land records; creation of a single window system for ensuring time bound project approvals; and measures to encourage investment in the real estate sector. The Act further provides for offences, the real estate appellate tribunal, finance and reports. The text consists of 88 Articles divided into 9 Chapters.

Policy: Law No. 04/2021 establishing the Great Options of the Plan for the Economic Year 2021.
Policy_Content: This Law approves the Great Options of the Plan for the Economic Year 2021. These Great Options are part of the ongoing economic recovery process, structured in measures and actions oriented towards the implementation and the achievement of the strategic objectives defined for the period 2018-2022. The Great Options of the Plan for the year 2021 are those assumed by the Government, as fundamental pillars of the governmental action, namely: a) Deepening the democratic rule of law; b) Robust economic growth and accelerated job creation; c) Improving the quality of health and social protection; d) Foreign policy at the service of development. The priority areas for intervention are mainly based on activities related to post-Covid 19 recovery, with highlights for transport infrastructures; capturing and distributing water to populations; improving the production, transport and distribution of electricity to the population; improving the quality of the education system at all levels; reform in the justice sector and the improvement of health care.

Policy: Loi nº 2020 - 37 du 03 février 2021 portant protection de la santé des personnes en République du Bénin
Policy_Content: La présente loi a pour objet : l'organisation de la protection de la santé des personnes ; la définition des sujétions imposées aux citoyens en leur personne en cos de maladies transmissibles, non transmissibles, contagieuses ou d'épidémies. Elle s'applique à toute personne vivant en République du Bénin ou entrant sur le territoire béninois. L'organisation de la protection de la santé des personnes vise à garantir la réalisation du droit à la santé pour tous et à contribuer à la promotion du renforcement du capital humain dans une approche multisectorielle. Elle garantit notamment à cet effet les principes de bonne moralité, de probité, d'éthique, d'équité, de dévouement et de responsabilité indispensables à l’exercice des professions de la santé en vue d'assurer le bien-être des populations. Elle vise précisément la protection de la personne humaine et le renforcement du capital humain par : la promotion des conditions optimales pour une bonne qualité des soins ; la promotion des bonnes pratiques dons le système de santé ; la modernisation du poteau technique des formations sanitaires ; l'augmentation des infrastructures sanitaires ; le renforcement des capacités des acteurs du système à tous les niveaux ; la protection de l'environnement et la promotion de l’hygiène et de l'assainissement de base ; la formation et le recrutement du personnel de santé qualifié ; l'amélioration du dispositif d'approvisionnement et de distribution des médicaments ; la répartition équilibrée et cohérente du personnel de santé sur tout le territoire ; l'amélioration du cadre et des conditions de travail du personnel de santé ; la responsabilité du service médical et paramédical ; la prévention des maladies émergentes el réémergentes, transmissibles et non transmissibles. L'organisation de la protection de la santé des personnes intègre les accords et conventions internationaux afin de déterminer les moyens à mettre en œuvre pour réaliser les objectifs visés au présent chapitre.

Policy: EIA Guidelines for Industries.
Policy_Content: The EIA Guidelines for Industries is a document developed by the Department of Environment of Bangladesh where an Initial Environmental Examination (IEE) and EIA study has been made regulatory need under certain categories of projects as specified in Environment Conservation Rule, 1997 for obtaining Environmental Clearance Certificate which is mandatory for any industrial and other development projects. These Guidelines present 6 steps of the EIA processes (1) screening, to determine the suitability of a site for industry or projects based on a variety of criteria including air and water quality, ecology, waste disposal, and noise; (2) scoping, to identify the scope of the EIA study and the information necessary for decision making, as well as determine the key issues and significant impacts and risks to be considered; (3) baseline data generation, required as preliminary information for conducting the EIA and should be comprehensive data including the following components: (i) physical; (ii) biological; and (iii) social and economic; (4) impact assessment, involving 3 main phases (1) identify in more detail the impacts under investigation associated with each phase of the project; (2) predict the nature, extent, duration, and other characteristics of major impacts; and (3) evaluate the significance of any other impacts that cannot be mitigated; (5) mitigation of impacts to minimize adverse impacts by finding better alternatives and adopting mitigation measures. The EIA report has to contain the following points (i) impacts to be mitigated; (ii) expected effects; (iii) alternative measures; (iv) costs; (v) implementation plan; and (6) environmental management plan, including mitigation measures to reduce the environmental impacts. Environmental monitoring should be designed to provide information on the actual impacts of activities, compliance with environmental operating conditions, and the effectiveness of environmental mitigation measures. The evaluation of monitoring results is necessary to ensure that environmental objectives are achieved.

Policy: Law No. 1759 “On ensuring biological security and biological protection”.
Policy_Content: This Law regulates public relations concerning controlled biological agents and toxins in order to strengthen the system of biological security and biological protection. Biological security shall be intended security measures combined with biosecurity procedures to reduce the risk of loss, theft or use of controlled biological agents and toxins as biological weapons, sabotage, bioterrorism or technology and practices to prevent their proliferation and inadvertent release. Biological security and biological protection are provided in accordance with the following principles: (a) legality; (b) rationing; (c) optimization; and (d) prevention. Ensuring biological security and biological protection include a set of measures and means (organizational, legal, technical, technological and therapeutic) aimed at protecting of public health during production, transportation, operation, storage, sale, consumption, disposal of products, performance of work and provision of services. Biosecurity includes security, control, and accountability measures applied to prevent the loss, theft, misuse, leakage, or deliberate release of controlled biological agents and toxins and their associated resources, and the unauthorized access, storage, or transfer of such material. This Law contains V Chapters divided into 22 Articles. Chapter I lays down the general provisions. Chapter II imposes prohibition measures in the field of biological security and biological protection. Chapter III regards state administration in the field of biological security and biological protection. Chapter IV establishes requirements in the field of biological security and biological protection.  Chapter V lays down final protection.

Policy: Executive Order 14008 of January 27, 2021, on Tackling the Climate Crisis at Home and Abroad
Policy_Content: This executive order states that it is the policy of my Administration that climate considerations shall be an essential element of United States foreign policy and national security. The United States will work with other countries and partners, both bilaterally and multilaterally, to put the world on a sustainable climate pathway. The United States will also move quickly to build resilience, both at home and abroad, against the impacts of climate change that are already manifest and will continue to intensify according to current trajectories. Policy: Decree No. 43 of the Council of Ministers validating the Regulation on the procedure for withdrawal (withdrawal) from circulation, return, export, disposal of dangerous products.”
Policy_Content: This Decree establishes the procedure for withdrawal (withdrawal) from circulation, return, export, disposal of dangerous products by the manufacturer (supplier, seller, importer) in order to prevent circulation of such products on the territory of the Republic of Belarus. It shall not apply to dangerous products, withdrawn, seized or converted to the benefit of the state in accordance with the procedure established by legislative acts. Competent bodies shall classify products as hazardous based on the results of laboratory research (tests) conducted by in accredited testing centers (laboratories); and on the basis of documents issued by the results of external inspection. Termination of import and/or circulation of hazardous products in the territory of the Republic of Belarus, their withdrawal (recall) from circulation shall be carried out by a business entity on the basis of the prescription issued by the competent authority. A business entity upon receipt of an order within a period of not more than 10 working days from the date of its receipt determines the possibility of bringing hazardous products into compliance with the requirements of technical regulations and informs the competent authority about the decision in written (electronic) form. The period of adjustment of hazardous products in accordance with the requirements of technical regulations must not exceed two months. A business entity is obliged to confirm the result of compliance of hazardous products with the requirements of technical regulations through implementation of the procedure of conformity assessment in accredited bodies and testing centers. In the event that hazardous products cannot be brought into compliance with the requirements of technical regulations within the specifies period, it shall be subject to disposal or return.

Policy: Regional Decree No. 25 validating the Regulation on nature monument of regional significance "Peat bog "Guchinsky".
Policy_Content: This Regional Decree establishes legal status of nature monument of regional significance "Peat bog "Guchinsky", defines its boundaries and particular protection regime. The main purpose of creating the nature monument is to preserve the natural complex of the lowland bog. The objectives of the nature monument are: (a) preservation of wild plant communities; (b) monitoring the state of natural complexes; (c) scientific research; and (d) environmental education. The following activities shall be prohibited on the territory of nature monument of regional significance "Peat bog "Guchinsky": (a) geological study of the subsoil and development of mineral deposits; (b) creation of timber processing infrastructure; (c) clear-cutting of forest stands; (d) cutting of healthy specimens of old-growth trees; (e) activities involving disturbance of soil cover, alteration of the hydrologic regime (excluding activities aimed at conservation, protection and regeneration of forests); (f) construction of infrastructure facilities; (g) construction of trunk roads, pipelines, and other communications, economic and residential objects, not connected with construction of trunk roads, pipelines, other communication lines, economic and residential facilities not associated with the functioning of the nature monument; (h) allotment of land plots for individual housing construction, construction of garden homes, gardening and horticulture facilities; (i) use of natural resources for industrial purposes, including procurement of soft resin, industrial procurement and collection of berries, fruits, seeds, medicinal and technical raw materials; (j) collection of biological collections, except for those carried out within the frameworks of scientific and research activities; (k) collection of fruits, berries, seeds, medicinal and technical raw materials for research activities; (l) activities resulting in disturbance of the growing and living conditions in habitats of flora and fauna species; (m) use and storage of pesticides, oil products, mineral fertilizers, plant protection chemicals, growth stimulators and other harmful substances; (n) passage and parking of motor vehicles outside of existing roads (excluding cases related to compliance with the parking of motor vehicles outside existing roads (excluding cases, connected with fulfillment of forest management arrangements (reforestation, fire prevention, forest protection) and biotechnical measures); (o) arrangement of resting places, bivouacs, tourist parking lots and campfires; (p) disposal of industrial and domestic waste; (q) destruction and damage of flagpoles, barriers, posts, boundary poles and other informational signs, equipped ecological trails and recreation areas; and (r) other activities that result in disturbance of the integrity of nature monument.

Policy: Arrêté du Gouvernement flamand modifiant l’arrêté du Gouvernement flamand du 19 décembre 2014 concernant les aides aux investissements et à la reprise dans l’agriculture.
Policy_Content: Cet arrêté modifie  l'arrêté du Gouvernement flamand du 19 décembre 2014 concernant les aides aux investissements et à la reprise dans l'agriculture. Dans les articles 1er e 3, des modifications formelles sont apporté, notamment pour réfléchir la différente dénomination du Code des Société en Code des sociétés et des associations. L'article 4 est modifié pour introduire la possibilité d'augmenter l'intensité de l'aide en présence d'au moins un des chefs d'entreprise âgé de moins de 41 ans. L'article 6 est modifié pour étendre la période de référence jusqu'au 2022 et pour introduire une prime à l'investissement en fonction de l'intensité des aides pour l'investissement subventionnable concerné et l'âge du directeur d'entreprise le plus jeune. Dans l’article 7, l'obtention d’une subvention d'intérêt est éliminée des objets pour lesquelles un investissement financé par un crédit  d’investissement peut être demandés seulement par intervention d’une institution de crédit. Les articles 8.1 et 8.2 sont insérés pour réfléchir, respectivement, le cas dans lequel un investissement n’est admissible au bénéfice de l'aide et les temps et les modalités, aussi substantielles, selon lesquelles l’agriculteur doit introduire une demande de paiement via le guichet électronique. L' articles 10 apporte des modifications formelles et l'article 14 est modifié par l'abrogation des points 1° et 2°.

Policy: Regional Decree No. 3-p validating the Instruction on regulation of emissions of pollutants to the atmospheric air under unfavorable meteorological conditions.
Policy_Content: This Regional Decree establishes the procedure for regulation of emissions of pollutants to the atmospheric air under unfavorable meteorological conditions with a view of reduction of negative environmental thereof and prevention of health risks for human beings. In the absence of observational data on atmospheric pollution risk degree of unfavorable meteorological conditions is determined on the basis of the analysis of the complex of unfavorable synoptic situations, meteorological conditions and characteristics of specific emission sources. It establishes reduction of emission levels in different risk periods. The period of validity of the list of measures to reduce emissions during unfavorable meteorological conditions shall not exceed 5 years if in the aforesaid period are not commissioned or reconstructed the existing sources of emissions of the pollutants. In the case of changes of emissions sources, it is necessary to submit for approval changes in the list of measures to reduce emissions during unfavorable meteorological conditions within two months from the date of putting in operation of the sources.

Policy: Executive Order on Protecting Public Health and the Environment and Restoring Science to Tackle the Climate Crisis (2021)
Policy_Content: This Executive Order provides that our Nation has an abiding commitment to empower our workers and communities; promote and protect our public health and the environment; and conserve our national treasures and monuments, places that secure our national memory. Where the Federal Government has failed to meet that commitment in the past, it must advance environmental justice. In carrying out this charge, the Federal Government must be guided by the best science and be protected by processes that ensure the integrity of Federal decision-making. It is, therefore, the policy of my Administration to listen to the science; to improve public health and protect our environment; to ensure access to clean air and water; to limit exposure to dangerous chemicals and pesticides; to hold polluters accountable, including those who disproportionately harm communities of color and low-income communities; to reduce greenhouse gas emissions; to bolster resilience to the impacts of climate change; to restore and expand our national treasures and monuments; and to prioritize both environmental justice and the creation of the well-paying union jobs necessary to deliver on these goals. To that end, this order directs all executive departments and agencies (agencies) to immediately review and, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, take action to address the promulgation of Federal regulations and other actions during the last 4 years that conflict with these important national objectives, and to immediately commence work to confront the climate crisis.

Policy: Decreto Nº 107 - Prohíbe la exportación de madera proveniente del bosque natural o extraída de embalses de agua, en troza.
Policy_Content: El presente Decreto prohíbe la exportación de madera proveniente del bosque natural o extraída de embalses de agua, en troza. Entiéndase por troza a cada una de las porciones en que se divide un tronco, mediante cortes transversales, para su salida del bosque. La madera proveniente del bosque natural o extraído de embalses de agua, solo podrá exportarse siempre y cuando cumpla con los siguientes requisitos: 1) Deberán de tener transformación y tratamiento primario, entiéndase por: i) Transformación primaria es el inicio del procesamiento al que se somete a las trozas de madera para su transformación óptima, mediante máquinas y técnicas que tienden a obtener el mayor volumen de madera aserrada con la más alta calidad posible (tablones, tablas, vigas, listones y además chapas y astillas, entre otros; ii) Tratamiento primario es el tratamiento preventivo contra agentes biológicos (insectos, hongos) que debe someterse a la madera, creando alrededor de la misma una barrera protectora con una cantidad mínima de producto de conservación a cierta profundidad según la intensidad de los riesgos biológicos. 2) Las especies de maderas para ser exportables deberán provenir de planes de manejo forestal sostenibles avalados por el Ministerio de Ambiente.

Policy_Content: This Act, divided into eleven Parts and consisting of 79 articles, provides for creating an institutional framework focused on: efficient waste management system within the county; prevention, control and abatement of air and noise pollution, in order to ensure the population a clean and healthy environment; reduction of health risks associated with a polluted environment. Policy: Regional Decree No. 9 validating the Regulation on creation of state nature reserve of regional significance “Derezovsky”.
Policy_Content: State nature reserve of regional significance "Derezovsky" is a protected natural area of regional significance, which includes natural complexes and objects of particular ecological and aesthetic value, and intended for use for nature protection, educational, scientific and cultural purposes. State nature reserve has a complex profile and is intended for: (a) preservation and restoration of natural complexes; (b) reduction of the level of anthropogenic impact on unique landscape complexes; and (c) maintaining the ecological balance in the region on the basis of rational use of natural resources.  State nature reserve of regional significance “Derezovsky” is stablished without limitation of its duration and without expropriation of land plots from owners, land tenants and landlords. The reserve was established to perform the following tasks: (a) preservation of natural complexes and objects in their natural state, restoration and reproduction of natural resources; (b) implementation of rational nature management; (c) scientific research; (d) environmental monitoring; and (e) environmental education, dissemination of environmental knowledge, ecological tourism. The following activities shall be prohibited on the territory of state nature reserve of regional significance "Derezovsky": (a) destroying anthills, clutches, holes, nests, other habitats of animals, collecting eggs of wild birds; (b) harvesting of edible forest resources and collection of medicinal plants, except for collection and harvesting thereof by citizens for their own needs; (c) collection and harvesting of non-timber forest resources; (d) creation of forest plantations and their exploitation; (e) geological exploration, prospecting and extraction of minerals, except for land plots containing groundwater used for potable and domestic water supply; (f) construction and reconstruction of objects of capital construction; (g) application of toxic chemicals, plant protection means and plant growth stimulants; (h) littering of the territory and waste disposal; (i) placement of cemeteries and burial grounds; (j) creation of facilities for disposal of domestic and non-domestic waste, radioactive, chemical, explosive, toxic and poisonous substances; (k) allotment of land plots for individual housing construction, gardening and horticulture; (l) recreational activities; (m) passage and parking of motor vehicles outside of existing roads; (n) destruction and damage of flagpoles, barriers, posts, boundary poles and other informational signs, equipped ecological trails and recreation areas; (o) ploughing up; (p) explosive works; (q) burning of vegetation; (r) organization of summer camps for farm animals; (s) discharge of sewage, including drainage water, on the relief; (t) clear-cutting, except for sanitary felling; and (u) other types of activities resulting in the reduction of ecological value of a particular area or that cause damage to natural complexes.

Policy: Regional Decree No. 1 validating the Regulation on nature monument of regional significance "Enchanted Forest”.
Policy_Content: Nature monument of regional significance "Enchanted Forest” is constituted without expropriation of land (forest) plots from owners, tenants and lessees of land (forest) plots. The natural monument is formed without a time limit. The purpose of creating natural monument shall be preservation of the unique, irreplaceable, ecologically, scientifically, culturally, and aesthetically valuable natural complex, conservation of the habitats of rare species of wild fauna and wild flora species and other organisms, which are necessary for the preservation of the natural habitats thereof and natural environment. The objectives of the nature monument are: (a) conservation of natural complexes (landscapes) and forests; (b) conservation of endangered bird species (c) maintenance of hydrological regime; (d) monitoring the state of natural complex; (e) scientific research; (e) environmental education; and (f) ecological tourism and recreation. The following activities shall be prohibited on the territory of nature monument of regional significance "Enchanted Forest": (a) clear cutting and timber extraction, except for sanitary felling and forest fire prevention arrangements; (b) burning of vegetation except for sanitary felling and forest fire prevention arrangements; (c) ploughing up, except for sanitary felling and forest fire prevention arrangements; (d) grazing; (e) any type of land reclamation work entailing change of hydrological regime of the territory; (f) construction; (g) passage and parking of motor vehicles outside of existing roads (excluding cases related to compliance with the parking of motor vehicles outside existing roads (excluding cases, connected with fulfillment of forest management arrangements (reforestation, fire prevention, forest protection) and biotechnical measures); (h) organization of provisional lodges for hunting and fishing; (i) destruction and damage of flagpoles, barriers, posts, boundary poles and other informational signs, equipped ecological trails and recreation areas; (j) littering and waste disposal; (k) holding cultural and mass events, sports competitions, sports festivals and training camps; (l) procurement of soft resin; and (m) exploration of mineral deposits and extraction of minerals.

Policy: Law No. 23.763 creating the State Policy for Community Tourism.
Policy_Content: This Law creates the State Policy for Community Tourism within the State of Minas Gerais, under Law No. 22.765 of 20 December 2017. Community tourism aims at unifying the values of good living, solidarity economy and fair trade, as a socio-economic activity planned and carried out by rural and traditional communities, in the countryside, in the city, in the forest and on the water, etc. The objectives of the policy are: encourage community-based tourism, through the promotion of supportive economic enterprises managed by family and community groups, participatory planning, sustainable management of natural resources and cultural appreciation, in order to allow them better living conditions; improve the use of environmental resources and maintain essential ecological processes, contributing to the appreciation and conservation of Minas Gerais’ socio-biodiversity; respect the sociocultural authenticity of host communities, conserve their material and intangible cultural assets, as well as their traditional values, as well as contribute to intercultural understanding and tolerance; ensure viable long-term economic activities that provide equitably distributed socioeconomic benefits, including stable employment and income generation opportunities, as well as social services for host communities that contribute to poverty reduction; promote support, advice and promotion to host communities, in order to enable a dialogical, satisfactory and meaningful experience for tourists, making them more aware of sustainability issues and promoting practices committed to sustainable tourism; make credit instruments available to support the policy; support the creation of partnerships with the Union and municipalities to develop policy actions covered by this law; support the creation of partnerships with international development organizations to attract resources from community-based tourism entrepreneurs; promote supervision and social control of the policy covered by this law, with the participation of state councils related to tourism, sustainable rural development and traditional peoples and communities; provide security and adequate sanitary conditions for tourists.

Policy: Environmental Code (Law No. 400-VI ZRK).
Policy_Content: This Code regulates public relations in the sphere of interaction between man and nature (environmental relations), arising in connection with the implementation of activities by natural and legal entities that have or can have impact on the environment. The relations regulated by this Code also include social relations in the field of environmental monitoring, meteorological and hydrological monitoring, which are aimed at provision of natural and legal persons with ecological and hydrometeorological information. The Environmental Code shall be valid throughout the territory of the Republic of Kazakhstan, including continental shelf and exclusive economic zone of the Republic of Kazakhstan in accordance with the norms of international law. The scope of the environmental legislation of the Republic of Kazakhstan is determination of legal grounds, tasks and principles, as well as mechanisms for implementation of the unified state environmental policy in the Republic of Kazakhstan. Objectives of the environmental legislation of the Republic of Kazakhstan shall be as follows: (a) ensuring a high level of environmental protection through the implementation of state regulation aimed at preventing environmental pollution, environmental damage, ensuring elimination of consequences of environmental damage, as well as gradual reduction of negative anthropogenic impact on the environment; (b) provision of environment favorable for human life and health; (c) ensuring sustainable development; (d) provision of contribution of the Republic of Kazakhstan to strengthening of global reaction to the risks of climate change in the context of sustainable development, as well as implementation of international, regional and transboundary programs on environmental protection and transition to "green" economy; (e) protection, preservation and rehabilitation of environment, including areas and objects of special ecological, scientific, historical, cultural, recreational, economic and social significance, including the rights of local communities to associate with nature; (f) creation of an effective public management system in the field of environmental protection which provides for cooperation and coordination among all government agencies; (g) encouraging and stimulating the government to "green" investments and wide use the best available resource-saving practices, reduction of waste volumes and waste hazardousness indicators, use of renewable energy, water conservation, and measures to improve energy efficiency, sustainable use and restoration of natural resources; (h) ensuring continuous and systematic collection, accumulation, storage, analysis and dissemination of environmental information to the public; (i) ensuring transparency and full public participation in addressing environmental protection and sustainable development issues in the Republic of Kazakhstan; (j) ensuring effective environmental monitoring and environmental; (k) creating conditions to attract investments into environmental protection measures, modernizing the existing and constructing new infrastructure to provide a high level of environmental protection; (l) compliance with international treaties and other obligations in the field of environmental protection; (m) forming environmental culture in the society, promoting environmental knowledge at all educational levels, development of environmental education; and (n) strengthening of law and order in the field of environmental protection and environmental security. The Code contains 24 Sections divided into 418 Articles. Section 1 lays down general provisions. Section 2 regards state management in the field of environmental protection. Section 3 regards state regulation of environmental relations. Section 4 regards economic regulation of environmental protection. Section 5 regards environmental damages. Section 6 regards sites of historic pollution. Section 7 regards elimination of the consequences of activities at facilities that have a negative impact on environment. Section 8 regards state monitoring of environment and natural resources. Section 9 regards activities in the field of meteorological monitoring, hydrological monitoring and monitoring of the state of environment. Section 10 regards state register of natural resources. Section 11 regards environmental supervision. Section 12 regards ecological culture and education. Section 13 regards ecological research. Section 14 regards atmospheric air protection. Section 15 regards waterbodies protection. Section 16 regards land protection. Section 17 regards nature protection. Section 18 regards climate and ozone layer. Section 19 regards waste management. Section 20 establishes ecological requirements for some types of activities. Section 21 regards areas of ecological emergencies and ecological disasters. Section 22 regards international cooperation in the field of environmental protection. Section 23 establishes liability for ecological offences and the procedure for dispute settlement. Section 24 lays down final provisions.
