Policy_Content: En application de l’arrêté interministériel n°2020-210 /MS /MINEFID /MESRSI /MAAH /MRAH/ MEEVCC du 30 juin 2020 portant attributions, organisation, composition et fonctionnement du Comité Technique de Pilotage, des Commissions Thématiques, du Secrétariat Technique et des Points Focaux One Health, le présent arrêté précise les attributions, la composition et le fonctionnement de la Commission Thématique One Health n°07 : « Système national de laboratoire », « Biosécurité Biosûreté ». La Commission Thématique One Health n°07 est l’organe consultatif en charge des domaines techniques suivants du Règlement sanitaire international : la coordination du système de laboratoires en lien avec la santé humaine, la santé animale, l’agriculture et l’environnement ; le renforcement des capacités des laboratoires pour la détection des agents pathogène des maladies prioritaires ; la collecte, transport des échantillons ; la gestion de la biosécurité et de la biosûreté ; la contribution dans la mise en œuvre des plans de surveillance épidémiologique et des actions de santé publique ; et le renforcement du système qualité des laboratoires. La Commission est consultée pour les questions qui relèvent de son champ de compétence. A ce titre, la Commission est chargée : de suivre les activités techniques mises en œuvre par les différents secteurs ministériels et relatives aux domaines techniques du Règlement sanitaire international ; de proposer des stratégies permettant de renforcer la synergie d’actions et de mutualiser les technologies et les ressources dans ces domaines; de mener des investigations conjointes ; d’apporter des avis pertinents et l’appui nécessaire aux autorités compétentes; de participer à l’analyse et la validation des résultats des études et recherches dans ces domaines ; de proposer des actions à entreprendre pour prévenir, détecter et répondre à toute menace pouvant provenir des secteurs d’activités et concernant ces domaines techniques ; de participer aux évaluations du Règlement sanitaire international et de la Performances des services vétérinaires et contribuer à la mise en œuvre des recommandations pour les domaines techniques de compétence ; d’émettre des avis sur l’organisation et le fonctionnement du réseau des laboratoires de référence ; de réaliser toute autre tâche confiée par les autorités compétentes ; d’apporter son avis sur les documents stratégiques en lien avec les laboratoires ; et d’interagir avec les autres commissions thématiques de la Plateforme One Health.

Policy: National Standard No. 1361 (2021) “Organic production. Requirements for production, storage, processing and transportation.”
Policy_Content: This National Standard regulates the stages of collection, harvesting, preparation, production, storage, transportation, packaging, labelling, import and sale of organic products, and also indicates the acceptable permitted input for fertilization and soil conditioning, pest and plant disease control, as well as food additives and processing aids. For labeling purposes, terms implying that organic production methods have been used apply only to products obtained from producers under the supervision of a notified body or certification body. The objectives of this standard are: (a) protection of consumers from deception and fraud in the market and unfounded claims to products; (b) protection of producers of organic products from false representation of other agricultural products as organic; (c) ensuring the possibility of testing at all stages of production, preparation, storage, transportation and marketing, as well as ensuring product compliance with the requirements of this standard; (d) harmonization of regulations on the production, certification, identification and labelling of organically grown products; (e) ensuring harmonization with international guidelines, rules and standards of organic food control systems, for the recognition of equivalent national systems; and (f) support and improvement of organic agricultural systems to protect the environment at the national and international level. This standard shall be applicable to the following products produced by organic production: (a) unprocessed plants and plant products, livestock and livestock products; (b) processed crops and livestock products intended for human consumption; (c) feedstuffs; (d) planting materials and seeds; (e) yeast used as food or feed; (f) aquaculture species; and (f) collection, harvesting and processing of wild flora species of plants, nuts, fruits, berries, mushrooms and medicinal plants. It shall not be applicable to wild fauna products (game) and GMO. The transition period from conventional to organic farming should start: (a) two years before sowing or planting (for annual plants); (b) two years before grazing or harvesting on pastures or meadows for use as organic fodder; and (c) three years before the harvest of organic products, (for perennials, except for fodder plants). In organic animal husbandry, it is not allowed to organize animal husbandry without sufficient land for grazing the animal. Herbivores must have access to pastures, and all other animals must be able to stay in open spaces. The certification body may make exceptions when the animal's physiological condition, adverse weather and soil conditions permit such exceptions, or the structure of certain "traditional" farming systems restrict access to pastures, provided that the health of the animals is guaranteed. Animals used to produce products that meet the requirements of this standard must originate from birth or breeding, from production units that meet this standard, or be the offspring of parents bred in accordance with the conditions specified in this standard. They must be raised in this system throughout their lives. Animals must not move between organic and non-organic farm units. Livestock animals that do not meet the requirements of this standard may be replaced.

Policy: National Standard of the Russian Federation GOSTR Organic products made from wild raw material. Requirements for collection, harvesting, purchases, deliveries, labelling and processing.
Policy_Content: National Standard of the Russian Federation GOSTR Organic products made from wild raw material establishes requirements for collection, harvesting, purchases, deliveries, labelling and processing of organic wild raw materials. It applies to organic products obtained from wild-growing raw materials, in natural, processed or re-processed form, and establishes requirements for the collection, processing, storage, transportation and labelling thereof. It shall not be applicable to forest seeds and planting materials, products of hunting and fishing in natural or processed form, and small fry, larvae, other seeding material used for artificial reproduction and acclimatization of aquatic biological resources. Organic wild-growing raw materials shall be intended non-cultivated wild-growing plants related to forest food resources and medicinal plants (wild-growing plants) obtained as a result of harvesting and collection in territories and plots of collection, complying with the requirements of this standard and intended for organic products. The collection and harvesting of organic wild-growing plants and raw materials is carried out in natural ecosystems in accordance with the environmental legislation of the Russian Federation and the requirements of this standard. Collection and harvesting of organic wild-growing plants and raw materials shall be prohibited: (a) in forests located on defense and security land, protected areas, other lands access to which is prohibited or limited by regulatory legal acts; (b) in areas contaminated with radioactive substances in accordance with the procedure, established by the legislation of the Russian Federation; and (c) on forest sites located near settlements located within the boundaries of exclusion zones. Collection and harvesting of wild-growing plants and raw materials located in the territories of traditional nature management of indigenous peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East of the Russian Federation to ensure the maintenance their traditional way of life, including the collection of wild plants, must comply with requirements, as well as the customs of small indigenous peoples.

Policy: Law of Georgia on State Support for Children and Youth Unions (No. 2139-IIs of 1999)
Policy_Content: This Law determines the notion, forms, and general principles of the state support for children and youth unions. It consists of five chapters: General provisions (I); Main forms of the state support to children and youth unions (II); Organizational bases for the state support to children and youth unions (III); and Transitional provisions (IV); and Final provision (V). Supporting children and youth unions includes a system of measures undertaken according to the law within the framework of the state youth policy towards self-realization and protection of the rights in civil life of children and youth, supporting the economic and organizational conditions of these unions, and to provide legal safeguards for the stability of their work. The children unions are established as non-commercial legal entities with their founding bylaws aiming to protect the freedoms and rights of children and youth, and to develop their talent and skills and support their self-realization in the society.
